beats.text: Bratus starts with his Spirit and builds quest counters. The casters explain that Arisana is known for defense and burst once it reaches level three. He needs to answer every threat Fruitcake plays.

Fruitcake's damage stacks up and he goes to level two. Polaris cannot kill the Seiryuu without a level-up buffer, and Fruitcake's Cometfall deals 12 total damage to the 13-health dragon. The casters say that is rough: he did not read the buff counter, and usually the answer is that you cannot come back.

Fruitcake cannot survive the Arcane Blast next turn. The casters note that Regal Inquisition cannot get rid of Fruitcake's threats, though it removes spell shields, and a spare spellshield probably comes in for Fruitcake. Bratus wins, and the match goes to Bratus 2-0.

before.summary: Zero0000000000 wins — Spirit Blade: Retribution with banished allies deals 15 to a Lifdrasyl who cannot find his Veiling Breeze

beats.text: Lifdrasyl goes first as the higher seed and opens with Fairy Whispers and a Surveil the Winds, which the casters call a great start. Zero0000000000 shows Backup Charger and holds a hedge deck, because TheRainGoddess was expected on Razor Gale and TeamTrueCaban on fractals.

Zero0000000000 plays Aesan Protector with a reclaim and Windmill Engineer, and loses allies to Lifdrasyl's Serro operative but keeps banishing the high-power allies. The casters say Ghosts of Pendragon is the pressure and that Prismatic Edge threatens three damage a turn.

Spirit Blade: Retribution comes for 15 damage with a sword added, compared with seven against TheRainGoddess, because the high-power allies are in banishment. Lifdrasyl has only nine life at Zander level two and needs a Veiling Breeze off a surveil, but he finds a Luxem Sight, and Zero0000000000 takes game one.

before.summary: Zero0000000000 wins — Regal Inquisition reveals the hand and a zero-cost Retribution for 16 beats one Veiling Breeze

beats.text: Zero0000000000 casts Regal Inquisition and sees Lifdrasyl's hand, and the casters say Lifdrasyl has Dungeon Guide-like lose conditions while the rest are minor annoyances. Lifdrasyl cannot play all his cards in the same turn, and Zero0000000000 uses Displace and Scout the Land to dig for Heavenly Guide.

Lifdrasyl never gets a big influence start. He has Windmill Engineer, Sadi and Incapacitate, and a Veiling Breeze helps him survive one turn by preventing seven, but he sits on three cards while Zero0000000000 recovers influence with Windmill and Sadi bounces.

Zero0000000000 takes Spirit Blade: Retribution from the graveyard at zero cost for 16 damage, and a free one-use Ghosts of Pendragon swings are added on top. Lifdrasyl loses, which ends the last Southeast Asia and North America hope in the final, and Zero0000000000 meets Jett. The casters call Zero0000000000 the player with a 0 percent win rate against everyone in Hong Kong.

before.summary: Jett wins — a free Zander level-up with Blinding Steel and a Lightweaver's Assault line beat GlenyBoi's greedy Pendragon turn

beats.text: GlenyBoi opens with Dungeon Guide and Aesan Protector, the high-pressure start a Wind Krux deck needs. Jett keeps Ensnaring Fumes and Veiling Breeze, and the casters note he has Heavenly Guide to re-use.

Jett resolves a level-up to Zander with Blinding Steel without losing a single card, which the casters call a blinding lead. GlenyBoi looks for Verdigris Decree to unlock the Pendragons and Sadi draws a Turbo Charge.

GlenyBoi uses Imperious Galebind to take the Lost Providence, the Poisoned Dagger and the Drawn Blade, and has three Ghosts of Pendragon to play for nine damage. He then plays Prismatic Edge instead of Clarent, Reimagined, which the casters call a little too greedy.
Jett suppresses the Ghosts and calms the damage with Calming Breeze. His Poisoned Dagger for one and a revealed Lightweaver's Assault deal eight damage to the face, and Jett wins game one.

before.summary: Jett wins — a Veiling Breeze for one keeps him alive for exactly one more turn, then Lightweaver's Assaults finish

beats.text: Jett brings in three cards and plays Sadi back from the banishment with only three cards in hand. GlenyBoi has no Stifling Trap to snipe Sadi on its return. Jett swings face rather than into the Aesan Protector and Scout the Land for a better position.

GlenyBoi uses Fluffy Shopkeep again and sends Clarent to the banishment. Jett uses Heavenly Guide to go up to level three and the casters say it is juicy, because GlenyBoi has no Stifling Trap. The Ensnaring Fumes, with a floating memory, are a big blowout.

The casters count 12.5 percent to find a Luxom card and Jett finds a Luxem Sight. GlenyBoi has two Veiling Breezes and a Retribution in hand. Jett has ten cards in hand and could play a raw Slice and Dice into Lightweaver's Assaults, and a Veiling Breeze for one barely keeps him alive for one more turn.
Jett finishes with Lightweaver's Assaults and the damage stays just above GlenyBoi's reach. Jett wins 2-0 and moves to the semifinals against TheRainGoddess, a Wind Luxom against Wind Krux match.

before.summary: ChemCollapse wins — Tricastles of Lucenia locks Razorgale, then Seiryuu's Command

beats.text: ChemCollapse uses Beseech the Winds to reach Guo Jia level one on turn one and builds quest counters with Scout the Land and Tangu. Jett responds with Fluffy Shopkeep, Backup Charger, and Windmill Engineer's Reclaim and trades.

After Dungeon Guide takes Guo Jia to level three, ChemCollapse plays Tricastles of Lucenia, preventing non-advanced element card activations. Once per turn, any player may banish a norm or advanced element card from hand to make Tricastles lose all abilities until end of turn.

ChemCollapse follows with Uther (removing a Razorgale), Aella and a Royal Oathguard. Jett plays three Dream Fairies, a Zephyr and Purifying Thurible but drops below six cards, which turns off Ensnaring Fumes. Aella suppresses Jett's Essence Crucible.
ChemCollapse flips Seiryuu, plays Seiryuu's Command (triple on-enter) to generate an Arcane Blast and empower it by eight. The Blast costs nothing and finishes Jett.

before.summary: Jett wins — Aesan Protector chip damage, then Zephyr and Veiling Breeze on the last Razorgale trigger

beats.text: Jett brings in Turbo Charge, plays Windmill Engineer and Aesan Protector early, and wants a board that can kill Tricastles of Lucenia in two turns. Fairy Whispers finds Razorgale Calling.
ChemCollapse levels with Beseech and Dungeon Guide and draws with Incandescent Reliquary, but a Tricastle banished by Throne-keeper mill and a Purifying Thurible deny him the lock.

Jett plays two Razorgales and Essence Crucible with Distilled Water potions. Imperial Countermeasure absorbs the first trigger. Jett Zephyrs his own Aesan Protector and then uses Veiling Breeze as the final Razorgale trigger for lethal. The Aesan Protector is the MVP of the game.

before.summary: Jett wins the deciding game (not shown in full)

beats.text: ChemCollapse goes first for the first time in the match, uses Beseech the Winds on turn one and Portentous Tanggu, and holds Blanch and Dungeon Guide. Jett opens with Windmill Engineer, Aesan Protector and Fluffy Shopkeep, to keep at least four damage of allies on board against another Tricastle.

Jett finds Razorgale Calling, Aesan Protector and Ensnaring Fumes with Fairy Whispers and keeps six cards in hand so the dragon stays locked. The broadcast cuts to the semifinal and confirms Jett closed out the game 2-1 within the next couple of turns.

after.summary: ChemCollapse wins — Tricastles of Lucenia locks Razorgale, then Seiryuu's Command

beats.text: ChemCollapse uses Beseech the Winds to reach Guo Jia level one on turn one and builds quest counters with Scout the Land and Tangu. Jett responds with Fluffy Shopkeep, Backup Charger, and Windmill Engineer's Reclaim and trades.

After Dungeon Guide takes Guo Jia to level three, ChemCollapse plays Tricastles of Lucenia, preventing non-advanced element card activations. Once per turn, any player may banish a norm or advanced element card from hand to make Tricastles lose all abilities until end of turn.

ChemCollapse follows with Uther (removing a Razorgale), Aella and a Royal Oathguard. Jett plays three Dream Fairies, a Zephyr and Purifying Thurible but drops below six cards, which turns off Ensnaring Fumes. Aella suppresses Jett's Essence Crucible.
ChemCollapse flips Seiryuu, plays Seiryuu's Command (triple on-enter) to generate an Arcane Blast and empower it by eight. The Blast costs nothing and finishes Jett.

after.summary: Jett wins — Aesan Protector chip damage, then Zephyr and Veiling Breeze on the last Razorgale trigger

beats.text: Jett brings in Turbo Charge, plays Windmill Engineer and Aesan Protector early, and wants a board that can kill Tricastles of Lucenia in two turns. Fairy Whispers finds Razorgale Calling.

ChemCollapse levels with Beseech and Dungeon Guide and draws with Incandescent Reliquary, but a Tricastle banished by Throne-keeper mill and a Purifying Thurible deny him the lock. ChemCollapse plays Regal Inquisition on Jett, discarding Ensnaring Fumes, but Jett draws another copy. The replacement keeps Seiryuu locked down.

Jett plays two Razorgales and Essence Crucible with Distilled Water potions. Imperial Countermeasure absorbs the first trigger. Jett Zephyrs his own Aesan Protector and then uses Veiling Breeze as the final Razorgale trigger for lethal. The Aesan Protector is the MVP of the game.

before.summary: PewPewStan wins — MaruX concedes at 27 damage

beats.text: MaruX opens with a hand that is hard to use: the casters say it is a choice between holding a whole hand of good cards or leveling. He draws many cards with Creative Shock to look for Dungeon Guide, and has Clarent, Reimagined on the board to protect his allies.

PewPewStan plays cautiously and uses Imperious Galebind, a Dream Fairy that goes the distance every time, and a Corhazi insignia for preparation counters so Striking Illuminance can deal real damage. Ayella suppresses MaruX's Prismatic Edge. The casters say the deck with the draw-focused start has a big advantage in this matchup.

PewPewStan finds Striking Illuminance and double Lightweaver's Assault, plus a Regal Inquisition, while MaruX has Lorraine, Spirit Ruler and a Prismatic Edge out. A rules question about the Drawn Blade that Sabella put into play is explained to the players.

before.summary: Outcome unconfirmed

beats.text: MaruX takes the first turn and baits out the Purifying Thurible. He plays Sword of Seeking, which had been replaced by the distortion versions for a while, and a Gentle Respite comes down for PewPewStan to get influence. There are no more preparation counters for MaruX.

MaruX plays Aesan Protector for three and follows up with Spirit Blade: Ascension. He uses a Clarent instead of the Sword of Seeking to kill the Dungeon Guide. PewPewStan keeps Resolute Stand, Vanish from Sight and two Luxem Sights in hand.

Ghosts of Pendragon and a second Ghosts of Pendragon in MaruX's hand build a big board, but it is MaruX's last turn in the overtime procedure. PewPewStan needs 27 damage on his final turn while at Zander and cannot get there. Time is called; the recorded match result is a draw. The casters say that one more turn for MaruX would have made a huge difference.

before.text: The casters expect ProAnnn to look for ways to clear the Krux board and name Bandersnatch as one idea. They also note a Lustrous Slime, which is not a Carter but a big body, as a possible tech against the windmill-style damage.

after.text: The casters discuss Bandersnatch as a taunt-and-recovery option, along with Slip Away and Nullifying Mirror. These are boarding suggestions; the broadcast does not establish which copies ProAnnn brings in.

before.summary: DuckHats wins — Aella suppresses the Ducal Seal at end of turn and ProAnnn has no recovery left

beats.text: DuckHats opens Lorraine, Blademaster with the Dungeon Guide and swings the Sword of Seeking into the Angel Attendant. ProAnnn answers with a Cerulean Decree, and the casters note how many recovery cards the Alice deck packs: Abnegation, Pearled Prayer and more.

A second Dungeon Guide takes DuckHats to level three, and he puts in Enfeebling Orb as his next material. With Ducal Seal and Spirit Blade: Retribution, the Alice player must recover again and again just to stay level. ProAnnn's Maledictum Vitae and a second Regal Inquisition are in the mix, and a full Regal mill takes nine cards each.
DuckHats suppresses with Aella on the Ducal Seal at the end of the turn. ProAnnn sees he has no recovery left and concedes game one.

before.summary: ProAnnn wins — two Dynastic Whirlpools mill DuckHats out after he whiffs on the Dungeon Guide

beats.text: DuckHats has an amazing hand with an ultimate spell and a Ghosts of Pendragon, but he cannot find the Dungeon Guide to get to level three. ProAnnn goes up to Alice level two with Phantasmagoria and ships the rest of the graveyard to the bottom of the deck to mill two instead.

ProAnnn finds an Engulf and a Dynastic Whirlpool; the casters count the deck at about 27 cards, so two whirlpools are enough. A Bauble of Abundance gives ProAnnn extra draws, and without the Enfeebling Orb in play DuckHats cannot deny any activations.

The casters call the mill of 15 a done deal. They note that ProAnnn forgot his Lost Providence in game one but now remembers it. Two Dynastic Whirlpools finish DuckHats's deck, and ProAnnn ties the match.

before.summary: DuckHats wins — main-deck Cleansing Reunion and Reflected Blight stop the Whirlpool plan, and ProAnnn scoops with no recovery

beats.text: DuckHats holds the third Dungeon Guide and does not activate it in the recollection phase, the way many players would. He pays Escape the Wreckage with the Dungeon Guide in memory as a bait, and the casters say ProAnnn has to decide whether to take it.

DuckHats tries again to take down the Angel Attendant for a draw. He has a Reflected Blight in the graveyard, and the casters say it stops a spell from resolving and does not go under Alice as a curse. The Cleansing Reunion and Reflected Blight, in the main deck, are the choices DuckHats made for this event.

ProAnnn tries a Dynastic Whirlpool plus a second one back in the deck, but DuckHats's Cleansing Reunion answers it. ProAnnn has only a Resolute Stand and no recovery, so he scoops the game. DuckHats wins the match 2-1 and goes 1-0, and the casters note his main-deck reads of the room.

after.summary: DuckHats wins — Cleansing Reunion disrupts the mill plan and Aella suppresses Ducal Seal

beats.text: DuckHats opens Lorraine, Blademaster with the Dungeon Guide and swings the Sword of Seeking into the Angel Attendant. ProAnnn answers with a Cerulean Decree, and the casters note how many recovery cards the Alice deck packs: Abnegation, Pearled Prayer and more.

DuckHats uses a second Dungeon Guide to reach Lorraine, Spirit Ruler, then materializes Enfeebling Orb. ProAnnn uses Maledictum Vitae for recovery and Regal Inquisition to discard Ghosts of Pendragon; DuckHats retrieves a Ghost with Crux Sight. ProAnnn materializes Ducal Seal to tax the incoming attacks.

DuckHats’s Cleansing Reunion denies ProAnnn’s Reflected Blight retrieval of Dynastic Whirlpool. Imperious Galebind lets Aella return at end of turn to suppress ProAnnn’s Ducal Seal. Facing the next attack turn, ProAnnn concedes.

after.summary: ProAnnn wins — two Dynastic Whirlpools mill DuckHats out after he whiffs on the Dungeon Guide

beats.text: ProAnnn’s Regal Inquisition strips DuckHats’s hand, but the replacement draws still miss Dungeon Guide. ProAnnn later uses Phantasmagoria to recycle his graveyard and mills an Engulf.

ProAnnn finds an Engulf and a Dynastic Whirlpool; the casters count the deck at about 27 cards, so two whirlpools are enough. A Bauble of Abundance gives ProAnnn extra draws, and without the Enfeebling Orb in play DuckHats cannot deny any activations.

DuckHats eventually finds Dungeon Guide, then levels to Lorraine, Spirit Ruler through materialization. ProAnnn materializes Bauble of Abundance and finishes with two Dynastic Whirlpools, tying the match.

after.summary: DuckHats wins — Cleansing Reunion disrupts Reflected Blight and ProAnnn concedes

beats.text: DuckHats holds Purifying Thurible to threaten ProAnnn’s Fracturize setup, then uses it before leveling with Dungeon Guide. Lorraine, Blademaster clears Angel Attendant and draws a card.

ProAnnn plays Extricating Touch. DuckHats responds with Escape the Wreckage, putting Dungeon Guide into memory. ProAnnn removes Spirit Blade: Ascension instead; DuckHats then materializes Lorraine, Spirit Ruler.

After ProAnnn reaches Alice level two, DuckHats uses Cleansing Reunion to remove the target of Reflected Blight. The failed retrieval also leaves Alice without that curse in her lineage. With Resolute Stand but no recovery available, ProAnnn concedes.

before.text: The casters go through TeamTrueCaban's side. Crimson Protective Trinket does not stop fire. Nullifying Mirror and Overlapping Visages are not useful in this matchup. Song of Frost could be the one card to bring in against Devastating Blow variants, but he feels strong about his Oblation matchup.

In the post-match interview Raylam explains the single Incapacitate in his deck and says it can be used to stop an opponent from drawing off a Creative Shock, or to cut the cost of a negate down to five fractals. He also says Nasome Blast in the main deck over the side is a flexible choice.

after.text: The casters go through TeamTrueCaban's side. Crimson Protective Trinket does not stop fire. Nullifying Mirror and Overlapping Visages are not useful in this matchup. Song of Frost could be the one card to bring in against Devastating Blow variants, but he feels strong about his Oblation matchup.
Raylam plays Rictus Tiding in game two; his registered Swiss list places it in the sideboard. The captions do not establish how many copies he brings in or which cards he removes.

before.summary: Raylam wins — an Enfeebling Orb at the wrong moment leaves TeamTrueCaban without the Burst Asunder he needed

beats.text: TeamTrueCaban uses a Fracturize to eat Raylam's floating memory, draws, and commits an ally to kill the Hasty Messenger. The casters note that Three of Hearts is a card many players cut as the format moved away from allies, and Raylam keeps it.

Raylam goes to CL level two, opens his omens and gets a Liminal Guide trigger to draw. TeamTrueCaban sees that without the Frostsworn Paladin he cannot control the board, so he builds fractals, with six now in play, double Shimmering Refraction and a Burst of Thunder ready.

TeamTrueCaban plays the Enfeebling Orb to put two cards of Raylam's hand down and tries to survive. The casters say he drew his first Burst Asunder in the materialize phase; if he had known it was there, he would have played a different line. Raylam takes game one.

before.summary: TeamTrueCaban wins — Raylam goes to zero influence to make Topsy Decree unnegatable, but the Burst Asunder still finishes

beats.text: TeamTrueCaban opens with an imbued Fractal of Rain and a hand with Refracting Missile, Zhang Jiao and a Glimmering Refusal, everything a Fractals player wants except more fractals. He takes far less pressure than in game one.

TeamTrueCaban holds a second and third Refracting Missile, Burst of Thunder and a Fractal of Insight. He finds the exact lethal line each turn, and the casters note he has Acquiescing Rejection in hand to negate or draw. Raylam's Chalice of Blood brings him to 20.

Raylam goes to zero influence so that his Topsy Decree cannot be negated and gains spell shroud, a line the casters say they did not think they would see. It is not enough: TeamTrueCaban does not have to give up anything for the Burst Asunder, and takes game two.

before.summary: Raylam wins — wide ally pressure, a Lost Providence draw and two Oblations through Acquiescing Rejection

beats.text: Raylam plays a wide aggressive ally strategy, which the casters say is not what Oblation CL usually does but works to pressure Fractals. Fluffy Shopkeep banishes a key card, and Raylam discards a Floating Memory he does not need.

TeamTrueCaban spends a Refracting Missile on an ally to take control of the board back, but Raylam has Incapacitate, a unique card in the deck, to answer. The casters note the Enfeebling Orb can put the rest of Raylam's hand down, so the Glimmering Refusal is not needed to push through.

Raylam uses Lost Providence in the pre-wreck step, pulls the Manxome Armoire out of the material deck and recollects a full five-card hand. TeamTrueCaban pays Acquiescing Rejection, but two cards are not enough to save him. Baleful Oblation resolves, the units go to the graveyard, and the Measure of Arar delivers the final blow. Raylam takes down the Omnidex number one.

after.summary: Raylam wins — ally pressure and Feu Awakening overwhelm Caban’s defense

beats.text: TeamTrueCaban Fracturizes his Powercell, then uses its floating-memory card for Frostsworn Paladin. Raylam sacrifices the threatened Hasty Messenger to Undeniable Truth. Three of Hearts and another Messenger later clear the Paladin.

Raylam reaches Ciel, Omenbringer and draws from Liminal Guide, then uses Dungeon Guide to reach Mirage’s Grave. Caban builds fractals but remains at level zero after materializing Enfeebling Orb; the casters calculate that his available damage and influence fall short.

Raylam attacks with his allies. Caban uses Enfeebling Orb and targets Hasty Messenger with Shimmering Refraction, but Raylam shows Feu Awakening and Caban concedes. The casters discuss leveling to Diao Chan as a possible alternative in hindsight, not an established misplay.

after.summary: TeamTrueCaban wins — Raylam survives Burst Asunder, but later falls to Refracting Missile

beats.text: TeamTrueCaban opens with an imbued Fractal of Rain and a hand with Refracting Missile, Zhang Jiao and a Glimmering Refusal, everything a Fractals player wants except more fractals. He takes far less pressure than in game one.

Caban develops his fractals and deals damage with Refracting Missile. Raylam reaches Ciel, Omenbringer but cannot find Dungeon Guide. Caban holds Glimmering Refusal for Raylam’s defensive Topsy Decree.

Caban answers Topsy Decree with two Glimmering Refusals. Raylam uses Feu Awakening at level two, discarding his hand and memory so Topsy resolves and grants spellshroud against Burst Asunder. Caban retains his fractals. On a later turn, Shimmering Refraction adds damage; Enfeebling Orb empties Raylam’s hand before Refracting Missile finishes the game.

after.summary: Raylam wins — a third Baleful Oblation breaks through after two are negated

beats.text: Raylam plays a wide aggressive ally strategy, which the casters say is not what Oblation CL usually does but works to pressure Fractals. Fluffy Shopkeep banishes a key card, and Raylam discards a Floating Memory he does not need.

Caban spends Refracting Missile to remove Hasty Messenger. Fractal of Intrusion later discards Raylam’s Incapacitate from memory. Caban then uses Glimmering Refusal on Fluffy Shopkeep to deny Raylam its draw.

Caban negates Raylam’s first two Baleful Oblations. On the following turn, Raylam materializes Manxome Armoire and uses Lost Providence before recollection. A third Oblation resolves after Acquiescing Rejection; the ensuing omen damage and Armoire activation finish the game.

before.text: The casters list TheRainGoddess's side options: Mystic Purifier, Obscured Offering to protect the Sensor, Essence Crucible or Nullifying Lantern, and Siphoning Gale and Verdigris Decree, which are good for hitting Paladins and breaking Fantasia.

Superior has Beastbond Boots as a very good sideboard call. The casters explain that Razorgale is not a "may", so with spell shroud the Razorgale player is forced to target themself. They also note Expel the Departed as a strong answer to a Razorgale on the field, but Superior does not have another fate stone in the deck.

after.text: The casters discuss Mystic Purifier, Obscured Offering, and Verdigris Decree as options for TheRainGoddess. These are suggestions, not confirmed boarding quantities.

Beastbond Boots and Expel the Departed are identified in Superior’s game-two deck; Expel is milled, not played. Blanche, Sheltering Saint is later seen in hand. The broadcast does not establish boarding quantities or cuts.

before.summary: Superior wins — Sensor and Lantern slow the Arisana start, then Genbu, Black Tortoise and Resonating Fugue push 18

beats.text: Superior has the classic anti-Razorgale tech: a Censer of Restful Peace and a Nullifying Lantern, with only two Unbroken Mustangs in the deck. The casters call it the anti-Razorgale attack, and note TheRainGoddess has to deal with the Sensor first.

TheRainGoddess starts with Floral Arrangement and Scout the Land, which finds Turbo Charge, and draws extra to fill her memory. She holds Ensnaring Fumes, which the casters call the absolute Genbu killer, but cannot play it with only five cards in hand.

Superior brings out the Tidestone Bovine and the Frostsworn Paladin for steady damage, destroys a Fractal of Rain with a Verdigris Decree and uses Seaside Ringleader to fill the graveyard. Genbu, Black Tortoise arrives for the first time in the Swiss stage, with Resonating Fugue for an 18-damage push. TheRainGoddess has Veiling Breeze in the stock and goes into the tank, but cannot stop the onslaught.

before.summary: Superior wins by game loss — TheRainGoddess takes a card from a Nullifying Lantern lock, a ruling that is upheld on appeal while Superior is in a commanding position

beats.text: Superior puts in Beastbond Boots and Expel the Departed and bounces back with a Throne-Keeper Bullfrog to protect the Bovine. TheRainGoddess holds up three cards with a Fracturize in hand, but Superior keeps building a board with Seaside Ringleaders and the Bullfrog, which gets a +2 buff and swings for nine.

TheRainGoddess uses Purifying Thurible and a Turbo Charge to draw, and Superior holds six cards of influence. The casters note Superior does not have to bring out the turtle at all when he is pressuring this hard, and TheRainGoddess is one turn from the Essence Crucible but at 22 life.

TheRainGoddess uses a Cyclical Breeze to add a Fairy Whispers to her hand while the Nullifying Lantern stops her taking a card from a graveyard without an element. The table judge rules that too much has happened to fix it and issues a game loss. The appeal to a higher judge fails, and Superior wins the match 2-0.

after.summary: Superior wins — Enfeebling Orb clears the way for Genbu and Resonating Fugue, backed by Frostbind

beats.text: TheRainGoddess uses Censer of Restful Peace to shut off Superior’s graveyard abilities, with Nullifying Lantern also available in the material deck. The casters note Superior has only two Unbroken Mustangs and may need Fracturize to answer the Censer.

TheRainGoddess starts with Floral Arrangement and Scout the Land, which finds Turbo Charge, and draws extra to fill her memory. She holds Ensnaring Fumes, which the casters call the absolute Genbu killer, but cannot play it with only five cards in hand.

TheRainGoddess’s Verdigris Decree destroys Superior’s Fractal of Rain. Superior uses Primordial Ritual and continues building his graveyard, then uses Enfeebling Orb to leave TheRainGoddess unable to pay for Ensnaring Fumes. Genbu and Resonating Fugue threaten 18 damage; Superior’s Frostbind stops Veiling Breeze to close the game.

after.summary: Superior wins by game loss — the broadcast reports an illegal Cyclical Breeze retrieval under Nullifying Lantern, upheld on appeal

beats.text: Superior shows Beastbond Boots and mills Expel the Departed. He holds Fracturize and removes TheRainGoddess’s Censer of Restful Peace. Later, Throne-Keeper Bullfrog enters with two buff counters alongside Tidestone Bovine and the growing ally board.

before.summary: Guruthos wins — a multi-Baleful Oblation turn with Manxome Armoire, and Jett's Orb of Sealing comes too late

beats.text: The casters say the Clarent nerf makes CL stronger against Wind Krux, and Guruthos has an easy time setting up. Both players generate influence and reach level three; Jett has no Stifling Trap-style card to play around, and the casters expect a game of Oblation timing.

Jett puts out the Enfeebling Orb and pushes ally damage with the Ghosts of Pendragon, but Guruthos is at healthy life. The casters say Jett cannot use Orb of Sealing right before the Oblation: he turns it at the wrong time, thinking he can seal, and is punished on the stack.

Guruthos pays three cards for Baleful Oblation and Manxome Armoire puts a fifteen-cost in. Jett's Crystallized Destiny is the card he needed, but the Armoire line gets around it. Three Baleful Oblations resolve, Jett cannot reveal how many win cards he has, and Guruthos takes game one.

before.summary: Jett wins — Eternal Magistrate stalls the Oblation turn and Spirit Blade: Ascension with Prismatic Edge pushes through

beats.text: Jett starts game two and puts out the Eternal Magistrate. He uses Cleansing Reunion to deny floating memory, and Lorraine reaches level three. Jett gets Orb of Sealing out and plays defensively, letting the weapon pressure wait.

Jett gets a Ghost of Pendragon, a Reclaim and a Spirit Blade: Ascension and pushes ally damage into Guruthos, who is in Chalice of Blood range. He strips two cards with a Dungeon Guide level up and a Prismatic Edge. The casters say Jett's Aella is not played yet.

Guruthos draws the fifteen-cost off the top, but with Grande Sonnerie instead of the Armoire he cannot make the full play, and Jett's Imperious Galebind denies the Grande Sonnerie damage. Feu Awakening plus the Array is not enough, the Oblation turn does not happen, and Jett takes game two.

before.summary: Jett wins — Eternal Magistrate, Enfeebling Orb and Zephyr's Hand keep Guruthos's hand locked, and a final Prismatic Edge swing ends it

beats.text: Guruthos goes first, which the casters say should let him level faster than Jett, whose list likes to take turns off for Turbo Charge and Backup Charger. He banishes at random to get the Golden Checkmate into the omens right away, and does not stop to build influence.

Jett's Fluffy Shopkeep and a Fairy Whispers find the Windmill Engineer for more influence. The Eternal Magistrate denies Guruthos's options, delaying the Oblation about as much as the Manxome Armoire matters. Aella, Zephyr's Hand is played on the Prismatic Edge.

Jett plays the Enfeebling Orb once more and uses Zephyr's Hand during the materialization, locking Guruthos's hand and his chances of moving on to the top eight. Guruthos has an Angel Attendant and a Golden Checkmate and needs to pop off, but never finds the Oblation. Jett wins the match 2-1, a match the casters say the sideboard changed.

after.summary: Guruthos wins — an initial Oblation punishes Orb of Sealing, then two more beat Veiling Breeze

beats.text: Guruthos orders his level-up triggers so Liminal Guide draws Baleful Oblation, leaving another Oblation and a fifteen-cost card near the top. Lost Providence enters play, while Jett’s Orb of Sealing threatens the fifteen-cost omen.

Guruthos plays the first Baleful Oblation in response to Jett’s Orb of Sealing. On Jett’s next turn, Ghosts of Pendragon rebuild the ally board and draw cards; one returns Enfeebling Orb to the material deck, leaving it unavailable to disrupt Guruthos’s next turn.

Guruthos materializes Manxome Armoire, draws Advent of the Stormcaller with Umbra Sight, and adds it as an omen at end of turn. He plays Baleful Oblation. Jett digs with Crux Sight and Fairy Whispers, then attempts Veiling Breeze. Guruthos responds with another Oblation and uses Armoire to restore a fifteen-cost omen, winning before Breeze resolves.

beats.text: Jett uses Purifying Thurible to deny Guruthos’s floating memory, then Dungeon Guide and Displace to reach Lorraine, Spirit Ruler. Eternal Magistrate shuts off Guruthos’s Guide plays and Lost Providence activation outside materialization. Jett then materializes Orb of Sealing.

Jett plays Aella during recollection and attacks with his allies. Guruthos uses Chalice of Blood, Umbra Sight, and Abnegation to stay alive. Jett responds to Abnegation with two Spirit Blade: Ascensions: Prismatic Edge draws cards and removes two from Guruthos’s memory, but deals no fire damage. Abnegation then recovers ten.

Resolute Stand buys Guruthos another turn. He retains Baleful Oblation and materializes Grande Sonnerie, then finds another fifteen-cost card. Jett’s Imperious Galebind denies the weapon damage needed to finish. Guruthos concedes without executing the proposed Oblation–Feu Awakening line.

after.summary: Jett wins — Aella and Prismatic Edge deny Ciel level three, then Lorraine lands the final weapon attack

beats.text: Guruthos goes first and uses Creative Shock to discard Golden Checkmate before leveling, choosing speed over a Backup Charger turn. Gentle Respite gives him another draw and floating memory.

Jett plays Eternal Magistrate to block Guruthos’s Guide acceleration, then uses Dungeon Guide and Displace to reach Lorraine, Spirit Ruler himself. Ghosts of Pendragon builds his board. Spirit Blade: Ascension brings in Prismatic Edge, which reveals wind, water, and Guruthos’s fire card for the full effect, including three damage.

Guruthos has Baleful Oblation and Feu Awakening, and uses Resolute Stand’s alternate cost to preserve cards for leveling. Jett’s Aella suppresses Prismatic Edge; its end-step return removes memory and denies Ciel level three. Guruthos materializes Chalice of Blood instead. On Jett’s next turn, ally attacks trigger the Chalice draw, but Guruthos finds Gentle Respite rather than another Resolute Stand. Lorraine’s Prismatic Edge attack finishes the game.

before.deck: Wind Krux Lorraine, Clarent-less build (Lorraine, Wandering Warrior; Sword of Seeking; Drawn Blade; Prismatic Edge; Spirit Blade: Retribution; Aella x3; Ghosts of Pendragon; Fluffy Shopkeep; Imperious Galebind; Obscured Offering; Displace; Dungeon Guide; Inverted Pyro Slash and a one-of fire card)

before.text: The casters list Asuna's options: Dream Fairy, which stops the Krux plan of playing five to seven cards in a turn, and Tempest Downfall, which can kill Aella if Lifdrasyl has not found a second one. They also mention a Blessed Clergy-type body.

after.text: The casters propose Blessed Clergy to limit activations, Dream Fairy to answer Aella, and Tempest Downfall for damage or ally removal. They do not confirm exact boarding changes. Tempest Downfall is later visible in game three.
The casters discuss Annul Spell, Calming Breeze and more attack cards as Lifdrasyl’s options. Annul Spell is visible in game two; exact swaps are not shown.

before.summary: Lifdrasyl wins — Prismatic Edge shows all three colors and Asuna has no cards left

beats.text: Lifdrasyl needs to get rid of Asuna's Eternal Magistrate. He hard levels Lorraine at level one so the on-enter still gives him the sword, and the casters remind that he cannot use Fluffy Shopkeep, Drawn Blade or Obscured Offering that turn. Prismatic Edge is used to rip cards from Asuna's memory.

Asuna builds with Essence Crucible, Scout the Land and Cyclical Breeze, and stacks age counters on the Crucible with herbs and distilled water. He cannot find a Razorgale or the Veiling Breeze for a while, but then Veiling Breeze comes out and Fairy Whispers shows the first Razorgale. Aella suppresses the Crucible and it loses its age counters.

Lifdrasyl takes lots of damage from two Razorgales and the speed potion, but plays Enfeebling Orb through his hand. Displace gives a free activation, and the Prismatic Edge shines in every color. Asuna has no hand left, and Lifdrasyl takes game one with about 30 minutes still on the clock.

before.summary: Asuna wins — three Razorgale triggers with Essence Crucible end the game faster than a Razorgale hit the field in game one

beats.text: Lifdrasyl builds influence with Fluffy Shopkeep and reclaims. The casters are unsure whether he lacks Dungeon Guide or is playing around Stifling Trap. Asuna finds Three Visits and a reclaim for the closing push.

Asuna finds all three Razorgales, while the casters identify a single Verdigris Decree as Lifdrasyl’s answer. Speed Potion helps Asuna recover cards, and Three Visits plus a reclaim set up the remaining damage.

Asuna plays the second and third Razorgales, adding their damage triggers. Essence Crucible boosts the closing damage; the casters explain that Annul Spell cannot stop the Razorgale triggers even if it negates the spell. Asuna ties the match.

before.summary: No winner — time runs out with both players in a tense position, and the round ends as a double loss

beats.text: Lifdrasyl opens with Verdigris Decree and Windmill Engineer. Asuna’s imbued Eternal Magistrate attacks the Engineer, which Lifdrasyl reclaims. Lifdrasyl then levels to Lorraine, Wandering Warrior and brings out Sword of Seeking.

Lifdrasyl plays Dream Fairy to remove Eternal Magistrate. Asuna responds with Escape the Wreckage to save his Magistrate, but does not replay it on the following turn. Asuna keeps digging for Razorgale while Lifdrasyl builds influence.

Lifdrasyl plays Spirit Blade: Retribution and a Sword of Seeking, but cannot play enough cards for the Retribution. The casters count ten cost and eleven cards needed, and Asuna holds a Veiling Breeze. The game goes to time, the result is a draw, and both players take a loss.

after.summary: Lifdrasyl wins — repeated Prismatic Edge triggers exhaust Asuna’s hand

beats.text: Asuna establishes two imbued Eternal Magistrates. Lifdrasyl suppresses one with Verdigris Decree, removing its imbue, then attacks the other after leveling to Lorraine, Blademaster. Asuna reclaims it, opening the way for Lifdrasyl to reach level three.

Asuna eventually finds Razorgale Calling with Fairy Whispers and builds toward multiple Razorgales. Lifdrasyl’s Aella repeatedly suppresses Essence Crucible, removing its accumulated counters, while Asuna uses Veiling Breeze to keep combat damage out.

Imperious Galebind reuses Aella, Ghosts of Pendragon and Prismatic Edge, helping Lifdrasyl find his fire card and cut Asuna’s influence. On Asuna’s next turn, Enfeebling Orb forces more cards down. Displace reuses Aella for another Prismatic Edge trigger showing all three elements; Asuna concedes.

changes.after: Round 6: Water Fractals Diao Chan against Wind Razorgale Arisanna

before.name: Noel
before.deck: Water Fractals Diao Chan, EU Nationals Gauntlet invite (Fractal of Snow, Fractal of Rain, Fractal of Intrusion, Refracting Missile, Shimmering Refraction, Burst Asunder, Glimmering Refusal, Acquiescing Rejection, Frostsworn Paladin, Zhang Jiao, Nullifying Lantern, Wind Resonance Bauble, Fracturize); undefeated at 5-0 coming in

before.name: Asuna
before.deck: Wind Razorgale Arisana (Razorgale x3, Essence Crucible, all four Speed Potions, Tenderland, Distilled Water, Healing Curb, Eternal Magistrate, Fluffy Shopkeep, Viridian Protective Trinket, Scout the Land, Three Visits, Veiling Breeze, Zephyr, Obscured Offering, Stifling Trap); Europe's only Swiss competitor

before.text: The casters see only small differences between the two lists and the side boards. They mention a two-cost wind ally for pressure, Calming Breeze and Nullifying Lantern as possible changes, and note that Noel read the matchup well going into the next game.
The casters call out that Asuna has all four Speed Potions, a greedier choice than the usual Razorgale build. They also say Asuna starts game three with Fluffy Shopkeep, a net-neutral influence card.

after.text: The casters discuss Mystic Purifier, Scatter Essence, Stifling Gyre, Blessed Clergy and additional Calming Breeze as Asuna’s options. They do not confirm the cards exchanged.
The casters discuss Nullifying Mirror and Jianyu, Fate's Premonition as Noel’s options. Nullifying Mirror is subsequently shown in game two; exact swaps are not reported.

before.summary: Noel wins — an imbued Eternal Magistrate does not stop a fast Burst Asunder, and Asuna loses within ten minutes

beats.text: Asuna has the initiative and uses Scout the Land to draw an additional card. His Viridian Protective Trinket makes Noel pay a lot for Refracting Missile at fast speed, and a Purifying Thurible eats the floating memory when Noel passes. Noel has seven cards in hand.

Noel plays a Wind Resonance Bauble to draw right away, builds fractals and glimpses two Shimmering Refractions on top. He puts down a Nullifying Lantern early, and Refracting Missile hits Gwendalin, Spirit of Wind for four. Asuna has an imbued Eternal Magistrate and keeps the Three Visits in memory.
Noel sends the Burst Asunder and Asuna has no answer. The casters say Asuna loses within ten minutes of the start of the round, because his Three Visits stayed in memory and his plan never started.

before.summary: Asuna wins — a triple Razorgale line, a lucky top-deck run and the Essence Crucible beat Noel's Burst

beats.text: Noel puts out the Fractal of Snow, building fractals, and is two turns away from winning. The casters call Noel's read going into the game insane. Asuna has an Essence Crucible and an Aetherial draw off the on-enter.

Asuna finds Distilled Water, a herb and a Speed Potion, and the casters say it might be enough. He fires off the Burst Asunder-style line: triple Razorgale, can you stop me? Noel's Glimmering Refusal has to hit the Speed Potion, and Acquiescing Rejection and Refracting Missile trade back.

Asuna comes back with three Razorgale triggers and a series of very fortunate top-decks and banishes. Noel scoops to save time for game three; the casters note the 50 minutes on the clock and that both players are on level one.

before.summary: Asuna wins — Speed Potions, Zephyr and Obscured Offering protect the Essence Crucible, and win card into win card finishes

beats.text: Asuna opens with Fluffy Shopkeep and a discounted Razorgale Calling, going to Arisana level one with a Reclaim. Noel plays a raw Fractal of Intrusion without taking extra floating-memory value. The casters say it is a longer, slower game where every marginal gain matters.

Asuna uses Tenderland to gather and draw, setting up another Speed Potion. Noel tries to Fracturize the Essence Crucible in response, but Asuna has six cards in hand, so the Fracturize does not matter. Obscured Offering gives the Crucible spell shroud, and the casters call it a devastating position for Noel.

Two Speed Potions give agility six and then three again at end phase. Asuna picks up the entire memory and finds three wind cards: a two-cost, a one-cost and a zero-cost for three damage each. Wind card into wind card into wind card is the game, and Asuna wins the match 2-1. There is no longer an undefeated player at Worlds, and the casters say it is revenge for HenkieTheGoat, whom Noel had denied a European Nationals slot.

after.summary: Noel wins — Burst Asunder ends the game while Asuna is still on Gwendalin

beats.text: Noel reserves Fractal of Intrusion to cast Refracting Missile before Intrusion’s on-enter resolves, then uses the floating memory to discard Asuna’s Speed Potion. Asuna has already found an opening Razorgale Calling with Scout the Land.

Asuna materializes Viridian Protective Trinket and later plays Eternal Magistrate, imbuing it with two Three Visits. Noel builds fractals, deals four with Refracting Missile and materializes Nullifying Lantern.

Noel sends Burst Asunder while Asuna remains on Gwendolyn, Spirit of Wind. Asuna has no answer and loses game one. The two Three Visits are in memory; the casters’ discussion of whether keeping one would have saved him is inconclusive.

after.summary: Asuna wins — three Razorgales and Essence Crucible force Noel’s concession

beats.text: Asuna opens with Fluffy Shopkeep. Noel’s Acquiescing Rejection stops Reclaim when Asuna declines the draw. Noel later changes Fractal of Intrusion’s discard choice from Razorgale Calling to Stifling Trap; Asuna levels to Arisanna and establishes three Razorgales.
Noel materializes Nullifying Mirror and develops Fractal of Snow. Asuna brings out Essence Crucible, keeps Distilled Water through the level cost and finds Speed Potion for the closing turn.

Noel contests Speed Potion with Acquiescing Rejection and Glimmering Refusal. The casters explain that brewing still gives Essence Crucible its counter despite the negation. Noel concedes with further Razorgale damage available.

after.summary: Asuna wins — Obscured Offering protects Crucible, then three wind spells finish

beats.text: Noel opens with two Fractals of Snow and keeps Fracturize for Essence Crucible instead of using it to build another fractal. Asuna uses Reclaim while Noel is committed to Backup Charger, then levels to Arisanna and plays the discounted Razorgale Calling.

Asuna sets up Viridian Protective Trinket, Tend the Land and two Speed Potions. Noel responds to the second brew with Fracturize targeting Essence Crucible. Obscured Offering gives Crucible spellshroud, preserving its counters; the proposed defensive Zephyr is not the play used.
The Speed Potions recover cards through agility. In the end phase, Asuna plays Veiling Breeze, Calming Breeze and Three Visits for three Razorgale damage each, winning the match 2–1.

before.name: Raylam
before.deck: Fire Oblation CL, ally-focused build (Baleful Oblation, Feu Awakening, Manxome Armoire, Hasty Messenger, Three of Hearts, Liminal Guide, Fluffy Shopkeep, Escape the Wreckage, Dungeon Guide x2, Mirage's Grave, Crystallized Destiny)

before.name: Jayare
before.deck: Fire Suzaku Guo A (Fabled Ruby Fatestone, Avatar of Suzaku from Radiant Origins, Peppered Chef, Searing Truth, Fiery Interference, Impact Hammer, Heated Vengeance, Blazing Throw, Loyal Valet, Crystallized Destiny, Restorative Flames; Orb of Sealing)

before.text: The casters expect Jayare to bring in Restorative Flames and an Abnegation-style card to answer a single Oblation. They say that after siding, he now has another out in addition to Crystallized Destiny, and that Feu Awakening forces a spell-shroud hand.

after.text: The casters propose Restorative Flame and Annul Spell as Jayare’s options against Baleful Oblation. They discuss Feu Awakening as counterplay to a negate; the recording does not establish the exact boarding changes.

before.summary: Raylam wins — Hasty Messenger into double Escape the Wreckage, early CL level three, and one Baleful Oblation after Jayare's bluff fails

beats.text: Raylam opens with Three of Hearts attacking the Hasty Messenger, and Escape the Wreckage discarded to the Hasty. Jayare can shoot the Hasty but loses a card, because there is no Fabled Ruby Fatestone yet, so he cannot get the quest counter. Raylam has an insane start: Hasty into double Escape plus a 15-cost already in the omens.

Jayare plays Guo A level one, puts out the Fabled Ruby Fatestone, a Searing Truth and Peppered Chef, and then Avatar of Suzaku, a new Radiant Origins card he plays for four and keeps two quest counters up. Six damage is marked on CL, but Raylam goes to CL level two with a Liminal Guide and gets a Dungeon Guide down to level three with Mirage's Grave.

Jayare uses his own Orb of Sealing to stop Raylam from using the Baleful Oblation on the 15-cost, turning both omens face down, but Raylam has the Manxome Armoire in the material deck. Jayare looks for Crystallized Destiny with Creative Shock and does not find it. He bluffs with six cards in hand, the bluff fails, and Raylam sends the Oblation to win game one.

before.summary: Jayare wins — a turn-two Heated Vengeance, Impact Hammer and Blazing Throw line kills before Oblation matters

beats.text: Jayare opens with Three of Hearts, and Raylam has the Hasty Messenger and Escape the Wreckage start again. Fiery Interference comes down before the Ruby Fate Stone, so Jayare does not get the quest counter. Raylam discards a Liminal Guide, and the casters say a double Three of Hearts would have turned it for him.
The casters call out the cards in Jayare's grip: Impact Hammer, Heated Vengeance and Blazing Throw, with all the pieces for a lethal turn two into four.

Jayare plays Heated Vengeance into a big swing at Raylam's face, hits with the Impact Hammer, and throws it with Blazing Throw. Raylam has no answer. The casters call it an insane turn-two Turbo line and say the two games took only 15 minutes. Raylam goes on to win game three, which the VOD does not show.

after.summary: Raylam wins — Manxome Armoire restores a fifteen-cost omen for Baleful Oblation

Jayare develops Fabled Ruby Fatestone, Searing Truth and Avatar of Suzaku. Raylam levels to Ciel, Omenbringer, discards Liminal Guide and uses Dungeon Guide to reach Mirage’s Grave; omen damage removes Avatar of Suzaku.

Jayare’s Orb of Sealing turns the omens face down. Raylam uses Manxome Armoire to restore the fifteen-cost omen and sends Baleful Oblation. Jayare digs with Creative Shock and Undeniable Truth but finds no saving Crystallized Destiny; Raylam wins game one.

changes.after: Round 7: Wind Crux Lorraine mirror

before.name: GlenyBoi
before.deck: Wind Krux Lorraine, 2024 world champion (Lorraine; Spirit Blade: Ascension; Aella; Ghosts of Pendragon; Spirit Ruler with Drawn Blade; Imperious Galebind; Crux Sight; Reclaim; Fluffy Shopkeep; Dungeon Guide; Turbo Charge; Windmill Engineer; Eternal Magistrate from the side; no Clarent)

before.name: DuckHats
before.deck: Wind Krux Lorraine, TM32 list, nearly card-for-card the same as GlenyBoi's (Lorraine; Dungeon Guide x2; Turbo Charge; Spirit Blade: Retribution; Displace; Fluffy Shopkeep; Eternal Magistrate x2; Psychopomp's Scale in the side; Chamberlain Toad)

before.text: The casters discuss Eternal Magistrate in the mirror: when it is imbued, neither player can bring cards out of the material deck, which hits Fluffy Shopkeep, Spirit Blade: Ascension and similar. They also mention Ghost of Pendragon as a mirror tiebreaker and Chamberlain Toad as a possible card to bring in.

after.text: The casters discuss Annul Spell, Calming Breeze, Chamberlain Toad and Psychopomp’s Scale as GlenyBoi’s options. Annul Spell is subsequently played in game two; exact swaps are not shown.

DuckHats plays imbued Eternal Magistrate in game two. It restricts GlenyBoi’s material deck outside GlenyBoi’s materialize phase, leaving DuckHats free to use his own Dungeon Guides. The broadcast also discusses Annul Spell and Calming Breeze as options.

before.summary: GlenyBoi wins — DuckHats sees no path in a mirror that tends to run long and concedes to start game two

beats.text: DuckHats gets a smooth Dungeon Guide level up to two and swings with Fluffy Shopkeep, while GlenyBoi has fewer Turbo Charges. The casters say a stack battle is coming, with Displace held up to use on the Dungeon Guide at the end of GlenyBoi's turn.

GlenyBoi plays Ghosts of Pendragon to put the Sword of Seeking back and draw two, finds Fairy Whispers, and the casters explain that the player who draws more Ghosts usually gets ahead on influence. Neither player has found an Aella yet, which the casters say is the card that turns the matchup into a fast-speed war.

A fire card drawn off the Purifying Thurible and GlenyBoi's Spirit Blade: Ascension hit hard. DuckHats sees he has no path to winning and, since Krux mirror games can run an hour, decides to go next. GlenyBoi goes 1-0.

before.summary: GlenyBoi wins — the Crux Sight line strips DuckHats down and ends the mirror in a very short game

beats.text: DuckHats opens with Turbo Charge, finds a Dungeon Guide and holds the Eternal Magistrate for Lorraine level two. GlenyBoi reveals the Eternal Magistrate off the imbue, so he knows what DuckHats holds. The casters note DuckHats wishes he had a Hurricane Sweep, but it is not in the deck.

GlenyBoi sniffs out the play and gets a huge push, bringing the Aella to hand and using Imperious Galebind and the Ghost of Pendragon at the right moments. DuckHats's second Eternal Magistrate comes out, and a Windmill Engineer could take out the Pendragon, but GlenyBoi has a Crux Sight.

GlenyBoi rips cards with Crux Sight and takes DuckHats's hand down to six, then seven. DuckHats reached level three early but did not have the Krux cards he needed. The casters call it maybe the fastest game of the whole stream, and GlenyBoi wins the mirror 2-0.

after.summary: GlenyBoi wins — repeated Prismatic Edge triggers and Ghosts draws force a concession

beats.text: Both players build influence with Fluffy Shopkeep and Backup Charger. DuckHats reaches Lorraine, Blademaster with Dungeon Guide. When GlenyBoi later uses Displace to level, DuckHats responds with his own Displace before the opposing Prismatic Edge engine can strip his memory.
GlenyBoi develops Ghosts of Pendragon and Spirit Blade: Ascension, keeping DuckHats low on influence through Prismatic Edge. A fire card in memory enables damage as well as the wind effect.

Imperious Galebind suppresses Prismatic Edge and Ghosts of Pendragon. The returning Ghosts put Sword of Seeking back and draw two. DuckHats draws Retribution without enough influence to use it and concedes.

after.summary: GlenyBoi wins — Annul Spell opens the level-up, then Aella and Ascension take over

beats.text: DuckHats reveals Eternal Magistrate while imbuing an Engineer, then plays Magistrate to constrain GlenyBoi. DuckHats breaks a hard-materialized Drawn Blade in combat and reaches level three ahead of GlenyBoi.

GlenyBoi’s Rally the Peasants misses. He later uses Annul Spell against DuckHats’s Imperious Galebind, gets the Lorraine draw and finds Dungeon Guide. That lets him reach Spirit Ruler, then play Ghosts of Pendragon and find Ascension.

GlenyBoi draws more Ghosts, Aella and Ascension. Aella suppresses Prismatic Edge, and Crux Sight returns Ascension for another Edge trigger. DuckHats loses more memory cards and concedes without finding the Crux cards to recover.

before.name: DragonJG
before.deck: Water Umbra Alice, Phantom Monarch mill, the deck's progenitor (Phantasmagoria, Dynastic Whirlpool, Tri-Castles, Maledictum Vitae, Rector's Tiding, Banner Sash, Turbo Charge x1, Backup Charger, Fracturize, Angel Attendant, Benediction Angel; no Fountain Seraphim)

before.name: Sano
before.deck: Wind Krux Lorraine, TM32 list, OCE Nationals winner (Prismatic Edge, Spirit Blade: Ascension, Obscured Offering, Windmill Engineer x2, Fairy Whispers with a low wind count in the low 30s, Turbo Charge, Ghosts of Pendragon, Cleansing Reunion, Displace)

before.summary: DragonJG wins — the recording shows only the early and middle game, and the casters confirm the win afterwards

beats.text: The casters say this is the same matchup as in CNAT, between the Umbra Mill Alice master and Wind Krux. DragonJG takes an off turn to Backup Charger and Fracturize up to Alice level one. The casters explain that Alice's Phantasmagoria mastery turns off floating-memory and graveyard effects that are not Spectre cards.

Sano influence-maxes with Windmill Engineer, Cleansing Reunion and Fairy Whispers, and finds Ghosts of Pendragon. He misses on purpose with Fairy Whispers on three Crux cards, a hard decision. The casters say his best route is an Ascension loop that hits every card in DragonJG's hand, which was not enough in CNAT either.

DragonJG goes to Alice level two and plays Phantasmagoria, which on his end phase puts the graveyard back into the deck and mills by the number of counters. He adds a Maledictum Vitae, a Turbo Charge that was not in his list at CNAT, and Dynastic Whirlpool as the nasty exalted water card. Sano has Obscured Offering to keep Prismatic Edge from being fracturized. The recording stops here, and the casters announce afterwards that DragonJG won the game and the match 2-0.

after.summary: DragonJG wins — only the opening is shown; the result is announced afterwards

beats.text: DragonJG uses Backup Charger followed by Turbo Charge. The casters first discuss Fracturize as a possible line, then explicitly identify Turbo Charge as the play instead.
Sano builds influence with Windmill Engineer and Fairy Whispers. When Fairy Whispers shows three Crux cards, he bottoms them and takes a blind draw that finds Reclaim.

The casters identify Maledictum Vitae for DragonJG and discuss his next level-up to Alice, Phantom Monarch. Sano’s Turbo Charge finds Ascension and Obscured Offering. The recording cuts off before the level-up or a finishing sequence; the casters then announce DragonJG’s game-one and 2–0 match wins.

before.text: TeamTrueCaban brings in a Nullifying Mirror, which the casters call a huge card against Veiling Breeze and Windmill Engineer. They note the mirror also turns off Spirit Blade: Ascension's imbue plan. He also keeps an eye on the Quicksilver Grail, which is strong with the Mirror, and Return to the Archive.
The casters say Sano has little to bring in. Crystallized Destiny can have value against Fractals, but Calming Breeze is the only card really shining in his side.

after.text: TeamTrueCaban brings out Nullifying Mirror in game two. The casters discuss its value against Veiling Breeze and wind imbue effects. Quicksilver Grail is a comparison; his registered divine relic is The Looking Glass.
Sano has Annul Spell in game two and plays it during the final exchange. The casters discuss Calming Breeze and Crystallized Destiny as possible additions; exact swaps are not shown.

before.summary: TeamTrueCaban wins — he goes first with five fractals and Zhang Jiao, and Sano concedes

beats.text: TeamTrueCaban wins the roll and goes first, which the casters call a pretty big deal for Fractals. He plays an unstable fractal and holds Zhang Jiao. He glimpses and bottoms two cards he does not need.

The casters note that Sano's list has no Clarent, so he has less defense against Burst Asunder. Sano has no Stifling Trap to stop the Zhang Jiao draws. TeamTrueCaban has eight cards in hand and four fractals, effectively 12 influence, with Glimmering Refusals backing up the kill turn.

Sano plays Purifying Thurible and stays on his spirit with five fractals staring him down. The casters call it a default win for TeamTrueCaban, who only had to play the cards, and Sano concedes early to keep time for game two. The casters say TM32 are happy to concede early with Wind Krux to avoid a double loss.

before.summary: TeamTrueCaban wins — Nullifying Mirror shuts off the Wind Krux engine and three Shimmering Refractions finish

beats.text: TeamTrueCaban brings out the Nullifying Mirror early, which stops Veiling Breeze and the imbues of Windmill Engineer and Fluffy Shopkeep. Sano's Fluffy Shopkeep does not resolve, so the Drawn Blade has to be hard materialized or skipped, and TeamTrueCaban draws two off the punish of cutting Clarent.

Sano has a Verdigris Decree for one of the fractals, and Windmill Engineers that are dead cards in hand because of the mirror. Lorraine, Blademaster cannot get anything out of her level and Sano is stuck. TeamTrueCaban holds a Fracturize and Return to the Archive and swings with the Frostsworn Paladin for three.

TeamTrueCaban sends three Shimmering Refractions, a Zhang Jiao poke and a Frostsworn Paladin attack, taking Sano to 15, then 16 with eight damage needed. Sano pays for his null spell, and Veiling Breeze does nothing under the mirror. TeamTrueCaban wins 2-0 and moves toward the asynchronous bracket. The casters call it a really heads-up play.

after.summary: TeamTrueCaban wins — he goes first with five fractals and Zhang Jiao, and Sano concedes

beats.text: TeamTrueCaban goes first with an imbued Fractal of Rain and builds toward Zhang Jiao, Way of Peace. He bottoms an extra Acquiescing Rejection and Burst Asunder while setting up the draw.

The casters note that Sano's list has no Clarent, so he has less defense against Burst Asunder. Sano has no Stifling Trap to stop the Zhang Jiao draws. TeamTrueCaban has eight cards in hand and four fractals, effectively 12 influence, with Glimmering Refusals backing up the kill turn.

The casters say TM32 are happy to concede early with Wind Krux to avoid a double loss.

after.summary: TeamTrueCaban wins — Nullifying Mirror limits Sano’s answers to the final Burst Asunder

beats.text: TeamTrueCaban uses Acquiescing Rejection on Fluffy Shopkeep. Sano allows the two-card draw, so Shopkeep resolves. TeamTrueCaban later uses Fractal of Intrusion to discard Ghosts of Pendragon, then kills Shopkeep with Refracting Missile.

Nullifying Mirror turns Sano’s memory cards norm, limiting Windmill Engineer’s imbue and Veiling Breeze. Sano uses Verdigris Decree on a fractal, but TeamTrueCaban’s Shimmering Refraction removes an Engineer before it can help Lorraine finish Frostsworn Paladin. The Paladin keeps attacking.

Three Shimmering Refractions and attacks from Frostsworn Paladin and Zhang Jiao set up Burst Asunder. TeamTrueCaban pays for Sano’s Annul Spell. Sano has only one Veiling Breeze against the held Nullifying Mirror and concedes the match.

before.summary: Z3US wins — an opening of triple Firebloom Flourish and Ravenous Pyre lets him dump his hand every turn, and Tristan dies at level one

beats.text: Schwarzer wins the die roll and goes first with Spirit of Wind, drawing seven cards. He opens with a Windmill Engineer and holds a Sadi and Innervate Agility, but the casters could not see a Reclaim. Z3US would have loved to go first with fire aggro.

Z3US plays Spirit of Fire and starts with two Firebloom Flourishes, the card that lets Diao Chan sit at low influence: at the beginning of the end phase, with four or fewer influence, he draws a card into memory and puts a glimmer counter on his champion. He dumps his hand each turn and goes from three up to five influence, always with six cards or more.

Z3US uses Shimmering Refraction for four damage and the triple Firebloom Flourishes ping for the rest. Schwarzer incapacitates one Searing Rebuke and the casters say he would have died a turn earlier without it, but there are too many fire damage sources. Tristan dies without leaving level one.

before.summary: Z3US wins — three Searing Rebukes, with Fractal of Sparks pinging himself, kill through Incapacitate and a Censer

beats.text: Schwarzer plays Spirit of Wind and a very interesting turn-one Blanche, Sheltering Saint, and holds a Reclaim to keep it protected. He then plays Fairy Whispers but drops to two cards in hand. Z3US sees the opening, and the first Firebloom Flourish and Blanche die to his damage.

Every card Z3US puts down is answered or taken off the board, but Fractal of Sparks deals one every turn, and the Necklace of Foresight digs for another Firebloom Flourish. Schwarzer materializes Shadow's Claw and passes, letting the Searing Rebuke damage come in; Z3US recovers four with a fast gear. Schwarzer has no Surveil the Winds to find the lethal opening.

Schwarzer keeps having to spend Incapacitate on a Searing Rebuke and cannot find the extra two damage for lethal. Z3US redirects an attack, plays Searing Rebuke in response to the Censer of Restful Peace, and has the Fractal of Sparks ping himself to trigger the Rebuke. The casters count three Searing Rebukes in the game, and Z3US wins 2-0, going 6-3 and into Day 2. Schwarzer finishes at 5-4.

after.summary: Z3US wins — Firebloom Flourish fuels a fast start, then Shimmering Refraction and Everflame Staff finish Tristan before his level-up resolves

beats.text: Schwarzer wins the die roll and opens with Sadi, followed by Windmill Engineer. He returns Sadi to hand for a preparation counter and uses Incapacitate to stop Searing Rebuke during the Engineer’s attack.

Z3US opens two Firebloom Flourishes and later finds a third. Ravenous Pyre pressures Tristan’s leveling, while Ashwick Cremator and Smoke Out add damage. The Flourishes replenish Z3US’s memory and glimmer counters after he empties his hand.

As Schwarzer attempts to materialize Tristan, Hired Blade, Z3US uses Shimmering Refraction and Everflame Staff for four damage each. The eight damage ends the game before Tristan gains the level-two life total.

after.summary: Z3US wins — three Searing Rebukes, with Fractal of Sparks pinging himself, kill through Incapacitate and a Censer

beats.text: Schwarzer opens Blanche, Sheltering Saint, then spends cards on Fairy Whispers. Z3US removes Blanche with Shimmering Refraction. Schwarzer follows with Backup Charger and Scatter Essence on Firebloom Flourish; Stifling Trap also removes Ashwick Cremator before it can contribute damage.

A second Scatter Essence removes Z3US’s next Firebloom Flourish, but Fractal of Sparks, Fanatical Devotee and Acolyte of Cultivation keep dealing damage. Schwarzer develops preparation counters, levels through Dungeon Guide and materializes Shadow’s Claw. Searing Rebuke stops him committing to the attack line; Z3US recovers with Fast Cure and later materializes Tariff Ring.

Schwarzer redirects an attack, then negates Searing Rebuke with Incapacitate as he materializes Censer of Restful Peace. The spent cards and preparation counters leave him short of lethal. On Z3US’s next turn, Schwarzer uses Innervate Agility and chooses stealth. Z3US plays another Searing Rebuke and targets himself with Fractal of Sparks, dealing the final three damage to Tristan after the delevel reduces his life total.

before.deck: Fire Diao Chan aggro from Indonesia (Firebloom Flourish x3, Searing Rebuke x3, Fractal of Sparks, Shimmering Refraction, Ravenous Pyre, Ashwick Cremator, Necklace of Foresight, Fanatical Devotee, Acolyte of Cultivation, Wind Resonance Bauble, Grand Crusader's Ring, Spirit of Fire with alternate art; Scatter Essence x3-4, Safeguard Amulet, Blanche and Staggering Strike in the side)

before.text: The casters think Schwarzer should bring in Blanche, Safeguard Amulet and Scatter Essence to deal with Firebloom Flourish, and the three Staggering Strikes to keep Z3US from a lethal line. They say cards like Ensnaring Fumes are too spell-based to matter, and even Guan Yu does little, because Diao Chan seldom fights a board. A printout issue with the sideboard list was sorted out by the judges before game two.
Z3US likes Necklace of Foresight, which glimpses four cards, to find his Firebloom Flourishes faster. The casters say Z3US may also bring in anti-Tristan tech such as Crystallized Essence.

after.text: The casters recommend Blanche, Sheltering Saint, Safeguard Amulet and Scatter Essence for Schwarzer. Blanche, Safeguard Amulet and two Scatter Essences are observed in game two. Ensnaring Fumes remains in the deck despite the suggestion to remove it. A sideboard printout issue is resolved before play resumes.

The casters identify three Staggering Strikes in Z3US’s sideboard as an option to remove Tristan’s preparation counters. They do not confirm a swap. In the post-match interview, Z3US describes Crystallized Destiny as preparation for Genbu and Crux Lorraine.

before.summary: Limbo wins — Storm of Thorns, taunt allies and Song of Frost keep Tristan from ever connecting

beats.text: Limbo opens with a three-attack hindered Seneschal on turn one, and Frostbind on the Blackmarket Broker's reclaim denies Silvercrowx his floating memory. The casters say two taunt allies are very hard to deal with, because swinging into one makes you swing into the other.

Limbo has Castling Boon and Corhazi Trapper in hand and nothing on his board dies. Lily returns cards each time he trades. Silvercrowx goes up to Tristan level one with three preparation counters, and the casters say it will be very difficult for him to come back.

Silvercrowx finds a Shadowstrike and Mastermind Scheme, goes up to 12 preparation counters and redirects with his shadows. Limbo holds a Storm of Thorns, a Song of Frost and other defensive cards, and every Tristan swing is stopped. The casters say Silvercrowx cannot close the game out.
Limbo returns to a full board of allies and Magebane Lash counters. Silvercrowx loses prep to every defensive card and Limbo wins game one by attrition.

before.summary: Limbo wins — Tariff Ring and Storm of Thorns undo Silvercrowx's preparation again and again, and the allies swing in

beats.text: Silvercrowx has a weak hand for the game: reclaiming Sadi makes no sense, and he has a Windmill Engineer and an Ancient Protector to play. Limbo uses the Grand Crusader's Ring and a Storm of Thorns, and Silvercrowx cannot clear the Corhazi Trapper's board.

Limbo uses Freezing Hail to bounce the Windmill Engineer and the Aesan Protector, and Silvercrowx must level up and loses another Aesan Protector. The casters note that Silvercrowx has three Aesan Protectors in the deck, and that his allies cannot swing past Limbo's Tariff Ring.

Silvercrowx is stuck in a loop where he builds his preparation counters and then loses them. The casters liken him to Sisyphus climbing a hill. Limbo's Lily and Corhazi Trapper return, and Limbo adds a Snow White to shut down attacks.

Silvercrowx swings his Windmill Engineer, Sadi and Winbless Lookout into Lily, but Limbo has more damage on board than he expected and finishes the game through the Aesan Protector. The casters say it was the ninth round and everyone was tired. Limbo has won an invite to Day 2.

after.summary: Limbo wins — defensive allies and attack prevention stop Tristan’s comeback

beats.text: Limbo opens with Aquifer Seneschal and Frostbinds Reclaim as it tries to save Blackmarket Broker. Lily and Corhazi Trapper establish a protected board.
Limbo keeps a protected ally board while Silvercrowx reaches Tristan level 1 with three preparation counters. The casters describe a difficult recovery for Silvercrowx.

Silvercrowx loses Shadowstrike during his level-up but rebuilds preparation with Mastermind Scheme. Storm of Thorns prevents his weapon attack, stopping the shadows from attacking. Limbo maintains his defensive board.
Silvercrowx finds Slice and Dice, but Limbo leaves Aquifer Seneschal active and answers with Deflecting Edge. Silvercrowx cannot turn his attacks into a finishing line, and Limbo takes game one.

after.summary: Limbo wins — Staggering Strike strips preparation and the rebuilt ally board closes through Aesan Protector

beats.text: Both players materialize Grand Crusader’s Ring. Freezing Hail removes Windmill Engineer during Aesan Protector’s entry, forcing the Protector to return itself.

Storm of Thorns protects Limbo’s board, and Staggering Strike removes three preparation counters. Tariff Ring restricts Silvercrowx’s attacks. Limbo uses Smoke Bombs on Aesan Protector, but Veiling Breeze prevents champion damage that turn.

After reaching Tristan level 3, Silvercrowx resolves Ensnaring Fumes, returning Limbo’s allies and removing his own shadow tokens. Limbo rebuilds with Corhazi Trapper and Snow White, and a second Staggering Strike strips preparation again.

Silvercrowx removes Snow White, but Limbo restores Jueying’s support with Lily. Freezing Hail keeps Tristan rested despite Veiling Breeze preventing its damage. Manxome Armoire returns Freezing Hail on the closing turn; Limbo clears Aesan Protector and finishes with his allies.

before.text: The casters think Limbo boards in extra water cards, such as a Menzo-armour card, in favor of the Nico plan, and say both decks have Mandate of Honour in the side. They say Silvercrowx's side has no Shadow Reaper plan, so he cannot ensnare Limbo's board.

after.text: The casters discuss Manxome Armoire, Staggering Strike and another Corhazi Trapper for Limbo, and Ensnaring Fumes and Tristan, Shadowreaver for Silvercrowx. Manxome Armoire, Staggering Strike and Ensnaring Fumes appear in game 2; exact swaps are not shown.

before.summary: Muck1234 wins — level 12 from Enlightenment counters, then Erratic Bolt and two Arcane Blasts for 18

beats.text: ZeRoMagus starts with Three of Hearts and plays Orb of Sealing, which flips all Muck1234's banished Arcane cards face down. The casters say this is the problem card for Rai: Muck1234 must play an Arcane Sight to break the Orb and turn them face up. Muck1234 stays at level 2 and does not find a Dungeon Guide.

Muck1234 puts three Arcane cards into memory and levels to three. He keeps his hand up with Enlightenment counters, plays Tome of Sacred Lightning and banishes Arcane cards every turn. With Power Overwhelming he reaches level 12, then 13, and he sculpts the top of his deck with Careful Study.

Muck1234 keeps two Arcane Blasts on top of the deck and throws nine banished cards into Erratic Bolt. Nine damage plus two Arcane Blasts is 18, and ZeRoMagus, on Merlin, has no answer. The casters say that this is the most extreme version of a Rai turn they have seen.

before.summary: Muck1234 wins — 21 damage through Merlin's board, with Advent of the Stormcaller and Erratic Bolt

beats.text: ZeRoMagus has a better game than game 1. Fluffy Shopkeep on turn one, then Liminal Guide and a Backup Charger, with more than seven influence.

Muck1234 draws with Peer into Mana but runs low on influence. ZeRoMagus levels to three; the casters anticipate four Dungeon Guides and two Hasty Messengers. Muck1234’s Topsy Decree interrupts the Guide sequence, leaving ZeRoMagus low on influence.

Muck1234 plays Enfeebling Orb to stop two plays, which pops Crystallized Destiny, and plays Tome of Sacred Lightning and a 13 to 15 level turn. Advent of the Stormcaller and Erratic Bolt add up to 21 damage, and the casters count that ZeRoMagus is dead even with Harmonious Mantra.

after.summary: Muck1234 wins — Rai’s Arcane engine overwhelms Merlin

beats.text: Muck1234 reaches a high level with his Arcane cards and uses Mnemonic Charm to reach level 15. Advent of the Stormcaller examines the remaining deck and leaves Arcane Blasts on top.

The casters count nine newly banished cards and enough damage with the available Arcane Blasts to end the game. ZeRoMagus had committed his hand to leveling Merlin and cannot survive the response turn.

after.summary: Muck1234 wins — a 21-damage Erratic Bolt finishes a much larger burst turn

beats.text: Muck1234’s Topsy Decree interrupts the anticipated Guide sequence as ZeRoMagus reaches level 3, leaving Merlin low on influence.
Enfeebling Orb forces cards down. Muck1234 uses Arcane Sight, Spirit of Purity’s ability and Tome of Sacred Lightning to build levels before Advent of the Stormcaller banishes more Arcane cards.

At level 21, Muck1234 casts Erratic Bolt for 21 after the Advent damage. The casters count total damage well beyond lethal even with Harmonious Mantra; the additional Blast lines they discuss are unnecessary.

before.summary: Tsu wins in about 8 minutes — Arthur, Veteran Blazebearer and Inverted Pyroslash pressure Over9000 before he can level

beats.text: Tsu levels to CL level 1 and gets Omen stacking immediately. Over9000 also levels to level 1. Veteran Blazebearer has steadfast, so it is a taunt on turn one, and Tsu plays Hasty Messenger, discarding Gentle Respite, and Fluffy Shopkeep to draw a card into memory.

Arthur, Young Heir comes down on turn two and Tsu attacks with Arthur and the Blazebearer. His fire Guardian attack cards, Inverted Pyroslash and Blazing Charge, hit for three or five with Impact Hammer, and they cost less with Omens. Over9000 loses influence each time he must play a card to survive, and Censer of Restful Peace stops his Gentle Respite from giving him a plus one.

Over9000 cannot level to Umbra level 3 because Tsu keeps up the pressure. The casters say Over9000 has Resolute Stand in hand but nothing else. He shakes his head when asked for a response, and the attack resolves for lethal.

before.summary: Tsu wins — Over9000 has a slow hand of level-three cards, and Heated Vengeance, Blazing Throw and Intensified Pyre end the game

beats.text: Over9000 goes first with Liminal Guide and Cremation Ritual, but his hand has Dungeon Guide, Liminal Guide, Baleful Oblation, Advent of the Stormcaller and Resolute Stand and few cheap plays. The casters say this slow start is as dangerous as it gets against fire aggro.

Tsu plays Arthur, Young Heir and a Veteran Blazebearer again, and they deal six damage per turn. Over9000 uses Resolute Stand and loses a Baleful Oblation card, and the Dungeon Guide level-up comes too late. Over9000 only has two influence for the Fluffy Shopkeep intercept, and Tsu removes it with Smoke Bombs.

Tsu plays Fire Resonance Bauble to draw more cards and puts Over9000 at 11, then 14, with attacks. Heated Vengeance comes in for seven. Blazing Throw and Intensified Pyre add the rest of the damage with Cinder Geyser, and Over9000 is dead before he reaches level 3.

after.summary: Tsu wins — early allies and Blazing Charge race the level-up

beats.text: Tsu establishes Veteran Blazebearer and Arthur, then Censer of Restful Peace. Over9000, not Tsu, plays Hasty Messenger and Fluffy Shopkeep.
Tsu follows the ally attacks with Impact Hammer and Blazing Charge, pushing Over9000 to 16 damage. The finishing attack resolves before Over9000 can reach level 3.

after.summary: Tsu wins — Arthur and Red Hare set up Heated Vengeance and Blazing Throw

beats.text: Arthur and Red Hare maintain pressure as Over9000 loses key resources while leveling. Fluffy Shopkeep supplies a blocker but cannot hold the attack off.
Tsu uses Fire Resonance Bauble and Intensified Pyre, then attacks with Arthur and Red Hare. Heated Vengeance and Blazing Throw supply the finishing damage before Ciel level 3 enters.

Over9000 plans to side out some of the extra Spirits. The casters say he also wants cards that stop Omens, and that Crystallized Destiny and Resolute Stand could have done more work in game 1.
