before.text: The casters talk through Asuna's side: Tempest Downfall, which is fast and breaks a spell, and the Zephyr, which does little in this matchup. They say the extra Shadowstrike protects him against Regal Inquisition.

after.text: The casters consider extra Astra defenses for AuraBomb and Scatter Essence, Regal Inquisition, Heavenly Guide and Blanche for Asuna. They discuss Tempest Downfall as a possible way to consume Spellshield: Astra’s prevention before Shadowstrike, not a confirmed swap. Scatter Essence is shown in Asuna’s game-two hand.

before.summary: Xenadrael wins — a fast allies start with Ardent Cloudstriker overwhelms Perfy

beats.text: Xenadrael opens with a fast allies start. An Ardent Cloudstriker, a five-cost three-four, is intimidating by itself, because it can take care of all the two-three allies. The casters say Perfy's early game is not impressive and he is not in a good position.

Perfy plays Chilling Touch and Cheshire Cat, but Xenadrael's cloud striker goes for the Cheshire Cat and adds three more damage. The casters say the game was very close to over twice already, and that if the Cloud Striker had stuck the game would have ended sooner.
Xenadrael closes out the quick game one. The casters say it was so fast and so aggressive that it looked like an allies deck.

before.summary: Xenadrael wins — Zephyr and two Tempest Downfalls recycle for the last seven damage

beats.text: Xenadrael goes to level two and plays favorable winds, which cost one and draw cards. He reveals a card to prove he cannot take more than three damage this turn. The casters say this game shows why a Razor Gale deck is still a threat.

Perfy keeps the Spirit Blade: Ascension up until Xenadrael's turn, which is smart. The casters say losing a card to the ascension is very painful. Perfy has Dungeon Guide and Ghosts of Pendragon in hand and plays safe with his Veiling Breeze instead of putting down cards.
Xenadrael has Zephyr and two Tempest Downfalls in hand, each dealing five damage, and the cards recycle so he only needs seven more damage. Xenadrael wins game two and the quarterfinal.

after.summary: Xenadrael wins — a fast allies start with Ardent Cloudstriker overwhelms Perfy

beats.text: Xenadrael develops two Ardent Cloudstrikers alongside Windmill Engineer. Perfy advances through Lorraine with Inert Sword and Cheshire Cat, initially attacking the champion. Usurp the Winds turns Shifting Currents west early, sharply increasing Cloudstriker damage.

Perfy loses another Cheshire Cat to a level-up banish, clears one Cloudstriker and develops Stalwart Shieldmate. The casters discuss a possible alternative kill with another Cat, but it is not the line played. Cloudstriker cannot attack the stealthed Cat directly.

Xenadrael uses Smoke Bombs to bypass the remaining defense and presents seven attack damage, which the casters identify as exact lethal. Perfy has no answer, and Xenadrael wins game one without developing Razorgale Calling.

after.summary: Xenadrael wins — Zephyr and two Tempest Downfalls recycle for the last seven damage

beats.text: Xenadrael plays Razorgale Calling on his first turn and adds a second early, supported by Backup Charger. Kongming level one supplies the Mage class bonus for Tempest Downfall. Veiling Breeze prevents Perfy’s attacks while the two Callings add damage with each wind activation.

Perfy reaches Merlin with Dungeon Guide and holds Spirit Blade: Ascension until Xenadrael’s turn to pressure both his life and memory through Prismatic Edge. Xenadrael retrieves Veiling Breeze with Cyclical Breeze rather than committing another Calling. Perfy develops Safeguard Amulet and Crux Sight while preparing Incarnate Majesty.

After Safeguard’s prevention expires, Xenadrael sets up Zephyr and two Tempest Downfalls. Perfy responds with Blanche, but Xenadrael adds another Downfall and Scout the Land before Blanche resolves. The casters count seven remaining damage from those activations and Razorgale triggers, enough to win game two.

before.text: The casters expect Perfy to bring in everything he has after a very quick and scary first game, including the Nullifying Lantern. They discuss that Razor Gale calling would be great if a card modified the elements of the cards.

after.text: The casters discuss Nullifying Lantern before the match and expect Blanche and Safeguard Amulet for Perfy after game one. Safeguard Amulet, Crux Sight and Blanche are confirmed in game two; the complete boarding package is not shown.

before.summary: Xenadrael wins — a close game where Razor Gale triggers, Veiling Breeze and Beastbond Boots hold on and Bratus runs out of ways to deal the last six damage

beats.text: Xenadrael builds with Eternal Magistrate, which prevents things leaving the material deck in the main phase but not extra materialization. The casters say the thing to see is the Razor Gale itself, and that Xenadrael is looking at a Seiryuu's Command in Bratus's hand and arcane blasts as the danger.

Bratus plays Dungeon Guide and puts Xenadrael to 18 damage. The casters say Xenadrael's influence is too low to win this turn. A Tempest Downfall and a Cyclical Breeze fight over the same damage, and Xenadrael plays his Innervate Agility in response to the Tempest Downfall.

Xenadrael is down to two life after the Innervate Agility, so he has to win. He keeps Veiling Breeze, Beastbond Boots and Scout the Land, and every card he activates deals one damage to the Razor Gale, but the Boots prevent it. Both players are really close to death, and Bratus cannot find the last six damage. Xenadrael wins by the skin of his teeth.

before.summary: Xenadrael wins — a more convincing game where the Eternal Magistrate does not stop him this time

beats.text: Xenadrael has a better start in game two. He plays the Eternal Magistrate with the Magistrate not blocking his own plays, and draws cards with Favorable Winds. The casters say the card draw is usually the best option in this deck.

Bratus is out of gas with his Cyclical Veiling Breeze and the Baby Green Slime. The casters note the Eternal Magistrate is a timing restriction, not an effect restriction, so you can materialize something like a Grand Crusader's Ring in response. A buffed Ardent Cloudstriker arrives for Xenadrael.

Xenadrael finishes game two without shortcutting. The first Canadian winner of an Ascent in his own country takes the title, and the casters call it an amazing deck choice and fun to see a non-meta deck win. Xenadrael qualifies for Worlds in Singapore.

after.summary: Xenadrael wins — defensive wind activations keep Razorgale damage accumulating through a long first game

beats.text: Xenadrael opens with Windmill Engineer and Eternal Magistrate while searching for Razorgale Calling. Bratus develops Baby Green Slime and allies, choosing normal level-ups around Magistrate’s timing restriction. Xenadrael uses Tempest Downfall against Shimmercloak Assassin and Zephyr to interrupt Displace on Brisk Windtrotter.

After finding Razorgale, Xenadrael threatens a Tempest Downfall and Cyclical Breeze damage chain. Bratus uses Innervate Agility in response to Cyclical Breeze to survive, then transforms Seiryuu and levels back to three. Xenadrael later finds his own Innervate Agility while under heavy attack pressure.

Xenadrael uses Ventus to suppress Seiryuu, follows with Dream Fairy and keeps Veiling Breeze available. Bratus’s Beastbond Boots threaten to prevent Razorgale damage, creating a standoff over Tempest Downfall. Xenadrael levels back up for a life buffer and uses Stifling Trap to remove Shimmercloak Assassin. With Bratus reduced to one remaining damage, another wind activation closes game one.

after.summary: Xenadrael wins — Ardent Cloudstriker pressure followed by Tempest Downfall finishes the match

beats.text: Bratus starts with Beseeched Fatestone before Eternal Magistrate can interfere. Xenadrael develops Ardent Cloudstriker and reaches Kongming, preparing to attack for six with Shifting Currents pointing west. The casters prefer using Bagua to draw cards over adding buff counters to Cloudstriker.

Bratus transforms Beseeched Fatestone into a blocking threat, but Xenadrael Zephyrs it before pushing damage with Cloudstriker and Magistrate. Bratus then uses Displace on Eternal Magistrate, removing its imbued status and opening a later level-up window.
Xenadrael follows with Tempest Downfall, Cyclical Breeze and another Tempest Downfall to finish the match. He wins 2-0 and takes the Ascent Niagara Falls title.

before.text: The casters point out that the Eternal Magistrate stopped Bratus in the first game, and say Bratus plays carefully for someone who has never played the matchup. Xenadrael says in the interview that he won game one without the sideboard cards, with no Ensnaring Fumes.

after.text: The casters discuss Ensnaring Fumes, additional Eternal Magistrates and Innervate Agility for Xenadrael. In the interview, Xenadrael says he did not add the two extra Magistrates and did not see sideboard cards in game two. The full boarding package is not confirmed.

before.summary: Xelomage wins — he disables Qbone's turns and a Seiryuu's Command line finishes

beats.text: Xelomage suppresses Qbone's plays and does not need a lot of influence, which the casters call the dream of the Seiryuu deck: disabling the opponent. Lost Providence draws him a card after he opens with an awakening line.

Qbone swings in with Heavy Swing for six including the mastery. The casters count 19 with allies in play, so Harness Lightning with Seiryuu's Command is a lethal line, and both players have to decide when to send it.
Qbone is one short of lethal, but Xelomage plays it so that Qbone does not have it. Xelomage takes game one with the classic Seiryuu list.

before.summary: Xelomage wins — he plays around Qbone's Manxome Armoire and Topsy Decree and ends with a generate-empower-empower line

beats.text: Xelomage goes for an aggressive Dungeon Guide into level two. The casters say he sets up so that level three would let him combo the following turn, and the Benediction Angel he activates sets Qbone back out of range.

Qbone throws down four cards for a Heavy Swing and holds a big hand. He pops the Manxome Armoire to trade for a Topsy Decree, and a Vanish from Sight is played in response. The casters stress that the order of triggers matters and are surprised by the exact line.

Xelomage goes to Guo Jia level three and recovers three again, shrugging off all the chip damage. He finishes with a Seiryuu swing and a generate-empower-empower sequence. The casters say he drew everything and executed well, and Xelomage wins 2-0.

after.summary: Xelomage wins — Imperial Countermeasure keeps Guo Jia alive before the Harness Lightning finish

beats.text: Coverage begins partway through game one. Qbone removes Portentous Tanggu with Reduce to Ash while Xelomage keeps Seiryuu’s Command available. Qbone has Umbra’s Rite, Lost Providence and Manxome Armoire for a possible combo.
Xelomage uses Imperial Countermeasure against Qbone’s Heavy Swing. The casters calculate possible Feu Awakening lines, but Qbone holds back rather than commit to the speculative finish.
After ally chip damage, Xelomage puts Harness Lightning on Seiryuu and attacks. The dragon’s damage and an empowered Arcane Blast finish game one; the discussed Resolute Stand is not found.

after.summary: Xelomage wins — Lost Providence finds Incapacitate to stop Vanish from Sight

beats.text: Qbone opens Fluffy Shopkeep and Three of Hearts, then pressures with Heavy Swing. Xelomage levels with Dungeon Guide; Benediction Angel recovery pushes Qbone’s possible lethal lines farther away.

Xelomage’s Topsy Decree banishes the Cremation Ritual Qbone intended to omen. Qbone uses Creative Shock and later Vanish from Sight while Xelomage reaches Guo Jia level three. Qbone subsequently resolves Dungeon Guide to reach Ciel level three.

Enfeebling Orb forces Qbone to use Manxome Armoire, exchanging Topsy Decree for Vanish from Sight. In response to Vanish, Xelomage draws Incapacitate with Lost Providence and negates it. Seiryuu’s Command and Byakko’s Command then deliver repeated dragon attacks and empowered blasts for the 2–0 finish.

before.name: Xelomage
before.deck: Wind Seiryuu Guo Jia (classic Seiryuu list: Seiryuu's Command, Byakko's Command, Harness Lightning, Lost Providence, Dungeon Guide, Benediction Angel, Heavy Swing, Vanish from Sight, Topsy Decree, Regal Inquisition and Incapacitate in the side)

before.name: Qbone
before.deck: Ciel toolbox deck (Heavy Swing, Manxome Armoire, Topsy Decree, Vanish from Sight, Dungeon Guide, Incapacitate; the casters call it a toolboxy deck that loops good cards)

before.text: The casters talk through Xelomage's side. They say Regal Inquisition from the side could come in and Incapacitates may replace cards that are weak in the matchup, but the deck has few spare slots.

after.text: The casters propose Vanish from Sight and Crystallized Destiny to stop the Seiryuu finish, with Regal Inquisition another option. Vanish from Sight and Crystallized Destiny are subsequently identified in Qbone’s hand.
Resolute Stand and Incapacitate are identified after sideboarding. Incapacitate later stops Qbone’s Vanish from Sight.

changes.before: Cleaned broadcast transcript, European Nationals Day 1 VOD, Round 1 stream match. Casters call the players "Zilage/Zel Mage" (Omnidex username Xelomage) and "Cubone" (Qbone). Result per Omnidex (Xelomage 2-0). Card names are as called by the casters and may contain minor ASR errors; mid-game details were summarized from a sampled read of the captions and are partly uncertain.
changes.after: Original European Nationals Day 1 captions, 43:32–82:26. Game-one coverage starts in progress; game two is shown through the finish. Xelomage and Qbone names and the 2–0 result match the event record.

before.summary: TatPap wins — fragmented memory and sheen counters give a Ravishing Finale-sized finish

beats.text: TatPap imbues a card for free and plays Angel Attendant and an ally with three fours as base values. The casters say the idea is to get sheen counters, and he needs one more fragmented card in memory so Merlin, Brilliant Vestige gets its on-enter. He is already on seven counters in the fragments.

Ne3tra uses Frostbind on the Dungeon Guide, because TatPap pays for it but does not have quite enough influence, and a Storm of Thorns surprises TatPap. Ne3tra tries to get Magebane Lash and Saber out, but TatPap has the faster clock.
TatPap reaches eight sheen counters and plays Spirit Blade: Terminus with an attack. The casters say that is game over for Ne3tra, and TatPap takes game one.

before.summary: Ne3tra wins — Nico lash counters and an Icebound Slam deal 11 while TatPap is without his Ghosts of Pendragon

beats.text: TatPap plays the careful route because his influence dropped so low. He uses Tweedle D to remove a Dungeon Guide, which the casters say feels bad. Ne3tra knows TatPap put a Fracturize in memory but still goes for the Nullifying Mirror.

Ne3tra materializes Magebane Lash with a floating memory and stacks sheen counters for Nico. He puts five lash counters on his champion, generating six lash counters for an Icebound Slam. TatPap's two Incapacitates are gone, and Ghosts of Pendragon is in the graveyard, not in hand.

TatPap has to survive one more turn against 11 damage, which the casters think is impossible. They say that if he had the Ghosts of Pendragon that he milled he could have finished the game. Ne3tra wins game two and time runs out, so the match is a draw.

after.summary: TatPap wins — Spirit Blade: Terminus builds 46 sheen counters for Labyrinth

beats.text: Quiet Refraction and Merlin’s level-ups build sheen counters. Frostbinder Apostle removes Ne3tra’s Tweedledee, then intercepts Icebound Slam. TatPap also Fracturizes Magebane Lash.

TatPap pays for Ne3tra’s Frozen Dismissal, but Frostbind then stops Dungeon Guide’s level-up. Ne3tra’s Ravishing Finale later deals damage and mills TatPap; it is Nico’s attack, not Merlin’s finisher.
TatPap reaches Merlin level three and uses Spirit Blade: Terminus. The casters count 46 sheen counters on Fractured Memories after its hit; Labyrinth, Jeweled Opus seals game one.

after.summary: Ne3tra wins — protected Magebane Lash and Ravishing Finale leave Merlin one turn short

beats.text: TatPap opens two Quiet Refraction and levels quickly, but Ne3tra’s taunt allies slow the attacks. Ne3tra’s Tweedledee removes Dungeon Guide. Ghosts of Pendragon eventually resolves through Frozen Dismissal and helps remove a Throne-Keeper Bullfrog.

Ne3tra redirects Fracturize from Magebane Lash to Temptation’s Facade. After removing Frostbinder Apostle, Ne3tra attacks with Ravishing Finale instead of Icebound Slam; the casters count 16 damage on Merlin and 32 cards milled.

TatPap’s Luminous Quartz deals 11, but Merlin cannot survive Ne3tra’s next attack. The hoped-for Ghosts of Pendragon is milled rather than drawn. Ne3tra wins game two and there is no time for a decider.

before.summary: Asuna wins — a controlling board and Veiling Breeze keep the slimes from a kill

beats.text: sungorio puts three slimes on board and an ephemeral Liminal Guide, and Asuna keeps Veiling Breeze, Blanche and the Orb of Sealing ready. The casters say it is hard to argue with Asuna's results, and that the deck comes down to whichever side finds its pop-off.

Asuna plays a raw Dream Fairy for damage and laughs about it, then gets the Purifying Thurible out and stops sungorio from gaining influence. He uses Expel to get rid of a Stifling Trap and keeps Asuna's board up.
The casters say Asuna must find the Razor Gale to finish while sungorio looks for a kill line. Asuna controls the game and wins the first game.

before.summary: sungorio wins — an Ethereal Slime swings in for lethal and Eruption finishes with three damage

beats.text: sungorio wants a kill line and notes there are two fire slimes and several non-fire slimes in the graveyard. He uses a floating memory from a reclaim and keeps the Essence Crucible out of play.
Asuna has built up a board and controls much of what sungorio does, but may run out of options. He needs to respond to sungorio's plays to survive.
The Ethereal Slime swings in for lethal and Slime Eruption banishes the last cards in response. The three damage is dealt and game two goes to sungorio.

before.summary: sungorio wins — Cremation Ritual and Portentous Tanggu build the slime board, and Asuna finds the Veiling Breeze without enough influence

beats.text: sungorio uses Cremation Ritual to draw more cards and keeps the floating memory with a Liminal Guide in play. He counts three cards in hand, and the next turn is an easy Portentous Tanggu with a Dungeon Guide.

He hits the slimes he needs and plays seven raccoons instead of six, a change that matters for the odds. Asuna can only put down so many cards for a Veiling Breeze, and Calming Breeze together with it is not enough.
Asuna finds the Veiling Breeze but does not have enough influence for it. The round goes to sungorio on Fire Slimes, 2-1.

after.summary: Asuna wins — two Razorgales and responses around Beastbond Boots finish game one

beats.text: The broadcast joins game one with sungorio’s Baby Gray Slimes and Liminal Guide facing Asuna’s two Razorgale Callings and Essence Crucible. Asuna brews Distilled Water and pushes damage with wind activations.
Asuna uses Fairy Whispers, Veiling Breeze and Three Visits before Beastbond Boots can protect Sylvie. Further responses bring sungorio close to lethal.
sungorio survives the immediate exchange, but Asuna can respond again to the next materialization. The casters call game one for Asuna after the final response.

after.summary: sungorio wins — Slime Eruption responds to Asuna’s protector activation

beats.text: Asuna opens Dream Fairy for early pressure, then uses Purifying Thurible and develops raccoons. These plays belong to game two.
sungorio uses Gaia’s Songbird to find Ethereal Slime and keeps pushing damage instead of holding defensive cards. Asuna responds to the slime attack with recovery.
sungorio plays Slime Eruption in response to Asuna’s protector activation. Its three damage resolves for lethal and ties the match.

after.summary: sungorio wins — the Storm Slime turn overwhelms Asuna’s recovery

beats.text: Cremation Ritual and Baby Gray Slime build sungorio’s influence. Slime Eruption removes Windmill Engineer in response to Reclaim; Undeniable Truth later answers Purifying Thurible by adding cards to the graveyard.
Asuna develops a raccoon but does not play Stifling Gyre. sungorio uses Portentous Tanggu and Dungeon Guide to reach Sylvie level three, then starts a large Storm Slime turn.

Asuna tries Three Visits, Calming Breeze and recovery while digging for an answer. The final draw is Fairy Whispers; the casters say even finding Veiling Breeze now leaves too little influence. sungorio takes the match 2–1.

before.summary: Yoroi wins — negates and Engulf keep FTWwings from getting value, and Genbu's pressure finishes

beats.text: FTWwings pushes damage early, which is what you want to do against Genbu, and plays a free four-power ally that draws a card. Both players have a spell like Excalibur in hand. FTWwings tries to level to two to clear the Fatestone with a buff counter.

Yoroi strips FTWwings's hand of negates and decrees early. Another fractal puller ends in his graveyard, and FTWwings plays Calming Breeze but Yoroi's Engulf answers it, and FTWwings cannot do anything about the Engulf.
Yoroi levels, uses Prismatic Edge-proof timing and Genbu's protection, and wins game one. The casters say the deck makes it feel like you are on the losing end whatever you try.

before.summary: Yoroi wins — FTWwings cannot play his Spirit Blade: Ascension in time

beats.text: FTWwings uses Purifying Thurible to remove Yoroi's floating memory and goes to level one, which turns his material deck face up. A Gale Bind effect and a Crux Sight are shown, and he has another Gale Bind card in hand and may use Dungeon Guide.

Yoroi goes for Engulf immediately so that FTWwings gets no value from Spirit Blade: Ascension, and suppresses two Frostsworn Paladins. The casters see a possible trap if Yoroi activates Conniving Plans, but he plays carefully. The casters say Calming Breeze and the other negates do not help FTWwings.
FTWwings activates Spirit Blade: Ascension but the effect does not do enough, and Yoroi has everything he needs. The casters call it an unfortunate game two for FTWwings. Yoroi wins 2-0.

after.summary: Yoroi wins — Resonating Fugue and Genbu attack through an Engulf answer to Veiling Breeze

beats.text: FTWwings starts Benediction Angel and later Stifling Gyre while Yoroi builds a water graveyard and a buffed Tidestone Bovine. Spirit Blade: Retribution is in FTWwings’s hand but is not played.
FTWwings levels Lorraine with Dungeon Guide and attacks the Bovine. Yoroi’s Cerulean Decree reduces Lorraine’s attack, denying the clear.
Yoroi uses Resonating Fugue and Genbu’s ability to set up the finishing attack. Engulf stops FTWwings’s Veiling Breeze and game one ends.

after.summary: Yoroi wins — repeated negates leave Lorraine exposed to another Genbu finish

beats.text: FTWwings uses Veiling Breeze against Frostsworn Paladin pressure, then reaches Lorraine level three with advanced-element cards in hand.

FTWwings activates Spirit Blade: Ascension in response to Yoroi’s level-up. Yoroi answers with Engulf. Later FTWwings tries Imperious Galebind against the two Paladins, but Cerulean Decree stops that play.
With FTWwings down to one card, Yoroi flips Genbu and has Resonating Fugue for the finish. Spirit Blade: Retribution remains unplayed; Yoroi wins 2–0.

before.summary: Sebastian wins — he keeps TeamTrueCaban's influence low and always has the right answer

beats.text: Sebastian puts out Spirit of Water and uses Unbroken Mustang to clear a sensor. The casters say Sebastian knows TeamTrueCaban's deck well, so he does not worry about mysteries. He focuses on keeping his opponent's influence as low as possible and makes TeamTrueCaban work for each play.

TeamTrueCaban commits to the board and cannot interact on Sebastian's turn. He levels to Ciel level one and looks to find another Heavy Swing to start chunking damage at Diana. A Frostbind, Snow White and the Tweedle D keep Diana rested.

TeamTrueCaban went far down on influence and has one card in hand. Sebastian swings in with a loaded-up Aquamirage, with seven from the Ranger Strides and four more from Take Aim, which goes over the top of the three-damage prevention. Sebastian takes game one.

before.summary: Sebastian wins — TeamTrueCaban is always one answer short, and Ranger Strides makes Diana distant

beats.text: TeamTrueCaban plays Blade Rift Seer and an Inert Sword, with Snow White staring at Diana. He keeps the Bandit in hand and levels to Ciel to keep Diana rested so she cannot pull her ability. Sebastian has to find a way to clear the Snow White.

Sebastian glimpses for a floating memory and finds a distant enabler to set up his powerful cards. The casters say it is unacceptable for Diana to become distant, and a Ranger Strides is popped before Sebastian knows if another unique human ally is coming to turn the Tweedle D back on.

Sebastian always has the right answer and keeps pressing distant. TeamTrueCaban never gets a free turn to find the extra damage he needs, and his Heavy Swing from game one does not show up. Sebastian wins 2-0 and is in for Day 2.

after.summary: Sebastian wins — Palvor Sword and Take Aim finish through the Trappers

beats.text: TeamTrueCaban uses Palvor Sword and raccoons to pressure Sebastian and remove floating memory. Sebastian protects himself with Flash Grenade while keeping Diana distant.

The earlier Aquamirage Whisper attack is not lethal, so Sebastian holds Take Aim. On the following turn, Frostsworn Paladin draws out prevention and Diana attacks with Palvor Sword and Take Aim to win.

after.summary: Sebastian wins — a loaded Archer attack and Palvor Sword close game two

beats.text: TeamTrueCaban uses Snow White to keep Diana rested, and combines allies to clear Frostsworn Paladin. Later Frostbind stops Backstep, forcing Sebastian to find another distant enabler.

Tactical Retreat makes Diana distant and enables Flash Grenade. Sebastian later brings out Ranger Strides, uses Fracturize on Inert Sword, and combines Take Aim with the Archer attack; the following Palvor Sword swing is lethal.

before.summary: PewPewStan wins — MaruX concedes at 27 damage

beats.text: MaruX opens with a hand that is hard to use: the casters say it is a choice between holding a whole hand of good cards or leveling. He draws many cards with Creative Shock to look for Dungeon Guide, and has Clarent, Reimagined on the board to protect his allies.

PewPewStan plays cautiously and uses Imperious Galebind, a Dream Fairy that goes the distance every time, and a Corhazi insignia for preparation counters so Striking Illuminance can deal real damage. Ayella suppresses MaruX's Prismatic Edge. The casters say the deck with the draw-focused start has a big advantage in this matchup.

PewPewStan finds Striking Illuminance and double Lightweaver's Assault, plus a Regal Inquisition, while MaruX has Lorraine, Spirit Ruler and a Prismatic Edge out. A rules question about the Drawn Blade that Sabella put into play is explained to the players.

before.summary: Draw — time expires

beats.text: MaruX takes the first turn and baits out the Purifying Thurible. He plays Sword of Seeking, which had been replaced by the distortion versions for a while, and a Gentle Respite comes down for PewPewStan to get influence. There are no more preparation counters for MaruX.

MaruX plays Aesan Protector for three and follows up with Spirit Blade: Ascension. He uses a Clarent instead of the Sword of Seeking to kill the Dungeon Guide. PewPewStan keeps Resolute Stand, Vanish from Sight and two Luxem Sights in hand.

Ghosts of Pendragon and a second Ghosts of Pendragon in MaruX's hand build a big board, but it is MaruX's last turn in the overtime procedure. PewPewStan needs 27 damage on his final turn while at Zander and cannot get there. Time is called; the recorded match result is a draw. The casters say that one more turn for MaruX would have made a huge difference.

after.summary: PewPewStan wins — MaruX concedes at 27 damage

beats.text: A judge review concerns Drawn Blade remaining after the Sabella that brought it into play has left. Play resumes with Drawn Blade moved to banishment.

PewPewStan’s Regal Inquisition had removed important draw cards from MaruX. After play resumes, Uncover the Plot finds a Luxem Sight reveal and PewPewStan follows with Striking Illuminance. MaruX reaches 27 damage and concedes.

after.summary: MaruX wins — Pendragon and Aesan Protector overwhelm the recovery

beats.text: MaruX repeatedly uses Prismatic Edge to attack PewPewStan’s memory. Spirit Blade: Ascension produces another reveal that banishes a Luxem Sight, reducing PewPewStan’s recovery engine.

MaruX builds three Ghosts of Pendragon, two Aesan Protectors and Numinous Monk. The attacks continue, and PewPewStan concedes. The casters explicitly announce game two to MaruX and a tied match before the players shuffle for game three.

after.summary: Draw — neither player finishes during overtime

beats.text: Angelic Channeling helps MaruX develop his hand. On his final overtime turn, Dungeon Guide takes Lorraine to level three; successive Ghosts of Pendragon add bodies, cards and damage.

PewPewStan starts his final overtime turn needing 27 damage. He uses Dungeon Guide to reach Zander level three, but the game ends without a winner. The broadcast announces a drawn match and both players moving to 4–2–1.

before.summary: Noel wins — she survives the burn plan with Pearl Prayer and Regenerate and finishes through Regal Inquisition and Cerulean Decree

beats.text: DjieDjoen reaches Jin level three and clears the Frostsworn Paladin. He plans to draw with Lost Providence and to activate Backup Charger for Berserker's Blade. The casters say Diana has only 19 life, so he does not need many damage counters for an enraged lethal.

Noel is very durable. Pearl Prayer and Regenerate replace themselves and recover six damage, and Relentless Outburst is only a board clear because Noel can go distant. A Cerulean Decree, mistaken for an Undercurrent Vantage by the casters, stops a big swing.

DjieDjoen swings with a plus two, plus four attack for 19 and tries not to overkill. Noel has all her influence left. Because DjieDjoen cast Regal Inquisition before anything else, Noel puts the damage counters on him perfectly and wins game one.

before.summary: Noel wins — Song of Frost and the queens on her board frustrate DjieDjoen, and a Krustallan Archer swings for the win

beats.text: Noel sideboards the Songs of Frost and Thronekeeper Bullfrogs, and plays Cheshire Cat as an ally that puts on pressure. The casters note the contrast with game one, where Noel tried to survive without dealing too much damage.
The queens on Noel's board are very annoying to deal with, and DjieDjoen's frustration is visible. A Krustallan Archer swings in for four and another attack for eight, and Noel wins the round 2-0.

after.summary: Noel wins — taxation and Fracturize stop Jin’s attempted counterattack

beats.text: DjieDjoen uses recovery to keep Jin alive while Noel builds pressure. Regenerate and Transfusive Aura belong to Jin’s plan, not Noel’s.

After a large attack, Noel taxes DjieDjoen’s Regal Inquisition with Cerulean Decree and Frostbind, then Fracturizes Jin’s weapon. DjieDjoen cannot assemble the finishing attack or enough Relentless Outburst damage and concedes.

after.summary: Noel wins — consecutive Snow Whites lock Jin out of leveling

beats.text: Noel finds both Snow Whites. The first keeps Jin rested and unable to level; Archer pressure and Cheshire Cat continue while the second Snow White is held ready.
Ranger Strides pushes the Archer attack to 12. DjieDjoen releases the spirit to survive but loses access to water cards while still locked out of leveling. Noel wins the match 2–0.

before.summary: shokoouo wins — Carter, Angel Attendant and the Manxome Armoire engine bury baniRien, who concedes

beats.text: shokoouo uses Surveil Possessions mastery and Angelic Channeling to banish a strength card and a Carter. The casters say Angel Attendant punishes any first attack from an Aetherwing, which has to waste a turn or wait for the Inert Sword. He has Resolute Stand and a stacked hand.

baniRien has a Cerulean Decree for minus three and a negate, and the casters note a cursed strength that cannot be negated will deal four damage. Carter and the Liminal Guide come out and he runs low on cards.
shokoouo gets another omen at the end of the turn and has three cards in hand, so he can use the Manxome Armoire and do it again. baniRien knows it and concedes game one.

before.summary: baniRien wins — a conservative Snow White with an aggressive ally on the board is the key

beats.text: baniRien uses Weaving Manastream greedily at the cost of the Crystallized Destiny, and Shokoouo throws down Creative Shock instead of being greedy. baniRien finds the Quickstep Treads and a floating memory, and is in a good position.

baniRien plays Snow White with an aggressive ally on board and stays conservative. shokoouo is made to discard and banish two cards from his graveyard, and a Liminal Guide hit by a banish is one less draw.
The casters say the Snow White with the aggressive ally was the key to the victory and the score is 1-1 with 22 minutes on the clock.

before.summary: baniRien wins — distant enablers and Aetherwing chargers beat a greedy shokoouo

beats.text: shokoouo goes for the greedy route and wants the Liminal Guide he has in hand into the graveyard. The casters say he leveled up with a plus-one Dungeon Guide and the mastery of the Ciel deck makes it beautiful to play.

baniRien plays Backup Charger to keep up influence and bullies shokoouo. The casters like that all his distant enablers either draw a card or are floating memory, and he has more Aether chargers than distant enablers. Mirage's Grave and Crystallized Destiny are difficult for shokoouo with only three cards in hand.

baniRien's four new cards include three floating memories, and a Resolute Stand with a tax question is explained. The casters count nine blocked and an 18-damage attack, which is game over for shokoouo, who needs the awakening to win and cannot find it. baniRien wins 2-1.

after.summary: shokoouo wins — Feu Awakening and Accursed Strength set up another Armoire loop

beats.text: shokoouo develops Carter and uses Accursed Strength with Feu Awakening. The sequence refills the hand after Feu Awakening and builds more omens.
With another Feu Awakening available through Manxome Armoire, baniRien concedes game one.

after.summary: baniRien wins — Snow White locks Ciel down while the Archers attack

beats.text: baniRien waits to combine Snow White with Krustallan Archer pressure. shokoouo uses Manxome Armoire to recover Topsy Decree, but the denial does not stop the attacks.
Ranger Strides and Archer attacks force shokoouo to release the spirit. Without the needed Dungeon Guide on the next turn, shokoouo loses game two.

after.summary: baniRien wins — sustained ranged pressure survives the final Resolute Stand

beats.text: shokoouo uses Regal Inquisition while baniRien keeps distant enablers and Cheshire Cat lines available. Quickstep Treads complicates the Crystallized Destiny defense, but Resolute Stand still prevents part of the large attack.
The match enters overtime with shokoouo still short of a finishing line. baniRien uses Backstep and Frostsworn Paladin threatens the final damage, taking the match 2–1.

before.summary: Xelomage wins — a double Byakko's Command turn and Ayella suppression carry the dragon through Sebastian's Imperial Countermeasures surprise

beats.text: Sebastian flips Spirit of Water and puts out a Looking Glass, and the casters say that with Diana you know what you are up against. A forest cake gives Xelomage a cycle and a draw, and Sebastian deals three damage with a swing.

Xelomage goes for the aggressive play, banishing his level-up cards carefully. A double Byakko's Command turn flips the dragon, and Ayella gives him a free suppress on the forest cake. He holds the Lost Providence and Incandescent Reliquary to extract as much as he can.
Sebastian is surprised by Imperial Countermeasures preventing his damage. Sebastian cannot get enough through, and Xelomage wins game one with the Seiryuu.

before.summary: Sebastian wins — he gets a fast Frostsworn Paladin start and Frostbind with Cerulean Decree stops the dragon

beats.text: Sebastian goes first with Quickstep Treads on a distant Diana. The casters note a skill check: when Resolute Stand can exist in the list, he must double-load the Aetherwing on turn two so it hits. Xelomage does not have an end-of-turn Angelic Channeling to get Dungeon Guide to three.

Xelomage holds Displace and asks when to flip the dragon. Sebastian plays the game slowly with a four-damage weapon from three Aether charges, and distant Diana forces Xelomage's hand. The casters say that when Diana is distant, the Treads can be ignored.
Sebastian has a Cerulean Decree and a Frostbind in hand and plays both. The Besiege the Winds is banished, which scoops the dragon plan, and game two goes to Sebastian.

before.summary: Sebastian wins — a fast Frostsworn Paladin start and Ranger Strides make the lethal before Xelomage can flip his dragon

beats.text: Xelomage has a hand with a Dungeon Guide and a Benediction Angel and besieges to one, but the casters say he needs a nice opener and cannot find the Auspicious Manifestation he needs. He reaches six quest counters and draws, taking the counters.

Sebastian plays the Frostsworn Paladins and Krustallan Archers to deal steady damage. The casters note he has nothing to sideboard while Xelomage had a lot, and that Xelomage's sideboarding might have taken his power level back.

Sebastian hits the floating memory with Diana and uses Ranger Strides for a 12-damage swing: at 19 damage with a five heal it is still lethal. The casters say it was way too fast, and a pause follows while the judges confirm the play. Sebastian wins 2-1.

after.summary: Xelomage wins — Imperial Countermeasure saves the dragon

beats.text: Aella repeatedly suppresses attackers while Xelomage holds further commands. Sebastian removes Aella and lines up a large attack at Seiryuu with Cheshire Cat and Ranger Strides.
Xelomage uses Lost Providence to afford Imperial Countermeasure through Quickstep Treads. The protected dragon survives and Sebastian concedes game one.

after.summary: Sebastian wins — successive negates keep Seiryuu from entering play

beats.text: Sebastian’s Frozen Dismissal stops Dungeon Guide while Diana maintains pressure and a large hand.
Xelomage then attempts Beseech the Winds, but Cerulean Decree and Frostbind stop it. Xelomage concedes without getting the dragon online.

after.summary: Sebastian wins — Archer pressure outpaces the delayed dragon

beats.text: Two Krustallan Archers pressure Guo Jia while Frostbind taxes Xelomage’s Windmill Engineer setup. Sebastian brings out Ranger Strides and prepares the final attacks.
Innervate Agility reduces Xelomage’s level and recovers damage, but also lowers the champion’s life total. Sebastian’s remaining damage is enough to take the match 2–1.

before.summary: Horinti wins — Heavy Swing pressure and a second Dwaying clear CasuaL's Aella and his Krux plan

beats.text: CasuaL's Lorraine list is very different from the usual one. He gets the Drawn Blade and Pallor Sword out with Lorraine, Spirit Ruler. The casters say Horinti's deck puts threats on board while squeezing the opponent's influence, and that Snow White prevents prevention.

Horinti uses Fairy Whispers and Displace to keep Ayella safe and plays Sabella, which can bring the Drawn Blade out if banished again. The second Dwaying swings into Ayella and takes it out, putting CasuaL in a dicey position.

CasuaL turns the Drawn Blade into a Prismatic Edge to clear some of the board, which disables the Dwaying unless Horinti finds another unique human ally. The casters say CasuaL has more cards available than expected, but Horinti takes the first game.

before.summary: Horinti wins — Heavy Swing, an interceptor in response and the Manxome Armoire loop finish a fast game

beats.text: CasuaL takes the first turn and passes entirely down. The casters say Horinti goes to level one, hits with Heavy Swing for six and then for seven with an omen, and that this is big pressure.

Horinti cannot redirect the Heavy Swing, but in response he plays the Rose, so an interceptor is in play when the swing resolves. CasuaL uses Spirit Blade: Ascension on the Sword of Seeking into the Prismatic Edge and plays Queen Cinder Hog for three damage.

Horinti gets out the Manxome Armoire and sets up to return Heavy Swing to hand after attacking. CasuaL's hand is entirely down, and Horinti wins game two and the round to be one win from the Top 8. The casters say it was very quick.

after.summary: Horinti wins — ally pressure and removal of Aella force a concession

beats.text: CasuaL tries to stabilize with Aella against Horinti’s wide board. Frostbind prevents Aella’s extra suppression value, and a second Jueying removes her.
Spirit Blade: Ascension produces Prismatic Edge and some card value, but CasuaL cannot recover enough board control and concedes.

after.summary: Horinti wins — a bricked Lorraine hand cannot survive the Armoire follow-up

beats.text: CasuaL struggles to develop, using Purifying Thurible to put cards in memory for leveling. Rose intercepts the first Heavy Swing, keeping Lorraine alive temporarily.
Enfeebling Orb and Frostbind shut down CasuaL’s Ghosts of Pendragon. With CasuaL’s hand down, Horinti uses Manxome Armoire to retrieve Heavy Swing and wins.

before.summary: Noel wins — Unbroken Mustang and a fast influence start beat a Hanky hand that lacks an Aetherwing

beats.text: Noel goes first, and the casters say whoever goes first has the advantage in the mirror. He does not level up and has no distant enabler, so he goes for Backup Charger, and HenkieTheGoat does have the enabler. Noel keeps Tactical Retreat in hand in a mirror, so he does not take damage from the Aetherwing.

HenkieTheGoat needs two Frozen Dismissals to stop Noel, who has six cards in hand, and cannot find them. The casters say his hand without an Aetherwing in play is not very good, but with an Aetherwing it would have been amazing, with Charge the Soul and a couple of other Aether charges.

Noel pops the Flash Grenade to prevent the damage from distant units and plays Quickstep Treads and Fracturize. The casters say the Unbroken Mustang was the key to victory, because it got rid of the Aquamirage Whisper early. Noel takes game one.

before.summary: Noel wins — a sacrifice swing for one more than lethal beats HenkieTheGoat's tight Cerulean Decree hand

beats.text: Noel plays a Cheshire Cat, with Charge the Soul loaded into the Aquamirage Whisper, and Krustallan Archer for four damage and a card. The casters say Snow White could lock the Diana champion for a turn, but Noel goes for tempo. A shuffle mix-up on glimpsed cards is caught and fixed immediately.

HenkieTheGoat leans back and stays relaxed. He holds a couple of Cerulean Decrees, but a Cerulean Decree costs one more than he has to keep a Frozen Dismissal up. The casters count that two Aether charges, being distant, the Whisper and Ranger Strides add up to a lethal amount.

Noel writes a 20 on his notepad and sacrifices a unit and the cat to swing for one over lethal, with the Flash Grenade ready. HenkieTheGoat cannot pay for multiple negates, and Noel wins the match 2-0 and moves into the Top 8.

after.summary: Noel wins — Mustang pressure and a final ranged attack close game one

beats.text: Noel’s Unbroken Mustang removes Aquamirage Whisper and adds repeated chip damage. Late in the game, Backstep draws into Frozen Dismissal to stop HenkieTheGoat’s Frostsworn Paladin.
Charge the Soul adds damage and loads Aquamirage Whisper. Noel sacrifices Cheshire Cat to boost Diana’s attack and wins game one.

after.summary: Noel wins — Krustallan Archer finishes after Refreshing Charge prevents the first lethal

beats.text: Noel sacrifices Ranger Strides and Cheshire Cat for a large attack while Quickstep Treads taxes HenkieTheGoat’s responses. Refreshing Charge keeps him alive through that attack.
Noel digs past the top cards and finds Krustallan Archer for the remaining damage. HenkieTheGoat concedes the match 0–2.

before.summary: KidDelicious wins — Purse, Ranger Strides and Evasive Maneuvers swing through Asuna's Veiling Breeze

beats.text: The casters think the Wake Up deck has the favor in the matchup. KidDelicious plays a Backup Charger for a power cell, a Tariff Ring and a Purse that can protect anything on the board. Asuna plays Veiling Breeze early and respectfully.

KidDelicious puts four damage counters on Asuna's Razor Gale-level champion and threatens a distant swing for eight after the next aim counter. With a double Ranger Strides, sacrificing the Cheshire Cat, he can swing for ten. Asuna's Veiling Breeze prevents four.

Asuna needs 11 damage through four prevented, and the casters note that an Evasive Maneuvers on the swing with Purse and Ranger Strides makes the numbers work. KidDelicious wins a tight, back-and-forth game one.

before.summary: Asuna wins — Razor Gale triggers on every wind activation, and the Nullifying Mirror stops the held Veiling Breeze

beats.text: Asuna has no influence generation without a turn-one Razor Gale and works to get the herbs off the boards. He sees the Distilled Waters and goes for the damage play. Scout the Land digs for the second Razor Gale.

KidDelicious has everything on board for a 20-damage swing from one Purse if it all goes through. Asuna still has a Razor Gale in play and deals damage with every wind activation. A Wind Resonance Bauble comes out for KidDelicious.

Asuna deals his damage before recollecting, and KidDelicious is left with exactly two cards in hand. The Nullifying Mirror will negate any held Veiling Breeze, and Asuna has two fast-speed wind cards in hand, one too many for KidDelicious to answer. The match goes to game three.

before.summary: Asuna wins — a long game decided by a missed trigger and a deck-cut ruling, with the Razor Gale finishing

beats.text: KidDelicious brings back a Windmill Engineer and builds a wide board, but the casters say the board is vulnerable. Asuna has not found a Dream Fairy and has a second Scatter Essence, and the Tempest Downfall in the side forces KidDelicious to protect Purse.

KidDelicious plays Second Wind and wakes up, and Asuna has only 15 life. He plays the Three Visits pre-recollection, which denies some damage. A gather trigger is missed when Asuna moves into the main phase, and the casters say it is gone.

Asuna hopes for a second Razor Gale. An extra-cards penalty is checked when Asuna cuts the deck, and both players become a little tilted from missed interactions. Asuna digs for the cyclical Veiling Breeze and finishes the game and the match, 2-1.

after.summary: KidDelicious wins — Perse attacks through the last Veiling Breeze

beats.text: Asuna uses Zephyr and Veiling Breeze while Razorgale damage leaves KidDelicious close to defeat.
KidDelicious attacks with Perse, Ranger Strides and Evasive Maneuvers. The casters revise their damage calculation as Asuna concedes; the precise lethal arithmetic is unclear in captions.

after.summary: Asuna wins — repeated wind activations force the last defensive response

beats.text: Asuna uses successive Veiling Breezes for Razorgale damage and materializes Nullifying Mirror to constrain KidDelicious’s held Veiling Breeze.
With two fast wind cards available, Asuna can answer the final defensive play. The exchange ends in Asuna’s favor, sending the match to game three.

after.summary: Asuna wins — two Windmill Engineers and Tempest Downfall close the long decider

beats.text: The broadcast discusses a missed Arisanna gather trigger, and later a Skirting Step draw and deck correction. These are caster accounts; the exact formal penalties are not established in the captions.

With KidDelicious’s hand down, Asuna digs with Fairy Whispers and finds Tempest Downfall. Two Windmill Engineers plus Tempest Downfall deal the last damage; the finish is an attacking line rather than Razorgale.

before.summary: Sebastian wins — a tactical retreat and a distant swing for seven finish a TeamTrueCaban who has lost his strong resources early

beats.text: Sebastian puts the Inert Sword out, which tells the casters a Cheshire Cat is on the way. TeamTrueCaban has a Dwaying in hand but needs a unique water human ally to turn it on. Sebastian uses Tactical Retreat to end combat, take no damage, set up a float and go distant.

TeamTrueCaban uses Storm of Thorns on a Frostsworn Paladin, but his floating memory is not enough. The casters say Sebastian, who made five misplays in a row in an earlier match, keeps the Fracturize for Quickstep Treads or Ranger Strides.

TeamTrueCaban holds a Frostbind but would have to put down his whole hand to use it. Sebastian fires off a distant attack: three from the Paladin and two from the game, plus two for distance, is seven and lethal. Sebastian takes game one.

before.summary: TeamTrueCaban wins — a Wraith Guard wall and a wide ally board win the war of attrition

beats.text: TeamTrueCaban thinks for a long time on the first turn about two or three turns ahead, so that he is not stopped as hard as in game one. He plays a Sensor and a Backup Charger for a power cell, and the one Fracturize in hand gives a floating memory for the level up.

Sebastian brings in Fracturize and the Drown Aether, and the casters say he keeps drawing cards that are good for the matchup. TeamTrueCaban resolves the Unyielding Wraithguard, and Sebastian has only two cards left in hand and cannot Frostbind it.

TeamTrueCaban builds a huge, wide board protected by other allies and keeps turning allies sideways. Sebastian's counters run out of steam, and the casters say having three Weaving Manastreams in the top nine cards is not what Sebastian needs. TeamTrueCaban ties the match 1-1.

before.summary: TeamTrueCaban wins — he wears out every Frozen Dismissal and a Freezing Hail finishes

beats.text: Sebastian passes his first turn and TeamTrueCaban develops a Corhazi Trapper. TeamTrueCaban's Frostbind banishes Sebastian's Refreshing Charge, which denies a float and forces Sebastian to commit two more Aether charges to attack with Diana.

TeamTrueCaban's Snow White rests the Diana so she cannot attack, and Sebastian has to play something. Sebastian plays Fracturize in response, which removes the Inert Sword line, and he holds a Nullifying Mirror in a board state that is hard for TeamTrueCaban.

TeamTrueCaban keeps wearing out Sebastian's negates until Sebastian has no Frozen Dismissal. A Nia hits the board and turns on the Dwaying, and a Freezing Hail from the top of the deck gives the lethal attempt. TeamTrueCaban wins and advances to the final, which locks his slot for Worlds. The casters call it a true war of attrition.

after.summary: Sebastian wins — Take Aim on a distant Frostsworn Paladin finishes

beats.text: Backstep and Flash Grenade preserve Sebastian’s Frostsworn Paladin from Ciel’s Inert Sword. Quickstep Treads then taxes TeamTrueCaban’s remaining responses.
Sebastian plays Take Aim on the distant Frostsworn Paladin and its attack is lethal. The finisher is the Paladin, not a Diana weapon swing.

after.summary: TeamTrueCaban wins — Wraith Guard and Paladin protect a wide board

beats.text: Unyielding Wraithguard and a held-back Frostsworn Paladin prevent Sebastian from reaching Ciel while TeamTrueCaban keeps attacking with the rest of the board.
Sebastian cannot break the defensive board and concedes, tying the match.

after.summary: TeamTrueCaban wins — Freezing Hail supplies the last damage

beats.text: TeamTrueCaban keeps deploying allies and exhausting Sebastian’s negates. The final attacks bring Diana to 18 damage while Ciel remains behind Unyielding Wraithguard.
Freezing Hail finishes Sebastian during the next turn’s exchange. TeamTrueCaban advances to the final and secures a Worlds place.

before.summary: TheRainGoddess wins — he is behind for the first half, then Ghosts of Pendragon, Spirit Blade: Ascension and Prismatic Edge turn the game

beats.text: TeamTrueCaban opens with Fluffy Shopkeep and a Windmill Engineer line and Nia, Mistveiled Scout names Lorraine, Blademaster, so Lorraine cannot level on time. The casters say no Wind Krux deck has levelled to Lorraine as its first materialization all weekend, and that TheRainGoddess must find a way to stop the early pressure.

TheRainGoddess uses Calming Breeze as his only saving grace and plays Gale Bind with an Exalted Heart. A Nullifying Mirror turns off the elements in his memory, but he builds a strong hand with Lost Providence and Spirit Blade: Ascension, and the casters say the odds flip back to him.

TeamTrueCaban plays a Frostsworn Paladin to remove the Ghosts of Pendragon, and TheRainGoddess finds an Ascension that returns Prismatic Edge to the material deck and draws two more. The casters call the top-deck backbreaking. TeamTrueCaban has no hand left, and TheRainGoddess deploys five damage and swings in.

before.summary: TheRainGoddess wins — a long, careful game where Ghosts of Pendragon finally arrive and Spirit Blade: Ascension finishes the fight

beats.text: TheRainGoddess goes second and draws the extra card. He plays Aesan Protector to bring back his Dream Fairy and keeps pressure on a TeamTrueCaban hand that is not what he wanted. The casters note that TeamTrueCaban notes down the cards to play around, and that he has only one Frostsworn Paladin, a Cheshire Cat and a few other two-three allies.

TeamTrueCaban plays Nia first and then the swing, which plays around the Storm of Thorns. The Tweedle D and his Extricating Touch let him see TheRainGoddess's memory, and TheRainGoddess holds two Spirit Blade: Ascensions and keeps the third in memory. The casters say TheRainGoddess has not found a Ghost of Pendragon all game.

TeamTrueCaban's relentless attacks, Frozen Dismissal and Song of Frost from the side keep TheRainGoddess on the back foot. The casters say Frozen Dismissal should have been held up and note TheRainGoddess is down to a single hope: a Spirit Blade: Retribution that puts the whole graveyard in banishment.

TheRainGoddess plays Ghosts of Pendragon, which returns a sword and draws two, and finds Cruxite and a fire card. TeamTrueCaban plays every out, but TheRainGoddess finds the damage and wins 2-0. In the interview he says he tested every deck and did not expect to make the quarterfinals.

after.summary: TheRainGoddess wins — repeated Prismatic Edge entries reverse the board, then allies finish

beats.text: TeamTrueCaban sends Frostsworn Paladin into Ghosts of Pendragon. TheRainGoddess uses Displace to return the Ghosts, recycle Prismatic Edge and draw two. Snow White prevents Lorraine from attacking, and TeamTrueCaban removes the Ghosts afterward.

With TeamTrueCaban’s hand committed, TheRainGoddess draws the fire card needed to combine all three Prismatic Edge effects. Repeated Spirit Blade: Ascension entries deal champion damage, remove cards from memory and refill the hand; Crux Sight retrieves another Ascension.
TeamTrueCaban has five life left after the Prismatic Edge sequence. Ghosts of Pendragon attacks for three and Aella attacks for two to finish, while Lorraine remains unable to attack.

after.summary: TheRainGoddess wins — suppressing Nullifying Mirror opens the final Prismatic Edge trigger

beats.text: TeamTrueCaban cannot force a finish through TheRainGoddess’s defense and keeps Frozen Dismissal and Song of Frost available.

At the end of TeamTrueCaban’s turn, Aella suppresses Nullifying Mirror. Displace and Reclaim reuse Ghosts of Pendragon, and further Ghosts draw into Crux Sight as TheRainGoddess builds the closing attack.
TeamTrueCaban reaches one remaining life. Prismatic Edge returns at the end step before the suppressed Mirror, reveals a fire card and deals the final three damage.

before.summary: Lifdrasyl wins — he reaches Zander level three through Noel's taxes and wins the damage race

beats.text: Noel has the first turn as the higher seed and goes for Sense of Restful Peace to disable abilities. Lifdrasyl has to banish Flagrant Guide to level up, which makes his turn awkward with the Vanitas tax on materialization.

Lifdrasyl plays Windmill Engineer and uses the draw to build influence, then Sadi and a Purifying Thurible for card flow. A missed Death Executioner trigger is ruled on and the casters note it is a card that is often missed in the heat of play.

Lifdrasyl reaches level three with seven influence even after paying all the taxes and plays Blinding Steel. Noel's damage is not unpreventable and the pressure comes too late. The casters say that getting the horse out earlier might have won Noel the damage race.

before.summary: Noel wins — Vanitas, Shizun of the Ash and a Poisoned Dagger swing the damage race back

beats.text: Noel goes first and plays carefully while Shizun of the Ash and the new Radiant Origins card enter. A game-state problem on a materialization is fixed by the media team and the judges, and the casters ask the players to stop touching memory.

Lifdrasyl finds a Serro operative and a Nullifying Mirror, and sits on six influence with a hand full of allies and Lightweaver's Assaults. He has an Incapacitate and a Dream Fairy, and he responds to everything Noel does.

Noel takes damage in a back-and-forth race: Lifdrasyl deals 19 damage and the pendulum swings every turn. Noel's Vanitas swings with a strong Brisk Windtrotter, and a Searing Rebuke and Poisoned Dagger line gives her the win.

before.summary: Lifdrasyl wins — surveil lines find Slice and Dice and the lethal damage through Noel's Searing Rebuke

beats.text: Noel levels to Vanitas one and puts all her faith in the top of her deck. The casters count eight guides and two Beseeches, and she brings Sadi back to the board and takes out an ally.

Lifdrasyl keeps a couple of cards in hand and replays Fluffy Shopkeep as an interceptor. His surveil lines dig deeper, and he loses an Ensnaring Fumes but sits on a solid memory. Vanitas does not connect, so there is no taxation and Noel's Poisoned Dagger comes out for free.

Lifdrasyl has the influence advantage and bullies Noel. His attacks push through 11 damage, and Slice and Dice closes the game as Noel's Searing Rebuke cannot stop it. Lifdrasyl moves to the semifinals.

after.summary: Lifdrasyl wins — Zander reaches level 3 and removes Noel’s board, prompting a concession

beats.text: Dungeon Guide allows Lifdrasyl to reach Zander, Blinding Steel through Vanitas’s taxes. The casters identify a missed Death Executioner trigger during the sequence.

Noel uses Searing Rebuke on a Dungeon Guide attack, but Lifdrasyl Reclaims the attacker so the combat does not occur. Two Lightweaver’s Assaults then remove Dilu, leaving Noel without the pressure needed to overcome Luxem Sight healing.
Noel concedes after Lifdrasyl establishes level 3 with a large influence advantage. The game ends before a damaging finishing sequence is played.

after.summary: Noel wins — growing allies overwhelm repeated Luxem Sight healing

beats.text: Noel uses Searing Rebuke with Impact Hammer’s self-damage, then attacks with Vanitas. Lifdrasyl allows the Rebuke to resolve, and the attack pushes Zander to 22 damage before the next healing cycle.

Brisk Windtrotter buffs and Beastsoul Visage make Noel’s allies difficult to clear. Lifdrasyl uses Lightweaver’s Assault defensively to heal and remove Dilu, but Red Hare, Lava Soul Tiger and Vanitas keep the pressure high.

Calming Breeze stops the wind-element Dilu, but Noel still has fire damage available. Lifdrasyl digs with Luxem Sight and Fairy Whispers, finds another Assault too late to afford the defense, and Noel’s final attack wins.

after.summary: Lifdrasyl wins — Incapacitate stops Searing Rebuke and Slice and Dice closes

beats.text: Calming Breeze prevents Vanitas’s attack from connecting, so Lifdrasyl avoids the next materialization tax. Backup Charger puts Luxem cards into memory, and the reveal damage removes both Brisk Windtrotters.
Noel builds a large Dream Fairy with Beastsoul Visage and keeps Searing Rebuke for the counterattack. Lifdrasyl finds Slice and Dice and prepares the finishing turn.
Lifdrasyl attacks with Poisoned Dagger. Noel responds with Searing Rebuke, but Incapacitate stops it; Slice and Dice follows and wins the match.

before.summary: Zero0000000000 wins — Ghosts of Pendragon and a row of Windmill Engineers deal lethal before Asuna reaches level three

beats.text: Asuna surprises the casters with an Oblation Ciel pivot built to return Baleful Oblation to the top of his deck once he reaches level three. Zero0000000000 starts with Drawn Blade into banishment, which the casters call very important because Lorraine, Spirit Ruler needs it to get a sword back.

Zero0000000000 uses Spirit Blade: Ascension to deny Asuna's level-up cards and brings out Prismatic Edge with Sword of Seeking. Asuna has no Dungeon Guide to help, so leveling puts only two cards in memory and Ascension can banish one of them.
Zero0000000000 pushes in every ally, with Windmill Engineers back to back, and takes Asuna to 30 damage counters. The Ghosts of Pendragon deal lethal, and Zero0000000000 goes 1-0 up.

before.summary: Zero0000000000 wins — Asuna is shut out of every element and never levels

beats.text: Asuna uses Angelic Channeling and Library Witch to find cards. The casters say Zero0000000000 will not let Asuna find an answer. Zero0000000000 plays Lorraine, Spirit Ruler and Drawn Blade, and keeps the Ghosts of Pendragon in reserve.

Zero0000000000 taps the Nullifying Mirror so Asuna cannot use his spirit cards, and uses Lost Providence to refill. Asuna keeps four Baleful Oblations in hand but cannot reach level three and play them, and he is shut out of wind, water and fire.

Zero0000000000 plays with correct materializations and holds up durable and Ascension. Asuna's Liminal Guide does one point of damage and the Library Witch is not enough. Zero0000000000 wins 2-0 and reaches the semifinals.

after.summary: Zero0000000000 wins — Asuna reaches level 3 with too few resources to stop the allies

beats.text: Asuna uses Nullifying Mirror and Gentle Respite to protect the level-up. Zero removes floating memory with Purifying Thurible, but Asuna still reaches level 3 and returns Baleful Oblation to the top of the deck.

Zero attacks with Dungeon Guide, Windmill Engineers and Ghosts of Pendragon while Asuna has only a small hand. Aesan Protector returns the Ghosts, allowing another three-damage attacker to enter and close the game.

after.summary: Zero0000000000 wins — a late Ascension stops Asuna’s level-up and prompts a concession

beats.text: Asuna reaches Ciel, Loyal Valet but struggles to cycle a hand containing four Feu Awakenings. Asuna’s Nullifying Mirror delays Zero’s Ascension plays while the ally board continues dealing damage.
Dungeon Guide, Aella and Ghosts of Pendragon keep Asuna under pressure. Asuna finds Creative Shock and attempts to reach level 3.

Zero uses suppression and resolves Spirit Blade: Ascension in response to the Mirror activation, removing a card from memory. Asuna cannot complete the level-up without finding additional floating memory and concedes.

before.summary: Jett wins — a free Zander level-up with Blinding Steel and a Lightweaver's Assault line beat GlenyBoi's greedy Pendragon turn

beats.text: GlenyBoi opens with Dungeon Guide and Aesan Protector, the high-pressure start a Wind Krux deck needs. Jett keeps Ensnaring Fumes and Veiling Breeze, and the casters note he has Heavenly Guide to re-use.

Jett plays Stifling Gyre naming Ghosts of Pendragon, making GlenyBoi pay four extra cards to resolve its on-enter draw. GlenyBoi levels to Lorraine, Wandering Warrior and brings out Sword of Seeking; Verdigris Decree is his potential answer to the Gyre.

GlenyBoi uses Imperious Galebind to take the Lost Providence, the Poisoned Dagger and the Drawn Blade, and has three Ghosts of Pendragon to play for nine damage. He then plays Prismatic Edge instead of Clarent, Reimagined, which the casters call a little too greedy.
Jett suppresses the Ghosts and calms the damage with Calming Breeze. His Poisoned Dagger for one and a revealed Lightweaver's Assault deal eight damage to the face, and Jett wins game one.

before.summary: Jett wins — a Veiling Breeze for one keeps him alive for exactly one more turn, then Lightweaver's Assaults finish

beats.text: Jett brings in three cards and plays Sadi back from the banishment with only three cards in hand. GlenyBoi has no Stifling Trap to snipe Sadi on its return. Jett swings face rather than into the Aesan Protector and Scout the Land for a better position.

GlenyBoi uses Fluffy Shopkeep again and sends Clarent to the banishment. Jett uses Heavenly Guide to go up to level three and the casters say it is juicy, because GlenyBoi has no Stifling Trap. The Ensnaring Fumes, with a floating memory, are a big blowout.

The casters count 12.5 percent to find a Luxom card and Jett finds a Luxem Sight. GlenyBoi has two Veiling Breezes and a Retribution in hand. Jett has ten cards in hand and could play a raw Slice and Dice into Lightweaver's Assaults, and a Veiling Breeze for one barely keeps him alive for one more turn.
Jett finishes with Lightweaver's Assaults and the damage stays just above GlenyBoi's reach. Jett wins 2-0 and moves to the semifinals against TheRainGoddess, a Wind Luxom against Wind Krux match.

after.summary: Jett wins — suppression buys time, then Assaults finish after Calming Breeze expires

beats.text: Jett plays Stifling Gyre naming Ghosts of Pendragon, adding four to the cost of resolving its entry trigger. GlenyBoi reaches Lorraine, Wandering Warrior and brings out Sword of Seeking.

Imperious Galebind suppresses Jett’s Lost Providence and Poisoned Dagger alongside GlenyBoi’s Drawn Blade. GlenyBoi later pays the Gyre tax to draw from Ghosts, but Jett suppresses the attacker and survives the turn.

GlenyBoi chooses Prismatic Edge over a defensive Clarent line. The forced reveal triggers Jett’s Assault damage. GlenyBoi uses Calming Breeze on Jett’s turn, so Jett waits until it expires, then uses Poisoned Dagger, Gleaming Cut and two Lightweaver’s Assaults to win.

after.summary: Jett wins — Veiling Breeze stops the last point, then Slice and Dice forces the handshake

beats.text: Jett uses Lightweaver’s Assault to reveal Luxem Sight, heal and remove attackers. GlenyBoi continues attacking and eventually puts Jett at 24 damage.
GlenyBoi commits Windmill Engineer for the final point rather than preserve both Veiling Breezes. Jett’s own Veiling Breeze prevents that one damage and keeps him alive.

Jett materializes Nullifying Mirror and uses Lost Providence to reach the resources for a finishing attack. The Zander reveal forces GlenyBoi’s remaining hand down; Slice and Dice begins the attack, and GlenyBoi concedes after the first hit.

before.summary: DJNoVa wins — a huge Aether charge turn and a Flash Grenade stop DinkyDane's Searing Rebuke

beats.text: DinkyDane levels to Diao Chan and plays Firebloom Flourish before turn two, then plays a Fanatical Devotee with exactly four influence. With the Diao Chan class bonus on, the attacks deal extra damage and DJNoVa takes damage from Fractal of Sparks and the board.

DJNoVa plays Manaflare Barrage for three memory to deal two damage to every unit except his champion, then Ignition Draw to look at six cards and banish up to two Aether charges. The Aether ring fills, and Charge the Soul and other Aether charges add small damage sources that DinkyDane cannot easily stop.

DinkyDane keeps four Glimmer counters and sets up Scathing Seminary and Smoke Bombs. The casters count that DinkyDane needs a Searing Rebuke and a way to survive the Aether ring damage. DJNoVa answers with Backstep and Flash Grenade, which cancels every point of damage from Searing Rebuke, and he wins at exact damage.

before.summary: DJNoVa wins — he sends the final attack through a Tariff Ring and a Flickering Cinder is exact lethal

beats.text: DinkyDane is on the play and must win this game to keep his Top 8 hopes (he and CasuaL are the last two European players in the race). His hand has no Fractal and no Firebloom Flourish. He draws Fiery Interference and holds a Glowering Conflagration, and the casters worry that he is short of cheap spells.

DJNoVa uses Ignition Draw each turn, but finds only one Aether charge from six cards. The casters explain that Diana's range is an inherited effect, so an Inert Sword attack also gets range and extra damage. He plays Palvor Sword and Inert Sword, and a Blazing Throw is a surprising card in the deck.

DinkyDane tries to stay alive with a Safeguard Amulet and Crystallized Destiny and a Tariff Ring that taxes DJNoVa's attack. He puts two Glimmer counters on his champion, so DJNoVa must play around Searing Rebuke.

DJNoVa uses Aetheric Calibration and decides to send it, whatever DinkyDane holds. Flickering Cinder, a one-cost fast guard that also deals one damage, is exactly lethal after the Tariff Ring tax. The casters say DinkyDane could not have won next turn even with Searing Rebuke.

after.summary: DJNoVa wins — Flash Grenade and the last Charge the Soul outlast Diao Chan’s burn

beats.text: DinkyDane develops Scathing Seminary and Fractal of Sparks while threatening Searing Rebuke from memory. DJNoVa uses Backstep to enable Flash Grenade.
DJNoVa digs with Ignition Draw and finds enough damage with Charge the Soul and the Aetherwing attack to get past the threatened prevention.

after.summary: DJNoVa wins — Flickering Cinder supplies the final point through Tariff Ring

beats.text: DinkyDane plays Ashwick Cremator and uses Tariff Ring to constrain DJNoVa’s next turn, but lacks the fast damage needed to finish first.
DJNoVa’s Flickering Cinder adds the last point to the finishing sequence. The casters initially overlook its own damage, then confirm exact lethal and the 2–0 result.

They warn that DJNoVa's many small, cheap damage sources can pop Crystallized Destiny before it reaches seven damage.
The casters say DJNoVa has few cards to swap in a fire mirror. They name Ignis Deus and a few Dissuading cards as the likely changes.

before.summary: Fallen Buu wins — Cheshire Cat on turn one cannot be removed, then Smoke Bombs make Carpsong Coda lethal

beats.text: Fallen Buu is on the play and plays Cheshire Cat on turn one with an Inert Sword. Cabin cannot remove the Cat, and its three damage each turn is the pressure he never answers. Cabin draws two with Unmake Duality, sacrificing the Looking Glass, and has Acquiescing Rejection ready.

Cabin builds fractals slowly: Fractal of Snow, Fractal of Intrusion (which looks at Fallen Buu's memory), Spalling Cleanse for recovery and a Throne-Keeper Bullfrog. He uses Tariff Ring and Shimmering Refraction to hold back Fallen Buu's allies, but he is out of actions and takes eight damage early.

Fallen Buu levels Diana, uses floating memory for Krustallan Archer and Languid Toadtroll, and holds Carpsong Coda. If he draws a second Coda, it is over. Cabin uses the Bullfrog and Tariff Ring to waste two damage. Fallen Buu then plays Smoke Bombs, which turns off the Bullfrog's intercept, and Carpsong Coda and the Cheshire Cat deal lethal.

before.summary: Cabin wins — Acquiescing Rejection stops Fallen Buu's distant play, then a sixth fractal and Burst Asunder

beats.text: Cabin is on the play and plays a traditional fractal build-out with Nullifying Lantern in the side. Acquiescing Rejection denies Fallen Buu a card and the distant he needs. Fallen Buu ends his turn with Backstep for distant, and Cabin gets a free build-out turn.

Fallen Buu pushes damage with Charge the Soul and Aquamirage Whisper, and plays Krustallan Archer and Frostsworn Paladin. Take Aim, a two-cost four-damage card, brings Cabin close to lethal: he takes 12 damage in one turn, and Cabin goes hands down with no defense.
Cabin plays Enfeebling Orb to tax Fallen Buu's hand, then plays a sixth fractal and exhausts two more with Shimmering Refraction. He pays four more for Burst Asunder, and it deals lethal damage.

before.summary: Fallen Buu wins — a very long game decided at the last point of damage; a Frostsworn Paladin finishes after Cabin's Burst Asunder falls one short

beats.text: Fallen Buu is on the play again and plays Cheshire Cat with Inert Sword on turn one. Cabin has Zhang Jiao, Way of Peace in hand to recover four, and he fractures the Inert Sword with Fracturize. A Frostsworn Paladin intercepts and kills the Cat with a retaliate, and the Ranger Strides plan is gone.

Fallen Buu keeps replacing his threats with Krustallan Archer, Frostsworn Paladin and Aquamirage Whisper, and Weaving Manastream gives free floating memory. Cabin answers with Acquiescing Rejection and Enfeebling Orb, and uses Shimmering Refraction and Flash Grenade to keep the Archer off the board. Cabin plays Nullifying Lantern and Tariff Ring and heals with Zhang Jiao.

Both players dig for the last points of damage with Captivating Opulence, Backup Charger, Crystalline Mirror, Prismspire Scepter and Smoke Bombs. Fallen Buu uses Ranger Strides to give Diana range four and Cabin fracturizes the Palvor Sword in response. Cabin resolves two Burst Asunder in one turn, but Fallen Buu answers with Refreshing Charge to recover three each time.

Cabin has eight Fantasia allies for Captivating Opulence and puts 17 damage on Fallen Buu. The casters think he fires too early: he does not target the Frostsworn Paladin, and the card he draws is a Fractal, not the lethal card. Fallen Buu's Frostsworn Paladin comes in for three and ends the game.

after.summary: Fallinbuu14 wins — Smoke Bombs lets attacks through the Bullfrog

beats.text: TeamTrueCaban relies on Throne-Keeper Bullfrog and Tariff Ring while building fractals. Fallinbuu14 uses Smoke Bombs to bypass the Bullfrog’s protection.
Carpsong Coda targets TeamTrueCaban, then Cheshire Cat and Diana attacks supply the remaining damage.

after.summary: TeamTrueCaban wins — six fractals enable Shimmering Refraction and Burst Asunder

beats.text: TeamTrueCaban builds five fractals and survives Fallinbuu14’s Take Aim turn. Enfeebling Orb then puts Fallinbuu14’s hand down.
Still on the spirit, TeamTrueCaban adds a sixth fractal, plays Shimmering Refraction and pays the higher cost for Burst Asunder to win game two.

after.summary: Fallinbuu14 wins — Shimmering Refraction falls short and Paladin ends the game

beats.text: TeamTrueCaban uses Fractal of Intrusion to discard Fracturize, then finds Shimmering Refraction through Fractal of Refreshment. The spell targets Diana and brings her to 17 damage.

TeamTrueCaban draws another fractal rather than a finisher. With no answer to the remaining Frostsworn Paladin, its attack wins the match for Fallinbuu14. The final near-lethal spell was Shimmering Refraction, not Burst Asunder.

before.summary: DJNoVa wins — a lucky start and a Cheshire Cat from the top of his deck beat the Safeguard Amulet

beats.text: Superior is on the play with Fractal of Rain and Unbroken Mustang in hand. He levels up early and plays Frostsworn Paladin, but refuses to attack so that he takes no damage. DJNoVa passes his first turn, which is normal for a fire Diana deck.

DJNoVa uses a pre-recollection Aether charge to deal three damage to every unit but his champion, which kills the Paladin. Infernal Manastreak and the Diana regalia weapon add more damage. Superior uses Unbroken Mustang to destroy the regalia weapon, and the casters say this removes DJNoVa's best damage source.

Superior has no way to stop DJNoVa's damage this turn and a Safeguard Amulet does not save him. DJNoVa draws the Cheshire Cat from the top of his deck, which adds three damage, and Staggering Strike and a Ranger Strides line add two more for exact lethal.

before.summary: Superior wins — he keeps influence up, wipes the Aether charges with Fracturize and builds a huge graveyard for Strategem of Myriad Ice

beats.text: Superior has Refracting Missile, Seaside Ringleader and Strategem of Myriad Ice and plays a protective game. He holds his influence against the fire deck and uses Refracting Missile to put floating memory in the graveyard. DJNoVa plays Ranger Strides early and draws a card.

DJNoVa puts out Palvor Sword, Infernal Vessel (no recover for Superior) and a Trivier regalia weapon, and his first Aether charges nearly end the game. Superior mills Fracturize, which the casters say may cost him the game. Palvor Sword banishes the graveyard face down, and Superior's water cards are denied.

Superior gets Song of Frost and Resonating Fugue online, flips Genbu (a 9/3 body with Fugue) and holds two Strategems of Myriad Ice. DJNoVa keeps pressure on with Quickdraw Piercer and Singeing Leap, but Superior has the Safeguard Amulet and the answers to each hit. DJNoVa scoops after he sees a Strategem.

before.summary: Superior wins — Fracturize and Tidal Lock deny the early Aether charges; Genbu and Tidestone Bovine mill for a 15-damage threat

beats.text: DJNoVa is on the play and wants a fast start. Superior has two Resonating Fugues, two Gentle Respites and a couple of Fractals of Rain in hand, and plays Tidal Lock at once. The casters ask if DJNoVa can load enough Aether charges.

Superior fractures the Trivier regalia weapon and negates the early Aether charges. DJNoVa plays Ignition Draw and finds only one Aether charge, and he uses Flickering Cinder and Burning Aethercharge to put two damage on Guo Jia.

Superior levels up, flips Genbu and attacks with Tidestone Bovine to mill two cards for quest counters. He mills three more with Fractal of Rain, so a Genbu attack for 15 is lethal. DJNoVa answers with Flash Grenade and Manaflare Barrage, but he has no distant enabler and no Dissuading card to stop the swing. The turtle wins the game.

after.summary: DJNoVa wins — Cat and Palvor Sword supply combat damage past Safeguard Amulet

beats.text: Superior removes Trivariate Dream with Unbroken Mustang and materializes Safeguard Amulet against non-combat damage.
DJNoVa brings out Palvor Sword and Cheshire Cat. Their attacks supply the five damage needed to finish despite the amulet.

after.summary: Superior wins — Genbu stays protected until Strategem of Myriad Ice

beats.text: Superior uses Guo Jia’s lineage release to negate Smoke Bombs, preserving Genbu’s taunt.
DJNoVa has no way through the defensive setup and concedes when Superior presents Strategem of Myriad Ice.

after.summary: Superior wins — graveyard setup makes the Genbu attack lethal

beats.text: Tidestone Bovine and Conniving Plans build Superior’s graveyard for a finishing Genbu attack, with Safeguard Amulet limiting burn damage.
Superior plays Resonating Fugue and attacks with Genbu. DJNoVa cannot combine a distant enabler with Manaflare Barrage using the influence available, and Superior wins 2–1.
