before.summary: ProAnnn wins — Demolition and a stream of burn spells bring Apaul down while he has no hand

beats.text: ProAnnn materializes his Spirit of Fire, but has no Beseech the Winds in hand and uses Fairy Whispers to look for it. The casters note he has seven quest counters while Apaul has ten, and a Peppered Chef is in his hand.
Apaul pays dearly for a Resolute Stand early. He sits on a hand of zero cards at 22 life. ProAnnn plays Demolition for three, levels to Guo Jia two and keeps Restorative Flame ready.

ProAnnn throws another burn spell and Suzaku's Command, and Apaul's Gazelle taunt cannot stop the burn. The casters say Apaul could take 16 to 20 damage in a single turn out of nowhere. ProAnnn takes game one.

before.summary: Apaul wins — he goes first, flips the Seiryuu with ten quest counters, and Resolute Stand pays out

beats.text: Apaul goes first and uses Glimpse and Winds of Destiny to dig through the deck. ProAnnn cannot use his Liminal Guide for a net-neutral level up. The casters say the Seiryuu needs only nine more quest counters and is easy to bring to ten.

ProAnnn answers with Rile the Abyss in Apaul's end step and top-decks a Creative Shock off a double Rile the Abyss. He has Heated Vengeance and a Tree of Hearts, and Apaul must show respect to the burn.

Apaul goes up to nine and then ten quest counters with the Dungeon Guide, and levels to Guo Jia level three. A Baby Green Slime targets the Fabled Ruby Fatestone, because it is not a spell, and Apaul's Seiryuu comes in. ProAnnn does not have the Resolute Stand and loses the game.

before.summary: Apaul wins — a top-decked Innervate Agility and Seiryuu's Command beat ProAnnn's burn, and ProAnnn forgets a Gazelle trigger

beats.text: ProAnnn goes first with no Creative Shock and no Rile the Abyss, so he has no net-neutral level up. He uses Searing Truth for two quest counters and keeps a Fabled Ruby Fatestone, but has no Peppered Chef to flip the Suzaku early.

Apaul uses Baby Green Slime to stop the Impact Hammer and a Fabled Ruby Fatestone, and the quest counters stay but the stone is suppressed. ProAnnn uses a Vermilion Decree for three damage, and Apaul answers with Winds of Destiny and Fairy Whispers.

Apaul pops Portentous Tanggu and finds Innervate Agility. Innervate Agility recovers five and lets him level, and he takes ProAnnn to 22 with a seven plus four plus eleven line. ProAnnn needs a Suzaku's Command but does not find it, and the casters say Apaul would take the game with the Seiryuu's Command.

Apaul forgets that Gazelle is tapped and makes a misplay, but ProAnnn still cannot burn him out. Apaul wins the match 2-1 and is the Ascent Taipei champion; the casters say they love a misplay that still wins.

after.summary: ProAnnn wins — Suzaku and Peppered Chef punish Apaul’s tapped-out turn

beats.text: Apaul spends his hand, including Resolute Stand, to flip the panda. ProAnnn uses Demolition, Impact Hammer and Embercrypt Burn to build the remaining quest counters.
ProAnnn flips Suzaku and uses Peppered Chef for the finishing damage. The predicted Guo Jia level-up and Suzaku’s Command lines are not the line played.

after.summary: Apaul wins — survives the burn turn, then commands Seiryuu

beats.text: Baby Green Slime denies a turn of Fabled Ruby Fatestone counters. ProAnnn later resolves Fiery Interference, but cannot afford the entire planned burn-and-command sequence.
Apaul uses Resolute Stand, then Seiryuu’s Command before recollection. ProAnnn has too few cards to cast Restorative Flame, and the match goes to game three.

after.summary: Apaul wins — Seiryuu pressure and Tariff Ring outlast ProAnnn’s burn

beats.text: Apaul reaches Guo Jia level 3 while preserving Seiryuu’s Command and Innervate Agility. Censer of Restful Peace limits ProAnnn’s floating-memory options.

Seiryuu’s Command produces an attack and Arcane Blast, but ProAnnn survives with Restorative Flame. Apaul then attacks with Gazelle; the casters note he overlooked ProAnnn’s Guo Jia level 2 life total.
Tariff Ring restricts ProAnnn’s reply. He draws another floating-memory card instead of the burn he needs, and Apaul takes the championship.

before.summary: Hyouka wins — a long Pneumonic Charm and Arcane Blast level-up sequence beats the Oblation clock

beats.text: DuckHats opens on Fire CL with Liminal Guide and Cremation Ritual, setting up a Baleful Oblation and holding a Feu Awakening. The casters call Feu Awakening the key card for DuckHats to find before Hyouka reaches level three.

Hyouka holds all four Dungeon Guides and goes straight to level three, using Undeniable Truth on a Liminal Guide to draw. He is influence-maxing with two Pneumonic Charms and Tome of Sacred Lightning, which makes each charm able to cast an Arcane Blast for free once he reaches level nine.

Careful Study gives a huge pile of enlightened counters, and a second Arcane Blast plus the Arcane Elemental are ready. The casters note CL's 30 life is a bigger buffer than most champions have, but Hyouka finds the swing before DuckHats can use his own lethal turn. Hyouka takes game one.

before.summary: DuckHats wins — Orb of Sealing and Topsy Decree stall Hyouka, and the Oblation clock closes

beats.text: DuckHats lines up Topsy Decree and an Oblation, and uses the Mansion/armoire turns to keep Hyouka off the arcane cards. Hyouka brings in the Orb of Sealing from the side as an answer to the fire build.

Hyouka digs for Arcane Sight and Erratic Bolt, and holds a Spell Shield Arcane. The casters say DuckHats wants exactly this, because it lets him play directly through the shield, and Hyouka tries to use Tome of Sacred Lightning to bank more arcane cards but only finds an Advent of the Stormcaller.
The casters call the 28 damage Hyouka needs a non-viable line, so he plays safer with Careful Study, but DuckHats closes the game. DuckHats wins game two and takes the match to a third game.

before.summary: Hyouka wins — going first, he stacks the top of his deck and finishes with Arcane Blast and Arcane Elemental

beats.text: Hyouka gets to go first, which the casters call night and day in level three matchups. DuckHats brings down the Grande Sonnerie with the reserve costs for a lethal attack on its own, and Hyouka answers with Fluffy Shopkeep and Three Visits.

Hyouka has too many arcane cards for his own hand, banishes the useless ones and digs with Careful Study. The casters note Fluffy Shopkeep on intercept is a good call. Lost Providence stacks the top of the deck.

Hyouka sends 15 damage at the face. With two Disorienting Winds, a second Arcane Blast and an Advent of the Stormcaller, he chains Arcane Blast into Arcane Elemental and Advent. Disorienting Winds returns the Arcane Elemental for another seven damage, DuckHats concedes and Hyouka wins the match.

after.summary: Hyouka wins — two Arcane Blasts and Arcane Elemental finish before DuckHats’s next turn

beats.text: DuckHats uses Undeniable Truth on Liminal Guide before leveling, then draws further cards through the returning Guide and Cremation Ritual. He reaches Ciel’s third level and fires Baleful Oblation while Hyouka has few cards in hand.

Hyouka uses Dungeon Guide and Disorienting Winds to reach Rai’s third level. On the following turn, Tome of Sorcery and Tome of Sacred Lightning help raise his effective level, with two Mnemonic Charms available.
Hyouka digs with Careful Study, then uses the two Charms to cast two Arcane Blasts. Arcane Elemental supplies the final attack before DuckHats can finish with another omen sequence.

after.summary: DuckHats wins — Orb of Sealing limits Rai’s level, then Grande Sonnerie supplies the finishing attack

beats.text: DuckHats’s Orb of Sealing turns Hyouka’s banished arcane cards face down, denying their level bonuses. Hyouka needs to regain levels before Alkahest can answer the Orb.

Hyouka uses Beseech the Winds to materialize and banish an arcane card, but DuckHats answers with Nocturne’s Oblivion on Alkahest. Tome of Sacred Lightning banishes Advent of the Stormcaller, and Careful Study adds resources without producing a lethal line.
DuckHats materializes Grande Sonnerie for a lethal Ciel attack. Manxome Armoire gives him a way through Spellshield: Arcane, and he takes game two.

after.summary: Hyouka wins — Advent of the Stormcaller sets up Arcane Elemental and Disorienting Winds

beats.text: Going first, Hyouka uses Purifying Thurible, Fluffy Shopkeep and Three Visits to prepare his levels. DuckHats takes a Backup Charger turn and draws with Angel Attendant and Cremation Ritual.
Hyouka banishes several arcane cards while leveling, then digs with Careful Study. DuckHats reaches level three but lacks a 15-cost omen and useful interaction for an Oblation finish.

After using Shattering Discharge and the Tome sequence, Hyouka resolves Advent of the Stormcaller and arranges his remaining draws. Fluffy Shopkeep attacks, then Arcane Elemental swings for seven. DuckHats’s Undeniable Truth draws Golden Checkmate, but cannot stop the Disorienting Winds replay line and he concedes.

before.summary: HolySamurai wins — constant raccoon and slime pressure lets him close without ever resolving a beast

beats.text: Xaleonidas starts with Spirit of Water and a Fractal of Snow, but throws only one Fractal, which the casters say is low for going second. He draws a second Fractal off the first Fractal of Refreshment and holds a Refracting Missile.
Xaleonidas snipes the Baby Gray Slime with Refracting Missile, which stops HolySamurai from returning it and negates the Escape the Wreckage. The casters call it a huge momentum shift.

HolySamurai has a Bandit and a Protector Raccoon in the opening hand, which the casters say constricts Fractals. He baits two Glimmering Refusals and gets in with Gaia's blessing and a Slime Eruption in hand. The casters say HolySamurai has lethal on board and beats his chest when game one is his.

before.summary: Xaleonidas wins — Enfeebling Orb and a burst of Fractals break HolySamurai's Blanch timing

beats.text: HolySamurai starts with Creative Shock and discards a Hymn of Gaia's Grace. Xaleonidas hits through the board three more times and takes HolySamurai to six damage of fifteen.

Xaleonidas plays Captivating Opulence to stifle HolySamurai, who must pay extra for each play. The casters point to the Stonescale Band, the Horn of Beastcalling and the Covenant of Thorns in HolySamurai's hand. HolySamurai tries to get the Slime King down, which needs three different elements of slimes.

HolySamurai will not pay ten into a Glimmering Refusal and instead slows down with Blanch in hand. The Frostsworn Paladin attacks into the Blanch and banishes it. Xaleonidas lines up an 18-damage burst, one over the needed amount. HolySamurai sends the Blanch too early, the Enfeebling Orb forces it to be popped, and Xaleonidas takes game two.

before.summary: Xaleonidas wins — a race against the clock ends in a Burst Asunder with six fractals out

beats.text: Both decks must end the game fast with little time on the clock. HolySamurai goes bandit into bandit and plays a double Dungeon Guide start. Xaleonidas plays a double fractal start with Fractal of Snow and Fractal of Insight, and throws a Burst Asunder away to the discard.

HolySamurai plays Limitless Slime and a Baby Red Slime for a six-damage turn, over half of Xaleonidas's life in one turn. The casters say it is the only play that makes sense, because he needs Slime Eruption to deal damage.
Xaleonidas has five fractals out, then six. He puts down the Enfeebling Orb and pays for a Burst Asunder. HolySamurai cannot stop it, and Xaleonidas wins the match 2-1.

after.summary: HolySamurai wins — constant raccoon and slime pressure lets him close without ever resolving a beast

beats.text: Xaleonidas finds a second Fractal of Refreshment from the first while looking for more fractals and Zhang Jiao. He holds Refracting Missile as HolySamurai sets up Baby Gray Slime.
Xaleonidas snipes the Baby Gray Slime with Refracting Missile, which stops HolySamurai from returning it and negates the Escape the Wreckage. The casters call it a huge momentum shift.

Bandit and Protector Raccoon restrict Xaleonidas’s floating memory. Two Glimmering Refusals stop the advanced-element slimes, but Baby Red Slime keeps attacking. HolySamurai later attacks with his small allies and responds to Shimmering Refraction with lethal Slime Eruption, paying through Acquiescing Rejection.

after.summary: Xaleonidas wins — Captivating Opulence restricts defenses before an 18-damage Burst Asunder

beats.text: Xaleonidas opens Aquifer Seneschal and protects its pressure with Bullfrog. HolySamurai uses Creative Shock, discarding Hymn of Gaia’s Grace, and develops Backup Charger for a slower start.

Captivating Opulence taxes HolySamurai’s activated abilities. Xaleonidas negates a Dungeon Guide and an advanced-element slime, then develops Zhang Jiao and Enfeebling Orb. When HolySamurai spends cards on Hymn of Gaia’s Grace, Crystalline Mirror removes Quicksilver Grail before he can afford its activation.

HolySamurai declines the expensive Storm Slime line and keeps Blanche available. Enfeebling Orb forces the defensive timing: Blanche enters early, and Frostsworn Paladin removes her in combat while banishing Return to the Archive for its attack benefit. Xaleonidas resolves an 18-damage Burst Asunder to tie the match.

after.summary: Xaleonidas wins — a race against the clock ends in a Burst Asunder with six fractals out

beats.text: With little time remaining, HolySamurai opens Bandit into another Bandit and holds multiple Dungeon Guides. Xaleonidas opens Fractal of Snow and Fractal of Insight, discarding a Burst Asunder. Both players spend early turns building resources rather than immediately leveling.

HolySamurai later levels to Silvie, uses Dungeon Guide to reach level two, and adds Baby Red Slime beside Limitless Slime. The small allies threaten six damage while Bandit continues to restrict Xaleonidas’s graveyard.

Still on spirit, Xaleonidas materializes Enfeebling Orb. Shimmering Refraction and Refracting Missile establish the damage needed for Burst Asunder, which sacrifices his fractals and wins the match 2-1.

before.summary: Royan wins — Tidal Lock into Engulf leaves JacePatrick with no interaction, then Genbu arrives

beats.text: JacePatrick uses Creative Shock, but Royan's Engulf stops Advent of the Stormcaller from going to the graveyard, so he adds it to the omens from hand. Royan is happy to see floating memory in the graveyard for later plays.

Royan draws extra from the Tidestone Bovine and takes his time because Genbu is hard to bring out unless he is set up. JacePatrick holds a scary hand with a 19-damage Baleful Oblation lethal line but no Feu Awakening yet, and the casters note that Royan has shown a Revitalizing Cleanse that answers it.

Royan casts Tidal Lock into Engulf, so JacePatrick is out of interaction. Genbu, Black Tortoise hits the battlefield and Royan takes game one. The casters say JacePatrick's early and mid game was rough even though he held late-game bombs.

before.summary: Royan wins — JacePatrick sends his whole hand to the graveyard with Feu Awakening, but Royan finds the line through Folded Shadow

beats.text: JacePatrick has drawn the Turbo Charge this time, and plays a Liminal Guide as the first play. Without a Creative Shock, he adds a Golden Checkmate to the banish with an omen counter. The casters say he has four guides in memory, which helps fight the water negate decks.

Royan keeps pressure on with annoying minions and the Tidestone Bovine, going up to six quest counters and six cards in hand for the Revitalizing Cleanse. JacePatrick's Folded Shadows puts Royan under spell shroud and stealth, and the casters say Royan cannot easily push through.

JacePatrick throws Feu Awakening and sends his entire hand to the graveyard in a hail-mary line. Royan still has the Revitalizing Cleanse that could escape lethal, takes the chance JacePatrick will walk in, and finds the path to win. Royan moves to 3-0 against the boogeyman of the event, Oblation CL.

after.summary: Royan wins — Tidal Lock into Engulf leaves JacePatrick with no interaction, then Genbu arrives

beats.text: Royan negates Creative Shock with Engulf. JacePatrick omens Baleful Oblation from the graveyard, keeping Advent of the Stormcaller in hand for a later Manxome Armoire exchange.

Frostsworn Paladin pressures JacePatrick while Royan develops Slick Torrent Rider and two Fractals of Polar Depths. JacePatrick takes several turns to reach level three, then sets up an Oblation threat. The casters identify Spalling Cleanse as a possible answer.

Royan follows Tidal Lock with Engulf, leaving JacePatrick without cards for interaction. Fractal of Polar Depths supplies the final quest counters; Genbu appears and Resonating Fugue prompts JacePatrick’s concession.

after.summary: Royan wins — Revitalizing Cleanse buys a turn, then Fracturize removes Folded Shadows for Genbu’s finish

beats.text: JacePatrick uses Backup Charger and Turbo Charge to build influence, but draws several Liminal Guides without an immediate way to discard them. He omens Golden Checkmate from hand. Later, Royan negates Dungeon Guide with Engulf and keeps attacking with Seaside Ringleader and Frostsworn Paladin.

JacePatrick pays through Cerulean Decree on Baleful Oblation, leaving no cards to contest Tidal Lock after Decree reaches the graveyard. Folded Shadows later gives JacePatrick’s Ciel spellshroud and stealth, stopping Royan’s direct attacks.

JacePatrick uses Feu Awakening to remove Frostsworn Paladin and strengthen Grande Sonnerie’s attack. Royan survives and uses Revitalizing Cleanse. On the next turn, Enfeebling Orb restricts JacePatrick’s hand, Fracturize removes Folded Shadows, and Genbu with Resonating Fugue closes the match 2-0.

before.summary: Dal157 wins — TheRainGoddess never finds Baleful Oblation and the Dynastic Whirlpool mills the deck out

beats.text: TheRainGoddess keeps the opening hand but has to be careful: against mill, each extra card drawn pulls the deck closer to empty. She removes a lantern and an Orb of Sealing from the material deck to draw an additional card.

Dal157 starts slowly and goes up to Jin level one, and the casters point out that levels one and two just lead to level three in these Jin decks. A triple Angelic Channeling puts advanced element cards in his lineage, and he uses Fracturize on TheRainGoddess's chalice.

TheRainGoddess has only 14 cards left, still no Baleful Oblation, and has drawn the cards Dal157 needed. A bubble of abundance and a 15-card mill finish it, and she scoops. Dal157 stabilizes and mills out TheRainGoddess to take game one, a game that was rough in the early stages for him.

before.summary: TheRainGoddess wins — a huge Turbo Charge start and a clean Oblation sequence, then Dal157 goes to sleep

beats.text: TheRainGoddess hits a 53 off Rector's Tiding with Backup Charger and Turbo Charge, going up to level one with Creative Shock and a discarded Liminal Guide. The casters call it the start you want in game two and note Cremation Ritual is next. Topsy Decree handles an Angelic Channeling.

Dal157 has the Spirit of Serene Water ready to heal six at any time and uses Umbra Sight to sculpt his hand. He goes down to 17 and back up to 32, and Transfusive Aura makes a recovery cheaper, but the casters say the longer game helps TheRainGoddess.

Dal157 goes down to 15 because of Transfusive Aura, but it is still not enough. TheRainGoddess finds no Berserker's Plate for him, plays Feu Awakening with Oblations and sends Dal157 to sleep. The casters call it a masterclass Oblation game and count 30 minutes for game one and 20 for game two.

before.summary: No winner — the round ends one card short of a TheRainGoddess lethal

beats.text: Dal157 goes first with about seven minutes left and keeps Spirit of Serene Water. His opening hand has Liminal Guide, Angelic Channeling and Angel Attendant but no Cremation Ritual. The casters say a double loss would be painful for both players, and the two are friendly with each other.

TheRainGoddess uses Fracturize on Dal157's Power Cell to deny his floating memory, Dal157 tries three games in a row to go to level one with floating memory and fails again. TheRainGoddess uses Creative Shock, Backup Charger and a Dungeon Guide to find Oblations, and she uses Cremation Ritual.

Dal157 uses Pearled Prayer to recover seven (down to 45 damage) and Manflesh, and goes to Jin level three with Undying Resolve. He uses Dynastic Whirlpool to mill 15, and the Serene Spirit takes him from 19 to 13, which TheRainGoddess has to push 28 damage through. She is one damage short; the next card would have been Feu Awakening, but time is called and the match is a draw.

after.summary: Dal157 wins — TheRainGoddess never finds Baleful Oblation and the Dynastic Whirlpool mills the deck out

beats.text: TheRainGoddess keeps the opening hand but has to be careful: against mill, each extra card drawn pulls the deck closer to empty. She removes a lantern and an Orb of Sealing from the material deck to draw an additional card.

TheRainGoddess uses Angelic Channeling to set up advanced-element cards. Dal157 uses Fracturize on his own Power Cell for a reservable fractal, but TheRainGoddess’s Topsy Decree denies the floating memory. Dal157 spends early turns drawing and setting up Jin while Fluffy Shopkeep attacks.

Dal157 survives heavy damage through Pearled Prayer, Mend Flesh and Regenerate, then mills with Dynastic Whirlpool. TheRainGoddess draws deeper through Devouring Malice and Umbra Sight but cannot find Baleful Oblation. Another 15-card mill and Bauble of Abundance leave no escape, and TheRainGoddess concedes.

after.summary: TheRainGoddess wins — a fast draw engine builds repeated Oblation pressure through Jin’s recovery

beats.text: TheRainGoddess hits five plus three with Rictus Tiding, then uses Backup Charger and Turbo Charge to build influence. Creative Shock discards Liminal Guide for the level-up, followed by Library Witch and Cremation Ritual. Topsy Decree again interferes with Dal157’s Angelic Channeling setup.

Oblation and Devastating Blow force Dal157 into recovery. He uses Chalice of Blood, Seething Intercession, Transfusive Aura and Pearled Prayer, while TheRainGoddess keeps Lost Providence available to support another finishing sequence.
Dal157 releases Spirit of Serene Water and benefits from Transfusive Aura, but another Baleful Oblation followed by Feu Awakening supplies enough damage to end game two. The match is tied 1-1.

after.summary: Draw — Jin’s recovery leaves TheRainGoddess one damage short as time expires

beats.text: Dal157 goes first and keeps Spirit of Serene Water. TheRainGoddess holds Liminal Guide, Angelic Channeling and Angel Attendant, but initially lacks Cremation Ritual. Both players must develop quickly with only a few minutes remaining.

TheRainGoddess uses Topsy Decree against Dal157’s Angelic Channeling setup. Dal157 later Fracturizes his own Power Cell to help level. TheRainGoddess draws with Creative Shock and Cremation Ritual, finding multiple Oblations, while Dal157 uses two Dungeon Guides to reach Jin, Undying Resolve.

Dal157 materializes Berserker Plate and uses Pearled Prayers to recover during the extra turns. He releases Spirit of Serene Water between Oblations. TheRainGoddess adds Feu Awakening and Manxome Armoire damage, but Lost Providence fails to draw the additional Feu needed. The final line is one damage short, and time ends the match 1-1.

before.summary: Guruthos wins — he survives a double Crystallized Destiny and a Grande Sonnerie swing finishes with an Oblation

beats.text: Jayare opens with a Dungeon Guide level-up that the casters call really bad, playing Liminal Guide-style value and Planted Explosive for a four-damage trap. Guruthos plays Angelic Channeling at end of turn and Mirage's Grave off a Dungeon Guide, going to 30 life with 21 left for Jayare to deal.

Jayare must play slowly because he needs Crystallized Destiny in hand to survive CL's big Oblation turn. Guruthos uses Nocturne's Oblivion on the Orb of Sealing and sends Baleful Oblation at the materialization.

Guruthos loses the Turbo Charge to memory, which he is happy about, and draws a Feu Awakening off the Grande Sonnerie. The Grande Sonnerie swings for five unpreventable damage and Jayare has no Restorative Flames with an empty fire graveyard. Jayare never finds Blazing Throw or Heated Vengeance, and Guruthos takes game one.

before.summary: Jayare wins — Suzaku's Command and Peppered Chef get through Oblation negation

beats.text: Jayare plays first with Suzaku Guo A. Guruthos has Resolute Stand and Topsy Decree down early and a Liminal Guide, and the casters say the Blanch is strong for him here. Jayare keeps up fire cards in the graveyard for the Peppered Chef.

Guruthos wants the Chalice of Blood and Manxome Armoire and uses a free Resolute Stand to get through. He pays for the Golden Checkmate, which is dangerous because Jayare can throw away the Checkmate. Jayare gets two quest counters with Fiery Interference while only two fire cards are in hand, so he cannot imbue it.

Guruthos plays Baleful Oblation to clear the board, but Jayare activates the Suzaku's Command before swinging with the Peppered Chef. Guruthos's Orb of Sealing flips the omen, so the Oblation does zero damage. The lethal Suzaku attack wins game two for Jayare.

before.summary: Guruthos wins — he goes first, banishes two to level up and uses Abnegation to stop the burn

beats.text: Guruthos goes first. The casters say going first is a huge advantage for CL into fire aggro, and that fractals and fire aggro are CL's worst matchups. He has only four cards in influence and must banish two to level up, losing an Angelic Channeling to Jayare's quest counters.

Jayare starts with the first Crystallized Destiny, then Manxome Armoire resolves and takes the Checkmate back to hand. The casters talk about the Chalice of Blood as the reason Guruthos may live through Jayare's damage.

Guruthos holds Abnegation, so Jayare's Fiery Interference line cannot use the heal. Guruthos plays Baleful Oblation at the end of turn with the Abnegation backup, and Jayare has no Restorative Flames and an empty fire graveyard. Jayare scoops and Guruthos wins the match 2-1, going to 4-1.

after.summary: Guruthos wins — survives Jayare’s double-Destiny turn, then finishes with Grande Sonnerie and omen damage

beats.text: Guruthos opens Dungeon Guide without using its level-up effect, then develops Ciel through Angelic Channeling and another Guide. Jayare opens Liminal Guide, sacrifices it with Undeniable Truth before leveling, and develops Avatar of Suzaku and quest counters.

Guruthos removes Jayare’s Orb of Sealing with Nocturne’s Oblivion, then materializes Manxome Armoire. During Jayare’s attack turn, Guruthos casts Baleful Oblation. Armoire breaks the first Crystallized Destiny, but Jayare has a second Destiny to prevent the Oblation damage to his champion. Suzaku returns and attacks, leaving Guruthos at 25 damage.

Guruthos materializes Grande Sonnerie, banishing Turbo Charge, and draws Feu Awakening. Ciel attacks for five; the end-phase omen adds the final two damage. Jayare has no fire cards left in the graveyard to support Restorative Flame, and Guruthos takes game one.

after.summary: Jayare wins — Fiery Interference denies recovery, and Orb of Sealing blanks the defensive Oblation

beats.text: Jayare goes first with Creative Shock and Liminal Guide, then clears Guruthos’s Fluffy Shopkeep with Demolition. Avatar of Suzaku and Vengeful Paramour build an ally-heavy board. Guruthos develops Angel Attendant and keeps Resolute Stand, discarding Blanche while leveling.

Guruthos uses Resolute Stand for its alternate cost, then materializes Chalice of Blood. Jayare cannot imbue Vermilion Decree with only two fire cards in hand, but uses Fiery Interference to add a quest counter and prevent recovery. Chalice draws Guruthos Abnegation, which cannot heal that turn.

Jayare uses Peppered Chef with Suzaku and activates Suzaku’s Command before the Chef’s attack. Guruthos attempts Baleful Oblation to clear the board, but Jayare’s Orb of Sealing turns the omen face down. The zero-damage Oblation cannot stop the lethal attack.

after.summary: Guruthos wins — Manxome Armoire restores the 15-cost omen for a decisive main-phase Oblation

beats.text: Guruthos goes first while Jayare develops two Vengeful Paramours. Guruthos holds Flamewreath Call but does not use it. Jayare’s Embercrypt Burn removes Angelic Channeling from the graveyard, forcing Guruthos to pay two cards to level; Ciel’s on-enter then discards Flamewreath Call.

Guruthos uses Dungeon Guide to reach Ciel’s third level with low influence. Jayare materializes Orb of Sealing. Guruthos chooses Manxome Armoire instead of Chalice of Blood, preparing an immediate Oblation attempt.

Guruthos plays Baleful Oblation in his main phase. Jayare activates Orb of Sealing, but Manxome Armoire returns Golden Checkmate to hand and places it back as a face-up omen. Jayare lacks the needed defense, and Guruthos wins 2-1.

before.summary: GlenyBoi wins — Ascension rips Limelight's memory apart and Prismatic Edge pushes the last damage

beats.text: The casters frame the match as a rematch of Worlds 2024 Round 1, when Limelight's Fire Umbra Diana beat Glenny's Merlin on the way to the lock. They favor the Oblation player in the matchup, but since the Clarent nerf to one prevention, much of the Oblation advantage is gone.

GlenyBoi sets up the dungeon guides on top of the deck and goes to level three. He uses Aella and Spirit Blade: Ascension to bring Prismatic Edge in and out of play, and plays Fairy Whispers to know what is on top. Fluffy Shopkeep and Calming Breeze do little against Limelight's plan.

Limelight finds Cremation Ritual and Liminal Guide, and keeps Resolute Stand and an Enel-style spell in hand to answer the pressure. The Baleful Oblation is banished off a Spirit Blade: Ascension on the Prismatic Edge. GlenyBoi swings with Prismatic Edge for three, then another Ascension, and takes game one, to the casters' praise for the deck mastery.

before.summary: GlenyBoi wins — Imperious Galebind and a double Ascension rip clear the last Oblation

beats.text: GlenyBoi draws into the Dungeon Guide he stacked on top, uses a Scout the Land to see two Ascensions, and starts with Sword of Seeking and Lorraine level one. He rips the Spurell out of the sideboard and into the banish before it can do anything, then rips Undeniable Truth out of Limelight's hand.

Limelight tries to level with Dungeon Guide and holds up the null spell. The casters say he has no Resolute Stand this time and has to look for another way to survive, but sacrificing his ally only draws Carter. Baleful Oblation clears the board, but GlenyBoi's Krux sight returns the Ascension to hand.

GlenyBoi uses Imperious Galebind on the Aella and Ghosts of Pendragon, and double Ascension rips Limelight's memory. Limelight casts Feu Awakening and sends the damage at Aella, but GlenyBoi has all he needs, and the casters celebrate his revenge from Worlds 2024.

after.summary: GlenyBoi wins — Ascension rips Limelight's memory apart and Prismatic Edge pushes the last damage

beats.text: GlenyBoi levels through two Dungeon Guides after Limelight removes Sword of Seeking with Reduce to Ash. Drawn Blade returns, letting Lorraine attack Library Witch for a draw. Two Ghosts of Pendragon then rebuild GlenyBoi’s hand.

After Limelight clears the board with Baleful Oblation, GlenyBoi uses Spirit Blade: Ascension and Crux Sight to repeatedly return Prismatic Edge. Memory banishes remove Oblation and other threats; Aella adds another suppression cycle. Fairy Whispers and Scout the Land find further Ascensions.

Limelight survives with Resolute Stand and later uses Devouring Malice to deal three and recover three. Another Ascension banishes his newly drawn Oblation. GlenyBoi replaces Aella under the unique rule and finishes with ally damage and Lorraine’s Prismatic Edge attack.

after.summary: GlenyBoi wins — Galebind on Manxome Armoire blunts Oblation, then Ascension finishes through Feu

beats.text: GlenyBoi builds resources with Fluffy Shopkeep, Reclaim and Aesan Protector before leveling Lorraine. In response to Limelight’s Dungeon Guide, Ascension brings back Prismatic Edge; Annul Spell stops Crux Sight, but Edge still banishes Spirelle from memory. A later Ascension banishes Undeniable Truth.

Limelight attempts Baleful Oblation with Manxome Armoire available. GlenyBoi uses Imperious Galebind on the Armoire rather than only his own value pieces, keeping the Oblation at three damage and preserving Aella. Limelight sacrifices Dungeon Guide to draw Carter, then uses Carter and an omen trigger to remove Ghosts of Pendragon.

With Limelight low on cards, GlenyBoi presses with his board and Prismatic Edge. Limelight uses Feu Awakening to try to remove Aella, but GlenyBoi responds with Crux Sight to retrieve Spirit Blade: Ascension. The Ascension finishes the match 2-0.

before.summary: Apaul wins — a turn-two panda and big Seiryuu's Command turns push Aqua to the edge, and Aqua runs out of out cards

beats.text: Apaul opens with a five-quest-counter Guo Jia start on turn two, using Scout the Land and recollect to draw into the panda. The casters introduce Daunting Panda and Angelic Channeling as the key cards that accelerate quest counters.

Seiryuu's Command triggers three modes on each attack and Apaul chooses empower. The Su Azure Dragon grows by one for every five damage counters on it, reaching 12 power. Aqua is at Jin level two with 24 damage and uses Enchanted Fete to recover memory.

Aqua lines up Relentless Outburst into Shangi plus a swing to finish the game, and the casters say he was literally one thing away. Apaul commands a huge amount of damage and Aqua is forced to win in one turn or lose. Apaul takes game one.

before.summary: Apaul wins — Optical Control locks out half of Aqua's deck and Aqua just misses the Quicksilver Grail line

beats.text: Aqua plays Spirit of Fortuitous Water to glimpse seven, and goes for a Backup Charger to level up as a control deck. Apaul uses a Besiege Faint Stone, Auspicious Manifestation discarded for a quest counter, and Angelic Channeling for another three quest counters.

Apaul brings out the dragon and a stifling trap, which had wrecked Aqua in the previous game. Optical Control shuts off a type of card, and the casters note it called action cards, so Aqua cannot use spells unless he pays four. Aqua takes up to 37 damage and must recover at least 10 to survive his end step.

Aqua thinks hard about a Quicksilver Grail into Shangi into Enrage sequence that would take the match to game three, and pops the Bauble of Abundance to draw. He finds Hemorrhaging Rend and Relentless Outburst, but there is not enough damage. Apaul takes round seven 2-0 with the dragon.

after.summary: Apaul wins — Innervate Agility stops Aqua’s return attack

beats.text: Angelic Channeling accelerates Guo Jia’s quest counters. Stifling Trap stops Aqua’s Dungeon Guide, delaying Jin’s level three.

Seiryuu and Byakko’s Command push Aqua far above his life total. Aqua responds with Relentless Outburst and flips Quicksilver Grail into Shuang Ji of Sacrifice, but Apaul has Innervate Agility for the attack and takes game one.

after.summary: Apaul wins — Optical Control leaves Aqua searching for an answer

beats.text: Daunting Panda repeatedly attacks, and Fatestone of Heaven destroys Aqua’s Berserker’s Plate. Optical Control is initially described as naming skill; the casters later correct the call to action card.

With Jin at 37 damage, Aqua searches for a winning line. The proposed Grail–Enrage sequence is not played: he materializes the spear directly, draws through Bauble of Abundance, and concedes when the needed damage does not appear.

before.summary: Emp wins — he survives Yamikin's raccoon pressure and closes with Baleful Oblation and Manxome Armoire

beats.text: Yamikin opens with a fast ally start: Bandit, Portly Raccoons and an early Cheshire Cat. The casters say it plays like an aggressive water deck or a tamer deck and not like a CL deck, and the raccoons start pressure on Emp. Yamikin has five damage on board and a full grip.

Emp does a clean Backup Charger turn and goes to CL level two with a Turbo Charge for two extra cards. Umbra Sight and Mirage's Grave hit the board for Emp, and he puts an Advent of the Stormcaller into the omens from hand to take out the Bandit.

Yamikin passes with four cards active but cannot survive the Baleful Oblation. Manxome Armoire comes out through the materialization and the casters call the damage huge. The Death Essence Amulet, which makes the opponent discard when an ally dies, is not enough, and Emp takes game one with an amazing finish.

before.summary: Emp wins — Yamikin is one step short, and Umbra Sight pays for Weighted Accord to cast the final Oblation

beats.text: Yamikin goes first and plays a Backup Charger, which the casters call a trap. Emp finds a Resolute Stand with Rector's Tiding and adds cards to the omens from hand. He has lots of influence but no Dungeon Guide to level up faster.

Yamikin goes up to CL level one with Snow White, and the casters note he has no Freezing Hail to keep Emp's level two CL rested. He pushes in as much damage as he can, with a Power Cell and an automaton, to bring Emp down.

Emp goes to level three, and without an Umbra Sight he could not cast Baleful Oblation because of Weighted Accord, but he has one. Yamikin goes down to 19 damage counters with one card in hand, Baleful Oblation does 15 and Feu Awakening seals it. Emp wins 2-0, and the casters call Oblation the talk of the Gauntlet.

after.summary: Emp wins — Armoire sets up Baleful Oblation

Emp reaches level three with Umbra Sight. Adding Advent of the Stormcaller to his omens removes Bandit. Manxome Armoire then sets up the Baleful Oblation that wins game one.

after.summary: Emp wins — Umbra Sight opens the Oblation and Feu Awakening finish

Emp uses Umbra Sight through Waited Accord and reaches level three. After the Liminal Guide attack and Enfeebling Orb exchange, he resolves Baleful Oblation for 15 and Feu Awakening to finish. The 19 damage discussed just before this belongs to Emp’s Ciel, not Yamikin.

before.summary: Leowong wins — a triple Gleaming Cut, triple Lightweaver's Assault turn-four kill

beats.text: Bailey gets a Floral Arrangement and herb generation going and sets up Cosmic Bolts. He pitches Gentle Respite for floating memory, but Leowong has a Turbo Charge, a Creative Shock and another Angelic Channeling, and the casters say Leowong is ahead on influence.

Leowong gets Zander, Blinding Steel to level three on the stack with a Dungeon Guide banishing two, and sets up the Insignia of the Corhazi to draw extra cards. Bailey goes to Arisana level three on Dungeon Guide, a new level three the casters have not seen before.

Leowong reveals seven and holds three Lightweaver's Assaults and a Striking Illuminance with two prep counters. Triple Gleaming Cut draws four more cards, and the Striking Illuminance counts every reveal, including the reveals from the Lightweavers. The casters call it one of the highest-roll games they have ever seen: a turn-four kill, and Leowong takes game one.

after.summary: Leowong wins — Striking Illuminance and Lightweaver’s Assault finish on turn four

Leowong materializes Insignia of the Corhazi rather than the proposed Portentous Tanggu. Zander’s reveals put Bailey’s hand down and generate more cards. After a Dungeon Guide attack, Striking Illuminance with Lightweaver’s Assault supplies lethal damage.

before.summary: Dit wins by Polar Depths mill-out

beats.text: Dit opens with an early Fractal of Polar Depths and Fabled Sapphire Fatestone, milling Seaside Ringleader and Fractal of Rain on turn one. It is rare to see main-deck Fantasia removal, so the unprotected Polar Depths goes unpunished.

boeboe has a clunky opener (three Dungeon Guides and little other Wind). They play Angelic Channeling before levelling, imbue a Windmill Engineer to show a Reclaim, and bank Fatestone of Heaven cards under Channeling for later.

boeboe levels Guo Jia quickly using Dungeon Guide banishes for quest counters, flips Seiryuu first (ten counters versus Genbu's nine), and sends an Arcane Blast to their banishment off the attack. A short judge ruling checks how Angelic Channeling's top/bottom trigger resolves.
Dit plays a defensive Frostsworn Paladin game rather than going for an unsafe lethal swing, and Primordial Ritual answers the attacking Paladin in response to the dragon's attack trigger.

boeboe plays Optical Control naming action cards, so Dit's Fugue costs four more. Auspicious Manifestation banishes Seiryuu so it returns awake at end of turn and can taunt. The line buys time but cannot beat the mill-out plan.

Dit plays three Fractal of Polar Depths in a row, stacking them to mill boeboe's library (target self, self, then opponent). boeboe concedes. Naming Fantasia instead of action cards would have been the only way to catch it.

before.summary: boeboe wins with a sideboarded lock and Arcane Blast

beats.text: boeboe opens with an imbued Benediction Angel and Dream Fairies. The fairies stop Dit from playing Bullfrog or Frostsworn Paladin for most of the game.
Nullifying Lantern hits the board. All cards in graveyards become no element, so Dit's Polar Depths mill and Deluge turn off. Dit holds Unbroken Mustang to remove it.
Dit plays both Unbroken Mustangs. boeboe answers with Stifling Trap, so the Lantern survives. Dit has no Primordial Ritual to sacrifice the Mustang and fizzle the trap.

boeboe adds Censer of Restful Peace and then Purifying Thurible. Dit's Fracturize answers the Sensor but not the Lantern, because of layering. boeboe keeps Aella, Zephyr's Hand ready to save the Lantern, and holds Psychopomp's Gale.
Dit stays alive with Song of Frost, Enfeebling Orb, Spalling Cleanse and Beastbond Boots, flips Genbu, and tries to dodge the dragon. The round timer runs low as boeboe stays patient.

Dit negates the first dragon attack trigger with Song of Frost. boeboe uses Byakko's Command to wake the dragon so it attacks again, and then fires the stored Arcane Blast for 11 damage that Dit cannot stop.

before.summary: Dit wins — game loss to boeboe for an illegal deck

beats.text: With about three minutes left, both players agree to try game three. In the rush, boeboe shuffles the generated Arcane Blast into their deck. They call the judge themselves, but the judges rule an illegal deck and give a game loss. Dit wins the match 2-1.

after.summary: Dit wins by Polar Depths mill-out

beats.text: Dit opens Fractal of Polar Depths, then levels into Guo Jia and Fabled Sapphire Fatestone. Seaside Ringleader is lost to the level-up banish; the early mills hit Fractal of Rain for Dit and Windmill Engineer for boeboe.

boeboe has a clunky opener (three Dungeon Guides and little other Wind). They play Angelic Channeling before levelling, imbue a Windmill Engineer to show a Reclaim, and bank Fatestone of Heaven cards under Channeling for later.

boeboe levels Guo Jia quickly using Dungeon Guide banishes for quest counters, flips Seiryuu first (ten counters versus Genbu's nine), and sends an Arcane Blast to their banishment off the attack. A short judge ruling checks how Angelic Channeling's top/bottom trigger resolves.

Dit develops Frostsworn Paladins and holds defensive interaction. When Seiryuu attacks a Paladin, Dit sacrifices that defending Paladin to Primordial Ritual. The dragon's on-attack trigger still resolves.

boeboe plays Optical Control naming action cards, so Dit's Fugue costs four more. Auspicious Manifestation banishes Seiryuu so it returns awake at end of turn and can taunt. The line buys time but cannot beat the mill-out plan.

Dit presents a third Fractal of Polar Depths, and boeboe concedes to the mill-out line. The casters explain a self, self, opponent sequence and discuss naming Fantasia with Optical Control as an alternative.

after.summary: boeboe wins with a sideboarded lock and Arcane Blast

beats.text: boeboe opens with an imbued Benediction Angel and Dream Fairies. The fairies stop Dit from playing Bullfrog or Frostsworn Paladin for most of the game.
Nullifying Lantern hits the board. All cards in graveyards become no element, so Dit's Polar Depths mill and Deluge turn off. Dit holds Unbroken Mustang to remove it.
Dit draws a second Unbroken Mustang but puts one into memory to play the other. Stifling Trap stops that Mustang’s trigger, leaving Nullifying Lantern intact; Dit has no Primordial Ritual response.

Boeboe adds Censer of Restful Peace, which Dit removes with Fracturize, then uses Purifying Thurible. The second Mustang is delayed; Dit later uses Enfeebling Orb before committing it. Boeboe retains Psychopomp's Gale as graveyard interaction and develops Aella, Zephyr's Hand, repeatedly suppressing Forest Cake for cards.
Dit stays alive with Song of Frost, Enfeebling Orb, Spalling Cleanse and Beastbond Boots, flips Genbu, and tries to dodge the dragon. The round timer runs low as boeboe stays patient.

Dit negates the first dragon attack trigger with Song of Frost. boeboe uses Byakko's Command to wake the dragon so it attacks again, and then fires the stored Arcane Blast for 11 damage that Dit cannot stop.

after.summary: Dit wins — game loss to boeboe for an illegal deck

beats.text: As the players prepare game three near the end of the round, boeboe accidentally shuffles a generated Arcane Blast into the deck and immediately calls a judge. The casters report a game loss for presenting an illegal deck, giving Dit the match 2-1.

before.text: boeboe sideboards in Nullifying Lantern (turns every graveyard card to no element, so Fractal of Polar Depths mills nothing and Deluge goes offline), Psychopomp's Gale (banishes the whole graveyard) and extra Dream Fairies. The casters also expect fast-speed Fantasia removal to stay out because Dit played an unprotected Polar Depths.
The casters predict Dit brings in the third Unbroken Mustang, Song of Frost and the last Engulf, to answer the Lantern and the dragon combo. These are caster predictions, not a confirmed list.

after.text: The casters recommend Nullifying Lantern, Psychopomp's Gale and Dream Fairy for boeboe. They also consider Expel the Departed because Dit exposed Polar Depths before gaining its class bonus. Lantern is shown and Gale is identified in hand in game two; exact swap counts are unconfirmed.

before.summary: TlsoVotl wins on card advantage and a clutch Fiery Interference

beats.text: TlsoVotl wins the roll and opens with Four of Spades. Suited cards replace themselves via Cardistry, so TlsoVotl keeps eight or more cards in influence and rebuilds the board quickly after Aqua's sweeps.

Aqua levels to Arisanna 2 and sets up the Polaris plan. Herbs sacrificed by pairs draw cards and add counters to Polaris. Calming Breeze (negates up to three damage) holds off early attacks, and Polaris and Meteor Strike clear the ally board twice.
TlsoVotl lands Six of Hearts and Arthur, Young Heir for a big swing that puts Aqua's spirit low. Aqua answers with Cosmic Bolt on Arthur and Three Visits to heal.
TlsoVotl holds Fiery Interference. In response to Aqua's Serene Spirit heal, it prevents the recovery and the final attacks go through. Aqua cannot stabilize before level three.

before.summary: Aqua wins with defensive cards and Cosmic Bolts

beats.text: Aqua starts with two Calming Breezes, two Gentle Beseeches and Gentle Respite. TlsoVotl's hand has few cheap allies and uses Backup Charger to fix it.

TlsoVotl commits Three of Hearts, Rouge and Eight of Hearts (sacrificing allies to reduce its cost). Aqua sweeps with Polaris and then Meteor Strike (via Cosmic Astroscope and Star Calling), and holds Safeguard Amulet.
Imperial Countermeasure and the Astra Sight glimpse keep Aqua alive. Two Cosmic Bolts take TlsoVotl's spirit down and Aqua closes out the game.

before.summary: TlsoVotl wins in overtime with Verita and Arthur

beats.text: TlsoVotl goes first and opens Four of Hearts into Arthur, Young Heir on turn two. Aqua has no Arisanna on turn one, so Polaris is two turns away.

Aqua uses Angelic Channeling to put Meteor Strike on top. After a Dungeon Guide level up, Aqua wipes the board with Meteor Strike via Cosmic Astroscope, and Polaris with Calming Breeze and Stifling Gyre blunt the follow-up.

TlsoVotl rebuilds with Verita (free by banishing suited allies from the graveyard) and The Duchess. Aqua stays alive with two Imperial Countermeasures but is down to 20 life, and the match enters overtime.

TlsoVotl sequences Arthur's swing first, then attacks with Verita and the others. Aqua has only a Cosmic Bolt to answer the board and is one glimpse short of stabilizing. TlsoVotl takes the match 2-1.

before.summary: Tress wins — survives Noel’s final attack to complete the mill-out

beats.text: Both players start the long Jin mirror with Spirit of Serene Water. Noel uses Gentle Respite and Back-up Charger well and uses Dungeon Guide to hit Jin level three first.
Noel plays Regal Inquisition to strip Tress's hand, leaving only Angel cards. Tress answers with Angelic Channeling, Fractal of Waves and Quicksilver Grail to rebuild.
Seething Intercession finds Return to the Archive, then Enrage, Engulf and a Regal. Banished cards cannot be discarded by a Regal, so these three hits give Tress a protected advantage.
Tress sets up Shade-Mist Priestess (recover one on every damage) and keeps a Regal in banishment. With four Regals, Tress changes the plan to a mill-out, and Noel has no anti-mill tech.
Noel transforms Huaji into Huaji of Abyssal Fall and adds Sunce for big unpreventable-damage attacks. Relentless Outburst deals the damage, but Shademist Priestess recovers the triggers.
Noel has already drawn out of cards. Noel goes all in at the end, but Tress shows a heal and Mend Flesh and survives.

before.summary: Noel wins — Tress runs out of healing, tying the match 1–1

beats.text: Both players play more carefully: Noel holds Backup Charger for a level up, and Tress plays Topsy Decree to deny Noel's float. The two sides trade Angelic Channeling and Fractal Fracturize tricks to set up top-of-deck cards.
Tress uses Dynastic Whirlpool to mill the cards Noel put on top with Channeling: three Regals and two Engulfs go to the graveyard. This removes Noel's protection and the main way to mill Tress.

Noel switches to a damage plan. Shuangji, Berserker Plate, Fracturize and an Enrage push huge swings, and Tress answers with Crimson Rupture on the Shuangji plus Pearled Prayer, Regenerate and Serene Spirit.
Tress digs for a heal using Tome of Abyssal Heaven but cannot find a second one. Noel wins game two with damage, tying the match 1–1 as time expires. The casters praise Noel for playing to outs.

before.summary: Caban wins — influence denial and a Burst Asunder that Superior cannot stop

beats.text: Caban plays a Fractals list that mostly runs Fractal of Intrusion, Acquiescing Rejection and four Topsy Decrees, so Superior's float and memory are banished each turn. The goal is to keep Superior's influence too low to flip Genbu.

Superior starts with imbued Fractal of Rain, then Safeguard Amulet, Tidestone Bovine and Fractal of Polar Depths. But the mills are poor and the key Polar Depths and Stratagem cards fall into the graveyard.

Caban Fracturizes cards to add fractals, uses Refracting Missile to pull out Safeguard Amulet, and negates every important play with Glimmering Refusal and Acquiescing Rejection. Superior's Diamond Ribbon gives influence but cannot get a play through.
With six or more fractals, Burst Asunder deals 14 or more. Superior responds with Cerulean Decree, but Caban pays and Burst Asunder resolves for lethal.

before.summary: Superior wins — Caban's Burst Asunder is Engulfed and Superior steals the race

beats.text: Superior plays Fractal of Polar Depths on turn one, unprotected, and Expel the Departed from the side to stop Caban's Zhang Jiao turn. Caban's Sapphire Fatestone mill and Return to the Archive give Caban a good start.
Caban tries an imbued Topsy Decree on Superior's Frostsworn Paladin trigger, but Superior has an imbued Cerulean Decree and a Title Lock. Superior comes out ahead with a 3/4 Paladin.
Superior double-activates Fugue to threaten lethal, but Caban holds two Glimmering Refusals. Superior then rebuilds influence with Seaside Ringleader and Diamond Ribbon and levels Guo Jia.
Caban has Burst Asunder and six fractals (14 damage) but no third Glimmering Refusal, so Superior uses Engulf on the Burst. Caban tests the waters and learns he is out of refusals.

Superior keeps the board with Shademist Priestess and Frostsworn Paladin. A fast Refracting Missile for eight damage nearly wins for Caban, but Superior activates Genbu to survive and wins the game on Fast Cure.

before.summary: Draw — time expires

beats.text: With only nine minutes left, both players have to race. Superior's Shademist Priestess recovers damage, and Caban Fracturizes the Safeguard Amulet and builds fractals.

Caban builds a lethal line in the last turns (Refracting Missile, Glimmering Refusal, extra fractals). Superior holds Engulf and Cerulean Decree. Caban plays two extra fractals to beat an Engulf plus recovery, but Superior has Engulf and Cerulean Decree instead. The game ends in a draw.

ChemCollapse waits a turn before flipping the dragon, and uses Aella to suppress his own Bullfrog target. Regal Inquisition makes mDuo13 show a hand with two Song of Frost. ChemCollapse discards both, mDuo13 draws two and misses the third, and Seiryuu's Command for lethal resolves.

before.summary: ChemCollapse wins — Sasha shuts off the graveyard and Uther removes Genbu

beats.text: mDuo13 starts with Tidestone Bovines and Fractal of Rain, and gets Genbu to 9 quest counters. Purifying Thurible banishes his float and ChemCollapse's Tariff Ring shuts down the Fugue plan, which is one card short anyway.
ChemCollapse follows with Censer of Restful Peace, then Uther, Illustrious King, which deletes mDuo13's Fabled Sapphire Fatestone (Guo Jia is only level one). Uther kills the Bovine in combat.
ChemCollapse fosters Sasha, Purifying Acolyte, so no graveyard exists for the rest of the game. Smoke Bombs and Aella protect Sasha and Uther, and mDuo13 concedes.

after.summary: ChemCollapse wins — Regal Inquisition clears Song of Frost, then Seiryuu's Command

ChemCollapse delays transforming Seiryuu and uses Aella to target mDuo13’s Bullfrog; mDuo13 responds with Primordial Ritual. Later, Regal Inquisition discards both Songs of Frost from mDuo13’s hand. The replacement draws find neither another Song nor an answer to Seiryuu’s Command, which wins the game.

ChemCollapse plays Censer of Restful Peace, then Uther, Illustrious King banishes Genbu while mDuo13’s Guo Jia is still level one. Uther later intercepts Tidestone Bovine and defeats it in retaliation.

ChemCollapse develops Sasha, Purifying Acolyte and Smoke Bombs. Sasha fosters, banishing the graveyards and preventing cards from entering them while its effect remains active. Aella adds another protective option, and mDuo13 concedes.

before.text: ChemCollapse has a large anti-Genbu side: Tricastles of Lucenia, two Sasha, Purifying Acolyte (banishes every graveyard when it fosters), Scatter Essence, Noble Dissolution, Blanch, Topsy Decree, Tempestuous Seraphim and Sunblessed Gazelle. The casters argue for nearly all of them, and Sasha and Tariff Ring are seen in game 2.
mDuo13 looks at Regal Inquisition, a fourth Song of Frost and Submerged Fatestone (a Genbu mirror card, not relevant here). Tariff Ring is seen in play.

after.text: The casters consider nearly ChemCollapse’s entire anti-Genbu sideboard, including Tricastles of Lucenia, Sasha, Scatter Essence, Noble Dissolution, Blanche, Topsy Decree, Tempestuous Seraphim and Sunblessed Gazelle. Sasha is confirmed in game two; the complete boarding package is not shown.

The casters consider Regal Inquisition, a fourth Song of Frost and Terraforming for mDuo13. They describe Submerged Fatestone as a mirror option. Terraforming is later revealed beneath Quicksilver Grail; Safeguard Amulet also remains available.

before.summary: Fallinbuu14 wins — Krustallan Archer and Ranger Strides for 12 through the Serene Spirit

beats.text: Fallinbuu14 has no distant enabler in the opener and plays Aetheric Calibration, Inert Sword and Cheshire Cat (a 3/3 with stealth and spell shroud) instead. Yadon uses Incapacitate on Reposition and Planted Explosive on the Cat.

Yadon opens with Angelic Channeling to protect Luxem Sight, Uncover the Plot and Lightweaver's Assault, levels Zander twice with Dungeon Guide, and stabilizes with Blinding Steel reveals and Tariff Ring.

Fallinbuu14 plays two Frostsworn Paladins, Quickstep Treads and Weaving Manastream. Yadon's Frostbind-able Planted Explosive are answered by a Frostbind. A final Incapacitate stops one distant enabler but Krustallan Archer plus Ranger Strides and a Cheshire Cat swing for 12 through the Serene Spirit.

before.summary: Yadon wins — double Lightweaver's Assault for lethal

beats.text: Fallinbuu14 finds only distant enablers and no Aether Charge, so the damage stays low. Yadon holds Topsy Decree, imbued, to strip the graveyard and levels to Zander level three with zero damage counters.

Yadon reveals Lightweaver's Assault, Sadi, Gleaming Cut and Luxem Sight through Blinding Steel and Corhazi Insignia, and uses Palvor Sword on Fallinbuu14's graveyard and Planted Explosive for Frostsworn Paladin. Fallinbuu14's Fracturize of the Insignia and Flash Grenade only delay.

Yadon reveals two Lightweaver's Assaults. Even through Flash Grenade (prevent three), each hits for four. With Exploit Vulnerability and the second Assault, the game ends. The Incapacitate held back covers the last reposition.

before.summary: Yadon wins — a final Lightweaver's Assault, with Fallinbuu14 two damage short

beats.text: Fallinbuu14 misses with Aetheric Calibration again and has Frostbind and two Backsteps instead of charges. Yadon removes Frostsworn Paladin and Cheshire Cat with Planted Explosive and a main-phase Topsy Decree.

Yadon uses Angelic Channeling again (Luxem Sight, Gleaming Cut, Excalibur) and takes Zander level three, though he forgets Lost Providence. Fallinbuu14 pushes 11 damage with Take Aim, Ranger Strides and a 12-card glimpse. Yadon's Chalice of Blood, Serene Spirit and Tariff Ring survive.

Fallinbuu14 gets within three, then two, damage of lethal on consecutive turns. Yadon uses Exploit Vulnerability and Mercenary's Blade on the Paladin, and finishes with Sadi and Lightweaver's Assault revealing seven cards.

before.summary: Zetdivx wins — Diana pressure races Stevo before Jin level three

beats.text: Zetdivx opens with Backstep to become distant, gets Aquamirage Whisper on level up, and uses Refreshing Charge and Aetheric Calibration to glimpse. Stevo, on Fortuitous Water, has a full hand of Regal Inquisition, Frostbind and Fracturize but starts slowly.
Frostsworn Paladin and Krustallan Archer add damage each turn, and Stevo does not get to level three. Stevo's Jin is at 20 total life and cannot heal out of Zetdivx's damage.
Zetdivx closes out game one with a final Archer attack, while Stevo has no interaction left. The casters note that 14 damage was lethal on that turn.

before.summary: Zetdivx wins again — a two-turn kill before Stevo can reach level three

beats.text: Stevo starts with Gentle Respite and holds Dungeon Guide, Regal Inquisition and Dynastic Whirlpool. Spirit of Fortuitous Water gives him a slower spirit than serene water, and he plans to Fracturize Zetdivx's board.
Zetdivx plays Inert Sword, Cheshire Cat, Reposition and Quickstep Treads on turn two. Tactical Retreat saves the Cat and ends Stevo's one big attack, while Fracturize hits the Treads.

Stevo is on 21 life with a Serene Spirit heal but never gets to use his lineage release at the right time. Zetdivx swings for three, then lethal, and Jin dies at 24 total life. Zetdivx secures a Gauntlet invite and moves to the semifinals.

after.summary: Zetdivx wins — Diana pressure races Stevo before Jin level three

after.summary: Zetdivx wins — floating-memory denial stalls Jin, then Tactical Retreat stops the heal

beats.text: Stevo switches to Spirit of Serene Water and opens Gentle Respite. Enchanted Fete heals and draws into memory before Jin reaches level two. Stevo then uses Fracturize on Quickstep Treads, but its on-enter draw still resolves.

Zetdivx uses Aetheric Reforging to banish the Fracturize floating memory Stevo needs for the next level. With a hand full of Exia cards, Stevo has to materialize Backup Charger instead. Krustallan Archer and Frostsworn Paladin keep attacking.

After Inert Sword and Reposition, Zetdivx answers the Serene Water heal during combat with Tactical Retreat, ending that combat before the heal resolves. Diana and Cheshire Cat then finish Jin at level two. Zetdivx advances to the semifinals and secures a Worlds invitation.

before.text: Zetdivx considers Song of Frost, Annihilation and Crimson Rupture-style cards but sees little that clearly needs to come in. The casters say that Zetdivx wants damage and allies, not more draw.

after.text: The casters recommend Spirit of Serene Water, Song of Frost and defensive Exia cards for stevo7653. Serene Water is confirmed in game two.
The casters find few clear sideboard changes for Zetdivx and favor maintaining the ally pressure. Additional Aetheric Reforging is discussed, but no swap count is confirmed.

before.summary: ChemCollapse wins — Tricastles of Lucenia locks Razorgale, then Seiryuu's Command

beats.text: ChemCollapse uses Beseech the Winds to reach Guo Jia level one on turn one and builds quest counters with Scout the Land and Tangu. Jett responds with Fluffy Shopkeep, Backup Charger, and Windmill Engineer's Reclaim and trades.

After Dungeon Guide takes Guo Jia to level three, ChemCollapse plays Tricastles of Lucenia, preventing non-advanced element card activations. Once per turn, any player may banish a norm or advanced element card from hand to make Tricastles lose all abilities until end of turn.

ChemCollapse follows with Uther (removing a Razorgale), Aella and a Royal Oathguard. Jett plays three Dream Fairies, a Zephyr and Purifying Thurible but drops below six cards, which turns off Ensnaring Fumes. Aella suppresses Jett's Essence Crucible.
ChemCollapse flips Seiryuu, plays Seiryuu's Command (triple on-enter) to generate an Arcane Blast and empower it by eight. The Blast costs nothing and finishes Jett.

before.summary: Jett wins — Aesan Protector chip damage, then Zephyr and Veiling Breeze on the last Razorgale trigger

beats.text: Jett brings in Turbo Charge, plays Windmill Engineer and Aesan Protector early, and wants a board that can kill Tricastles of Lucenia in two turns. Fairy Whispers finds Razorgale Calling.

ChemCollapse levels with Beseech and Dungeon Guide and draws with Incandescent Reliquary, but a Tricastle banished by Throne-keeper mill and a Purifying Thurible deny him the lock. ChemCollapse plays Regal Inquisition on Jett, discarding Ensnaring Fumes, but Jett draws another copy. The replacement keeps Seiryuu locked down.

Jett plays two Razorgales and Essence Crucible with Distilled Water potions. Imperial Countermeasure absorbs the first trigger. Jett Zephyrs his own Aesan Protector and then uses Veiling Breeze as the final Razorgale trigger for lethal. The Aesan Protector is the MVP of the game.

before.summary: Zetdivx wins — a patient build-up, then a 19-damage one-shot

beats.text: Zetdivx goes first as the top seed and plays Censer of Restful Peace, which Jett's Fracturize removes. Zetdivx levels Diana, plays Aetheric Calibration to find Aetheric Reforging, and loads the Aquamirage Whisper.

Jett uses Protector Raccoon, Purifying Thurible and Veiling Breeze to blank the Whisper's first hit trigger. Jett has zero damage taken for much of the game and builds a hand of eight cards, while Zetdivx gets no float value.

Jett lands two Razorgales and Essence Crucible, but Zetdivx's Fracturize removes the Crucible (Jett has no Obscured Offering). Jett's hand has clunky norm cards, and Cyclical Breeze to get Veiling Breeze back is answered by Aetheric Reforging.

Zetdivx tests a Flash Grenade, gets no response, and then plays Krustallan Archer with Ranger Strides, two Take Aims and five Aether Charges in the Whisper. Quickstep Treads makes Jett's responses cost two more. That is a 19-damage swing and the attack finishes Jett.

before.summary: Jett wins — board control with raccoons and Aesan Protector

beats.text: Zetdivx starts with a Krustallan Archer to bait Veiling Breeze and holds Expel the Departed, Fracturize and the second Reforging. But Jett's Aesan Protector, Bandit and Protector Raccoon block float, and Dream Fairy locks Cheshire Cat.

Jett uses Aesan Protector to reclaim his raccoons and Windmill Engineer. Zetdivx plays a Seeker's Aetherwing to remove the Dream Fairy, but Skirting Step prevents the damage, and Zetdivx never gets a glimpse.
Jett gets Razorgale Calling off Fairy Whispers. Zetdivx has 14 damage and Jett holds 12 cards. Tariff Ring taxes attacks, and Zetdivx concedes.

before.summary: Jett wins — Essence Crucible with three counters and double Razorgale

beats.text: Bandit finds Bandit with a one-in-six scavenge. Jett denies Zetdivx's float again and strips Backup Charger lines. Shademist Priestess stops Razorgale pings for a while, and Jett needs Dream Fairy to remove it.

Zetdivx trades Weaving Manastream and Krustallan Archer for Aesan Protector, builds Ranger Strides, Inert Sword and Quickstep Treads, and plays Nullifying Mirror to turn off Veiling Breeze. Jett's Fluffy Shopkeep keeps Zetdivx's Cheshire Cat from connecting. Zetdivx uses Drown in Aether on a rested Bandit.

Jett plays Essence Crucible, brews Distilled Water potions through Ingredient Pouch for three counters and a second Razorgale from Fairy Whispers. Each wind card now deals eight damage. Zetdivx's two Shademist Priestesses recover, but Jett responds to each trigger and a Fairy Whispers finishes the game.

Jett repeatedly returns allies with Aesan Protector and Reclaim. Zetdivx uses Seeker’s Aetherwing to attack the Dream Fairy holding Cheshire Cat, but Jett’s Skirting Step prevents the damage. Charge the Soul had gone to Jett’s champion, leaving Fairy healthy enough to survive that line.

Jett builds a large hand and an attacking board, then develops Tariff Ring and Razorgale Calling. Zetdivx Expels the first Calling; Jett finds another with Scout the Land. With Tariff Ring taxing attacks and Jett still controlling the graveyard, Zetdivx concedes.

after.summary: Jett wins — Essence Crucible with three counters and double Razorgale

beats.text: Jett’s opening Bandit finds another Bandit on the sixth scavenge card and repeatedly removes Zetdivx’s floating memory. Zetdivx builds influence with Backup Charger and plays Shademist Priestess, forcing Jett to find an answer before Razorgale damage can accumulate efficiently.

Zetdivx uses Drown in Aether on a rested Bandit, later Frostbinds Reclaim to secure an attack, and trades Weaving Manastream plus Krustallan Archer for Aesan Protector. Ranger Strides, Inert Sword, Quickstep Treads and Nullifying Mirror build a threatening board. A later Drown in Aether removes the attacking Dream Fairy and frees Priestess; Jett’s Viridian Protective Trinket makes it cost four.

Jett brews a speed potion and two Distilled Waters, bringing Essence Crucible to three counters. Fairy Whispers finds a second Razorgale, so each wind activation threatens eight damage. The casters discuss responding above the Priestesses’ recovery triggers, but correct their lethal calculation when recovery resolves during Scout the Land. A following Fairy Whispers supplies the finishing triggers.

before.text: Jett brings in Obscured Offering (to protect Essence Crucible from a Fracturize), Topsy Decree, Turbo Charge, Blessed Clergy and Fluffy Shopkeep.
Zetdivx brings in a second Aetheric Reforging, Nullifying Mirror (to turn off Veiling Breeze), Expel the Departed, Nullifying Lantern as an option, Shademist Priestess.

after.text: The casters recommend Obscured Offering and discuss Topsy Decree, Blessed Clergy, Fluffy Shopkeep and Stifling Gyre for Jett. Turbo Charge and Fluffy Shopkeep are confirmed in game two; the complete boarding package is not shown.

The casters discuss another Aetheric Reforging, Nullifying Mirror, Nullifying Lantern and Shademist Priestess. Expel the Departed, two Reforgings and a nullifying regalia are identified in game two; Mirror and Priestess are confirmed in game three.

before.summary: Jett wins — Purifying Thurible and Protector Raccoon deny the float, then two Razorgales

beats.text: Jett opens with Purifying Thurible (not Censer of Restful Peace) and holds Protector Raccoon. Quarax's Krustallan Archer attack is answered by Protector Raccoon banishing the Charge the Soul float, so no card is drawn. Jett waits for the last moment to respond.

Bandit scavenges into a third raccoon. Fluffy Shopkeep, an animal, is protected by Protector Raccoon, and Viridian Protective Trinket makes Quarax's water cards cost two more. Quarax's Cheshire Cat kills the Fluffy Shopkeep and the Raccoon.

Jett plays two Razorgales and brews a Speed Potion in Essence Crucible. Quarax's Fracturize removes the Crucible (Jett has no Obscured Offering). Dream Fairy kills the Cheshire Cat, and Aesan Protector returns it to hand. Razorgale pings, Cyclical Breeze and Tariff Ring leave Quarax with one damage from death.
Calming Breeze prevents the final Razorgale trigger damage. Quarax has no way to deal the last damage to Jett or stop the board, and scoops. Jett leads 1-0.

before.summary: Quarax wins — Krustallan Archer with a float and Jett cannot imbue Skirting Step

beats.text: Quarax goes first and passes. He levels Diana on turn two with Backstep and Aquamirage Whisper, then hits with Nullifying Mirror in play, so Veiling Breeze is unavailable to Jett.

Jett plays Purifying Thurible and a Protector Raccoon, but Quarax Fracturizes the Thurible to force the response. Bandit scavenges six cards and puts two Razorgales and a Dream Fairy at the bottom, which hurts Jett's win conditions.

Quarax finally keeps a float and attacks with Krustallan Archer for four. Jett plays Skirting Step but cannot imbue it, so it prevents nothing, and Jett drops to one life. Jett is forced to level up and Quarax finishes the game.

Jett levels to Arisanna with Reclaim and Windmill Engineer, imbues Skirting Step, and plays Razorgale Calling and Dream Fairy on the Cheshire Cat. Quarax finds Seeker's Aetherwing and Prudent Nock, but cannot get damage through the reclaimed Windmill Engineers and Dream Fairy.

Jett plays Essence Crucible. Quarax's Expel the Departed removes the first Razorgale, but Jett brews, Cyclical Breeze brings it back and Quarax has no Reforging. Quarax tries Reposition to become distant, and Jett answers with Veiling Breeze. Quarax is 2 damage short and Jett wins the title.

after.summary: Jett wins — Purifying Thurible and Protector Raccoon deny the float, then two Razorgales

beats.text: Jett opens with Purifying Thurible (not Censer of Restful Peace) and holds Protector Raccoon. Quarax's Krustallan Archer attack is answered by Protector Raccoon banishing the Charge the Soul float, so no card is drawn. Jett waits for the last moment to respond.

Bandit scavenges into a third raccoon. Fluffy Shopkeep, an animal, is protected by Protector Raccoon, and Viridian Protective Trinket makes Quarax's water cards cost two more. Quarax's Cheshire Cat kills the Fluffy Shopkeep and the Raccoon.

Jett plays two Razorgales and brews a Speed Potion in Essence Crucible. Quarax's Fracturize removes the Crucible (Jett has no Obscured Offering). Dream Fairy kills the Cheshire Cat, and Aesan Protector returns it to hand. Razorgale pings, Cyclical Breeze and Tariff Ring leave Quarax with one damage from death.

Quarax develops Flash Grenade but must first become distant to use it. Jett activates Tariff Ring and answers Diana’s attack with Calming Breeze, preventing the attack damage while adding Razorgale triggers. Quarax is left one damage from defeat and concedes.

after.summary: Quarax wins — Krustallan Archer with a float and Jett cannot imbue Skirting Step

beats.text: Quarax goes first, then uses Backstep to set up Diana and Aquamirage Whisper. Jett’s Calming Breeze stops the opening shot. Nullifying Mirror later removes Veiling Breeze as a useful defensive option while Quarax builds pressure.

Jett plays Purifying Thurible and a Protector Raccoon, but Quarax Fracturizes the Thurible to force the response. Bandit scavenges six cards and puts two Razorgales and a Dream Fairy at the bottom, which hurts Jett's win conditions.

Quarax attacks with Diana, finds floating memory and follows with Krustallan Archer. Jett plays Skirting Step without imbuing it. The casters initially calculate that it saves him at one life and discuss leveling, then correct themselves: the damage prevention also requires imbue. With Topsy Decree among Jett’s cards preventing that imbue, the Archer attack ends game two.

after.summary: Jett wins — Bandit, Protector Raccoon and Razorgale's pings close out the title

beats.text: Jett opens with Windmill Engineer and then Censer of Restful Peace, holding Bandits while Quarax builds influence. When Bandit is finally activated, Quarax plays Frozen Dismissal; Jett pays four and finds Protector Raccoon on the fifth scavenge card. Quarax loses Tactical Retreat on leveling and has no distant enabler available for Diana’s on-enter, leaving her without an Aetherwing.

Jett levels to Arisanna with Reclaim and Windmill Engineer, imbues Skirting Step, and plays Razorgale Calling and Dream Fairy on the Cheshire Cat. Quarax finds Seeker's Aetherwing and Prudent Nock, but cannot get damage through the reclaimed Windmill Engineers and Dream Fairy.

Jett develops Essence Crucible and brews a potion. Quarax’s Expel the Departed removes Razorgale Calling, but Cyclical Breeze retrieves it without a Reforging response. The replayed Calling and Aesan Protector bring Quarax within two damage of defeat. Jett waits until Quarax attempts Reposition, then plays Veiling Breeze; the Razorgale trigger deals lethal damage and wins the title.
